   "claude",
   "Explore",
   "general-purpose",
   "Plan",
   "statusline-setup"
  ],
  "addedLines": [
   "- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)",
   "- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: \"medium\" for moderate exploration, \"very thorough\" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)",
   "- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)",
   "- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)",
   "- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)"
  ],
  "removedTypes": [],
  "isInitial": true,
  "showConcurrencyNote": true
 }
}

{
 "attachment": {
  "type": "skill_listing",
  "content": "- a11y-debugging: Uses Chrome DevTools MCP for accessibility (a11y) debugging and auditing based on web.dev guidelines. Use when testing semantic HTML, ARIA labels, focus states, keyboard navigation, tap targets, and color contrast.\n- aitool-continue: Continuous self-learning initialization — loads operational learning, commander profile, delegation principles, rewind context, project state, and recent session history so every session starts smarter than the last. NOT /resume (restoring a prior session). This is the self-learning thread.\n- aitool-eval: Read-only reference card for tool evaluation methodology — hard blocks, yellow flags, health flags, discovery playbook, Homebrew verification, sandbox walkthrough. Available in ANY repo. Use before installing or recommending any tool.\n- aitool-ops: Read-only reference card for tool-ops operational knowledge — deny rules, hooks, CC version dependencies, doc access methods, governance modes. Available in ANY repo. Use when checking tool behavior, deny rules, hook behavior, CC version deps, or doc access methods.\n- chrome-devtools: Uses Chrome DevTools via MCP for efficient debugging, troubleshooting and browser automation. Use when debugging web pages, automating browser interactions, analyzing performance, or inspecting network requests.\n- handoff: End a session by producing a verified handoff prompt for the the accepting session. Use when ending a session, context is getting large, switching machines, or significant work products need to carry forward. Orchestrates audit, assessment, writing, and verification via subagents.\n- intent-audit: Audit a file against its intent statement. Use when checking if a file's content matches its stated purpose, or when content may have drifted beyond scope.\n- intent-writing: Writing intent statements for markdown files, code files, and sections. Use when creating or modifying intent statements in any file.\n- investigate: Investigate when something went wrong. Use when a rule was violated, a deployment failed, a bug recurred, or a process broke down. Covers the full lifecycle: triage, RCA (5 Whys, Swiss cheese model), remediation, corrective actions, barrier analysis, and verification.\n- mission-control: Monitor running missions -- process health, activity, work products, deliverable validation. Use when launching competing missions, checking mission progress, assessing mission health, or deciding whether to FRAGORD a mission. Codifies the 7 ad-hoc monitoring patterns that worked in multi-mission operations.\n- optimize-plan: Review and improve an existing plan file. Use when a plan needs re-evaluation after new discoveries, scope changes, or multiple implementation sessions. Detects stale sections, dependency issues, leverage opportunities, and scope drift.\n- planning: Session and plan strategy for Claude Code sessions. Use when starting a planning session, deciding session scope, coordinating subagents, or managing context budgets. Covers batch sizing, session flow, subagent parallelization, and user collaboration patterns.\n- scratch: Ephemeral session scratch files — session directories, naming conventions, commit message pattern. Use when writing temp files, staging commit messages, or running complex scripts that should not be inlined.\n- frameworks: Read, update, and add frameworks in the registry. Use when checking if a framework exists, looking up a framework's artifacts, updating a stale entry, adding a new adopted framework, or discussing which discipline governs a decision point.\n- glossary: Read governed vocabulary definitions and add new terms. Use when checking a term's meaning, adding a new governed term, or resolving a terminology ambiguity.\n- governed-data: Manage governed data access — add new governed registries, audit compliance, verify three-layer enforcement. Use when creating a new JSON registry, checking if a file should be governed, or auditing governed data access patterns.\n- harvest: Manage the artifact harvesting lifecycle — harvest session artifacts, evaluate for promotion, review for generalization, prune stale items. Use when harvesting code from .scratch/, reviewing harvesting/ contents, promoting artifacts, or running generalization analysis.\n- incident: File an incident in incidents.json. Use when a spec deviation, broken cross-reference, ambiguity, or operational failure is found that should be tracked. Also use when the user says /incident or asks to file an incident.\n- tool-eval: Evaluate install methods for managed tools. Use when adding a new tool, re-evaluating an existing tool's install method, verifying provenance, comparing delivery options, or updating health flags.\n- tool-ops: Read and write per-tool operational metadata — governance modes, deny rules, hooks, context injection, KPIs, and verification specs\n- tool-registry: Read and update managed tool entries in the registry. Use when checking a tool's install method, verifying versions, adding a new tool entry, or updating an existing entry.\n- pre-update: Prepare for aitools update -- capture state, clear logs, load failure remediation context\n- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., \"what car to buy\" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.\n- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.\n- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.\n- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.\nTRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it \"looks like a one-liner\" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).\nSKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).\n- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).\n- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation\n- review: Review a pull request\n- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch",

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# aitools -- pull latest aitools scaffolding and manage dev tools
3	# Installed to ~/.local/bin/ by scripts/aitools-install.{sh,ps1}
4	#
5	# The entire script is wrapped in main() so bash reads it fully into memory
6	# before executing. This prevents corruption when the installer overwrites
7	# this file on disk during Step 6.
8	
9	AITOOLS_INSTALLED_VERSION="dev"
10	
11	main() {
12	
13	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
14	# Ensure Homebrew tools (node, etc.) are on PATH
15	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
16	# Interactive shells get this from ~/.zprofile, but non-interactive invocations
17	# (Claude Code hooks, MDM, `!` shells, scripts) do NOT source profile files. The
18	# config/JSON setup scripts shell out to `node`, so without this they fail with
19	# "node required for JSON manipulation". Mirrors bootstrap.sh.
20	if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ] && ! command -v brew >/dev/null 2>&1; then
21	    if [ -x /opt/homebrew/bin/brew ]; then
22	        eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
23	    elif [ -x /usr/local/bin/brew ]; then
24	        eval "$(/usr/local/bin/brew shellenv)"
25	    fi
26	fi
27	
28	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
29	# Helpers
30	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
31	
32	# Read a top-level string value from a JSON config file.
33	# Handles UTF-8 BOM (PowerShell 5.x writes one) and JSON-escaped backslashes.
34	read_config_key() {
35	    local file="$1" key="$2"
36	    [ -f "$file" ] || return 1
37	    local val
38	    val=$(tr -d '\357\273\277' < "$file" \
39	        | grep -o "\"$key\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\"[^\"]*\"" \
40	        | head -1 \
41	        | cut -d'"' -f4)
42	    [ -n "$val" ] || return 1
43	    # Unescape JSON backslashes: \\ -> \
44	    printf '%b' "$val"
45	}
46	
47	# Convert a Windows path to Unix-style for Git Bash / MSYS2. No-op elsewhere.
48	to_native_path() {
49	    if command -v cygpath &>/dev/null; then
50	        cygpath -u "$1"
51	    else
52	        printf '%s' "$1"
53	    fi
54	}
55	
56	# Display-friendly path for user-facing messages (native Windows on MSYS).
57	display_path() {
58	    if command -v cygpath &>/dev/null; then
59	        cygpath -w "$1"
60	    else
61	        printf '%s' "$1"
62	    fi
63	}
64	
65	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
66	# Logging
67	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
68	
69	LOG_DIR="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/aitools"
70	[ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ] && LOG_DIR="$HOME/Library/Logs/aitools"
71	LOG_FILE="$LOG_DIR/deploy.log"
72	mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
73	LOG_DISPLAY=$(display_path "$LOG_FILE")
74	ERRORS=0
75	WARNINGS=0
76	
77	log() {
78	    local level="${2:-info}"
79	    printf '[%s] [aitools] [%s] %s\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$level" "$1" >> "$LOG_FILE"
80	}
81	log_ok()    { log "$1" "ok"; }
82	log_error() { log "$1" "error"; printf 'error: %s\n' "$1" >&2; ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1)); }
83	log_warn()  { log "$1" "warn"; printf 'warning: %s\n' "$1" >&2; WARNINGS=$((WARNINGS + 1)); }
84	
85	# Check profile.json for issues and optionally prompt for fixes.
86	# Usage: check_profile <warn|interactive>
87	# Requires: node, $repo_path, $config
88	check_profile() {
89	    local mode="${1:-warn}"
90	    command -v node &>/dev/null || return 0
91	    [ -d "$repo_path" ] || return 0
92	
93	    local check_script="$repo_path/scripts/profile-check.js"
94	    [ -f "$check_script" ] || return 0
95	
96	    local result
97	    result=$(node "$check_script" --config "$config" 2>/dev/null) || return 0
98

101	        let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c);process.stdin.on('end',()=>{
102	            try{console.log(JSON.parse(d).status)}catch{console.log('error')}
103	        })
104	    " 2>/dev/null)
105	
106	    case "$status" in
107	        ok|unconfigured) return 0 ;;
108	        error)
109	            local msg
110	            msg=$(printf '%s' "$result" | node -e "
111	                let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c);process.stdin.on('end',()=>{
112	                    try{const r=JSON.parse(d);console.log((r.issues[0]&&r.issues[0].message)||'profile.json has issues')}catch{console.log('profile.json has issues')}

279	            fi
280	            git -C "$user_repo_dir" add -A
281	            git -C "$user_repo_dir" commit -m "Migrate profile.json from v1 to v2"
282	            git -C "$user_repo_dir" push 2>/dev/null || echo "  (push failed -- run 'git push' manually in $(display_path "$user_repo_dir"))"
283	            echo "Profile migrated and committed."
284	        fi
285	    fi
286	}
287	
288	# Version string from a git repo using tag-based scheme.
289	# v0.14.0              → 0.14.0       (on tag exactly)
290	# v0.14.0-5-gabcdef    → 0.14.0+5    (5 commits ahead of tag)
291	# The +N suffix indicates unreleased commits; it is never a real version.
292	repo_version() {
293	    local desc
294	    desc=$(git -C "$1" describe --tags --match "v*" 2>/dev/null) || true
295	    if [ -n "$desc" ]; then
296	        local base="${desc#v}"              # strip leading v
297	        if [[ "$base" =~ ^(.*)-([0-9]+)-g[0-9a-f]+$ ]]; then
298	            local tag_part="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"   # 0.14.0
299	            local commits="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"    # 5
300	            echo "${tag_part}+${commits}"
301	        else
302	            echo "$base"
303	        fi
304	    else
305	        # No tags yet — fallback to date + hash
306	        git -C "$1" log -1 --format='%cd (%h)' --date=short 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown"
307	    fi
308	}
309	
310	# Deploy all config scripts from the repo's scripts/ directory.
311	# On Windows (Git Bash), calls .ps1 variants via pwsh.
312	# Child scripts log to LOG_FILE themselves (via tee/Add-Content), so we
313	# redirect stdout to /dev/null to prevent double-logging.
314	deploy_configs() {
315	    local script_dir="$1"
316	    local errors=0
317	    export AITOOLS_DEPLOY=1
318	    if $dry_run; then export AITOOLS_DRY_RUN=1; fi
319	    if $force; then export AITOOLS_FORCE=1; fi
320	    case "$(uname -s)" in
321	        MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*)
322	            if ! command -v pwsh &>/dev/null; then
323	                log_error "pwsh (PowerShell 7) not found. Install: winget install --id Microsoft.PowerShell --source winget"
324	                return 1
325	            fi
326	            local deploy_scripts="setup-user-claude.ps1 setup-user-mcp.ps1 setup-user-skills.ps1 setup-cursor-ide-mcp.ps1 setup-user-cursor.ps1 setup-user-hooks.ps1"
327	            for script in $deploy_scripts; do
328	                local script_path="$script_dir/$script"
329	                if [ -f "$script_path" ]; then
330	                    # Validate PS1 syntax before executing
331	                    if ! pwsh -NoProfile -Command "
332	                        \$e = \$null
333	                        \$null = [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile('$(cygpath -w "$script_path")', [ref]\$null, [ref]\$e)
334	                        if (\$e.Count -gt 0) { exit 1 }
335	                    " 2>/dev/null; then
336	                        log_warn "$script has parse errors -- skipping"
337	                        errors=$((errors + 1))
338	                        continue
339	                    fi
340	                    # Run without output redirection -- child PS1 scripts log to
341	                    # deploy.log via [IO.File]::AppendAllText. PowerShell's 2>> holds
342	                    # an exclusive file lock that blocks the child's AppendAllText.
343	                    if ! pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass \
344	                        -File "$(cygpath -w "$script_path")"; then
345	                        log_error "$script failed (exit $?) -- see $LOG_DISPLAY"
346	                        errors=$((errors + 1))
347	                    fi
348	                else
349	                    log_warn "$script not found -- skipping"
350	                fi
351	                # Show cloud MCP status after setup-user-mcp
352	                case "$script" in
353	                    setup-user-mcp.*) show_cloud_mcp install setup-user-mcp ;;
354	                esac
355	            done
356	            ;;
357	        *)
358	            local deploy_scripts="setup-user-claude.sh setup-user-mcp.sh setup-user-skills.sh setup-cursor-ide-mcp.sh setup-user-cursor.sh setup-user-hooks.sh"
359	            for script in $deploy_scripts; do
360	                local script_path="$script_dir/$script"
361	                if [ -f "$script_path" ]; then
362	                    # Validate bash syntax before executing
363	                    if ! bash -n "$script_path" 2>/dev/null; then
364	                        log_warn "$script has syntax errors -- skipping"
365	                        errors=$((errors + 1))
366	                        continue
367	                    fi
368	                    # Run without output redirection -- child scripts log to
369	                    # deploy.log via >> append. Removing redirection ensures
370	                    # parity with the Windows fix and lets errors surface.
371	                    if ! bash "$script_path"; then
372	                        log_error "$script failed (exit $?) -- see $LOG_DISPLAY"
373	                        errors=$((errors + 1))
374	                    fi
375	                else
376	                    log_warn "$script not found -- skipping"
377	                fi
378	                # Show cloud MCP status after setup-user-mcp
379	                case "$script" in
380	                    setup-user-mcp.*) show_cloud_mcp install setup-user-mcp ;;
381	                esac
382	            done
383	            ;;
384	    esac
385	
386	    # Best-effort: mirror relay.md into ~/.cursor/AGENTS.md (Cursor IDE).
387	    # Non-fatal if Python or sync fails.
388	    local sync_py="$script_dir/sync-relay-to-cursor-agents.py"
389	    if [ -f "$sync_py" ]; then
390	        local sync_args=()
391	        if $dry_run; then sync_args+=(--dry-run); fi
392	        # Deploy-formatted line comes from Python when AITOOLS_SYNC_DEPLOY_LOG=1 (not --dry-run).
393	        if ! $dry_run; then export AITOOLS_SYNC_DEPLOY_LOG=1; fi
394	        if command -v python3 &>/dev/null; then
395	            if python3 "$sync_py" "${sync_args[@]}" >>"$LOG_FILE" 2>&1; then
396	                if $dry_run; then log_ok "relay→AGENTS sync (dry-run)"; fi
397	            else
398	                log_warn "sync-relay-to-cursor-agents.py failed (non-fatal)"
399	            fi
400	        elif command -v py &>/dev/null; then
401	            if py -3 "$sync_py" "${sync_args[@]}" >>"$LOG_FILE" 2>&1; then
402	                if $dry_run; then log_ok "relay→AGENTS sync (dry-run)"; fi
403	            else
404	                log_warn "sync-relay-to-cursor-agents.py failed (non-fatal)"
405	            fi
406	        else
407	            log_warn "Python not found — skipping relay→AGENTS sync"
408	        fi
409	        unset AITOOLS_SYNC_DEPLOY_LOG 2>/dev/null || true
410	    fi
411	
412	    unset AITOOLS_DEPLOY
413	    unset AITOOLS_DRY_RUN
414	    unset AITOOLS_FORCE
415	    return $errors
416	}

418	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
419	# MCP server registry
420	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
421	
422	# Returns URL for a known MCP server name, or empty string if unknown.
423	mcp_server_url() {
424	    case "$1" in
425	        vercel)  echo "https://mcp.vercel.com" ;;
426	        webflow) echo "https://mcp.webflow.com/mcp" ;;
427	        *)       echo "" ;;
428	    esac
429	}
430	
431	# Display cloud MCP servers from claude.ai configuration.
432	# Usage: show_cloud_mcp <context> [script_name]
433	#   context: "mcp" (concise header) or "install" (descriptive header)
434	#   script_name: if set, uses structured logging with [timestamp] [script_name] prefix
435	# Silent no-op if claude CLI unavailable or no cloud servers found.
436	show_cloud_mcp() {
437	    local context="${1:-mcp}"
438	    local script_name="${2:-}"
439	    command -v claude &>/dev/null || return 0
440	
441	    local saved_claudecode="${CLAUDECODE:-}"
442	    unset CLAUDECODE
443	
444	    local raw
445	    raw=$(claude mcp list 2>/dev/null) || true
446	
447	    if [ -n "$saved_claudecode" ]; then
448	        export CLAUDECODE="$saved_claudecode"
449	    fi
450	
451	    [ -n "$raw" ] || return 0
452	
453	    local parsed
454	    parsed=$(printf '%s\n' "$raw" | perl -ne '
455	        s/\e\[[0-9;]*m//g;
456	        next unless /^claude\.ai\s+(.+?):\s+.+\s+-\s+(.+)$/;
457	        my ($name, $status) = ($1, $2);
458	        $status =~ s/\s+$//;
459	        my $pad = length($name) < 24 ? " " x (24 - length($name)) : " ";
460	        printf "  %s%s%s\n", $name, $pad, $status;
461	    ')
462	
463	    [ -n "$parsed" ] || return 0
464	
465	    if [ -n "$script_name" ]; then
466	        # Structured logging for deploy sequence
467	        local ts
468	        ts=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
469	        printf '[%s] [%s] Cloud MCP servers (configured at claude.ai):\n' "$ts" "$script_name"
470	        while IFS= read -r line; do
471	            printf '[%s] [%s] %s\n' "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$script_name" "$line"
472	        done <<< "$parsed"
473	    else
474	        echo ""
475	        echo "Cloud (claude.ai):"
476	        printf '%s\n' "$parsed"
477	    fi
478	}
479	
480	# show_summary is provided by aitools-lib.sh (sourced after repo_path is resolved)
481	
482	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
483	# Usage / flags
484	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
485	
486	usage() {
487	    cat <<'EOF'
488	Usage: aitools [COMMAND] [OPTIONS]
489	
490	Commands:
491	  (none)               Sync configs: pull + rebuild + deploy all configurations
492	                       (deploy includes relay → ~/.cursor/AGENTS.md when Python is available)
493	  gitpull [--patch]    Update source: pull + rebuild + deploy + changelog + version tag
494	                       --patch: bump patch (v0.14.0 -> v0.14.1) instead of minor
495	  install              Full setup: pull + rebuild + install tools + deploy configs
496	                       (install Step 22 / deploy: relay → Cursor AGENTS.md mirror)
497	  mcp                  Show MCP server status for current project
498	  user init            Set up user repo and configure session archiving hook
499	  sessions list [proj] List archived sessions (optionally filter by project)
500	  sessions archive ID  Manually archive a session by ID (full or prefix)
501	  sessions move F proj Refile an archived session under a different project
502	  dashboard            Start the live mission control dashboard server
503	                       --stop: stop the server  --status: show server status
504	                       --snapshot: generate static HTML  --background: for hooks
505	
506	Options:
507	  --addmcp <name...>   Enable MCP server(s) for current project (vercel, webflow)
508	  --dry-run            Preview what would change without writing any files
509	  --force              Overwrite all files without prompting for review
510	  --version, -v        Show installed and repo version
511	  --help, -h           Show this help
512	
513	Install flags (passed through to installer):
514	  --skip-gh-auth       Skip GitHub CLI authentication
515	  --repos-path PATH    Set repos directory without prompting
516	  --skip-drive-detection  Skip Google Drive auto-detection
517	EOF
518	}
519	
520	show_version=false
521	show_help=false
522	do_install=false
523	do_gitpull=false
524	gitpull_patch=false
525	do_mcp_status=false
526	do_user=false
527	user_subcmd=""
528	do_sessions=false
529	sessions_subcmd=""
530	sessions_args=()
531	do_dashboard=false
532	dashboard_args=()
533	addmcp_seen=false
534	addmcp_servers=()
535	dry_run=false
536	force=false
537	passthrough=()
538	
539	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
540	    case "$1" in
541	        --version|-v) show_version=true; shift ;;
542	        --help|-h)    show_help=true; shift ;;
543	        --dry-run)    dry_run=true; shift ;;
544	        --force)      force=true; shift ;;
545	        install)      do_install=true; shift ;;
546	        gitpull)
547	            do_gitpull=true; shift
548	            if [[ $# -gt 0 && "$1" == "--patch" ]]; then
549	                gitpull_patch=true; shift
550	            fi
551	            ;;
552	        mcp)          do_mcp_status=true; shift ;;
553	        user)
554	            do_user=true
555	            shift
556	            if [[ $# -gt 0 && ! "$1" =~ ^-- ]]; then
557	                user_subcmd="$1"; shift
558	            fi
559	            ;;
560	        sessions)
561	            do_sessions=true
562	            shift
563	            if [[ $# -gt 0 && ! "$1" =~ ^-- ]]; then
564	                sessions_subcmd="$1"; shift
565	            fi
566	            # Collect remaining positional args for sessions subcommands
567	            while [[ $# -gt 0 && ! "$1" =~ ^-- ]]; do
568	                sessions_args+=("$1")
569	                shift
570	            done
571	            ;;
572	        dashboard)
573	            do_dashboard=true
574	            shift
575	            # Collect all remaining args for dashboard subcommand
576	            while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
577	                dashboard_args+=("$1")
578	                shift
579	            done
580	            ;;
581	        --addmcp)
582	            addmcp_seen=true
583	            shift
584	            # Collect all following args that don't start with --
585	            while [[ $# -gt 0 && ! "$1" =~ ^-- ]]; do
586	                addmcp_servers+=("$1")
587	                shift
588	            done
589	            ;;
590	        *)            passthrough+=("$1"); shift ;;
591	    esac
592	done
593	
594	# Reject unknown arguments when not installing (typos like "installs", "mcpp", etc.)
595	if ! $do_install && [ ${#passthrough[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
596	    log_error "unknown argument '${passthrough[0]}'"
597	    echo "Run 'aitools --help' for usage."
598	    return 1
599	fi
600	
601	# Reject --addmcp with no server names
602	if $addmcp_seen && [ ${#addmcp_servers[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
603	    log_error "--addmcp requires at least one server name (vercel, webflow)"
604	    return 1
605	fi
606	
607	if $show_help; then
608	    usage
609	    return 0
610	fi
611	
612	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
613	# Migrate config directory: ~/.config/ai-tooling/ -> ~/.aitools/
614	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
615	
616	old_config_dir="$HOME/.config/ai-tooling"
617	new_config_dir="$HOME/.aitools"
618	
619	if [ -d "$old_config_dir" ] && [ ! -d "$new_config_dir" ]; then
620	    mv "$old_config_dir" "$new_config_dir"
621	elif [ -d "$old_config_dir" ] && [ -d "$new_config_dir" ]; then
622	    log_warn "both $old_config_dir and $new_config_dir exist -- using $new_config_dir"
623	fi
624	
625	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
626	# Resolve repo path from config
627	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
628	
629	config="$HOME/.aitools/config.json"
630	repo_path=""
631	
632	if raw=$(read_config_key "$config" "repoPath") || raw=$(read_config_key "$config" "aiToolingRepoPath"); then
633	    repo_path=$(to_native_path "$raw")
634	fi
635	repo_path="${repo_path:-$HOME/repos/aitools}"
636	
637	# Auto-migrate: aiToolingRepoPath -> repoPath (repo renamed ai-tooling -> aitools)
638	if read_config_key "$config" "aiToolingRepoPath" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
639	    if command -v node &>/dev/null; then
640	        migrate_out=$(node -e "
641	const fs = require('fs');
642	const f = process.argv[1];
643	try {
644	    const cfg = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8'));
645	    if (!cfg.repoPath && cfg.aiToolingRepoPath) {
646	        cfg.repoPath = cfg.aiToolingRepoPath.replace(/ai-tooling/g, 'aitools');
647	    }
648	    delete cfg.aiToolingRepoPath;
649	    fs.writeFileSync(f, JSON.stringify(cfg, null, 2) + '\n');
650	    console.log('migrated');
651	} catch (e) {
652	    console.error('config migration failed: ' + e.message);
653	    process.exit(1);
654	}
655	" "$config" 2>&1) || log_warn "config key migration failed: $migrate_out"
656	        # Re-read repo_path after migration
657	        if raw=$(read_config_key "$config" "repoPath"); then
658	            repo_path=$(to_native_path "$raw")
659	        fi
660	    fi
661	fi
662	
663	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
664	# --version
665	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
666	
667	if $show_version; then
668	    echo "aitools $AITOOLS_INSTALLED_VERSION"
669	    if [ -d "$repo_path/.git" ]; then
670	        echo "  repo: $(repo_version "$repo_path") @ $(display_path "$repo_path")"
671	    fi
672	    return 0
673	fi
674	
675	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
676	# mcp — show MCP server status
677	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
678	
679	if $do_mcp_status; then
680	    if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
681	        log_error "node required for mcp status"
682	        return 1
683	    fi
684	
685	    node -e '
686	const fs = require("fs");
687	const path = require("path");
688	const os = require("os");
689	
690	const home = os.homedir();
691	const cwd = process.cwd();
692	
693	function readJson(f) {
694	    try { return JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(f, "utf8")); } catch { return null; }
695	}
696	
697	// --- Claude Code ---
698	const claudeJson = readJson(path.join(home, ".claude.json"));
699	const claudeSettings = readJson(path.join(home, ".claude", "settings.json"));
700	const projectSettings = readJson(path.join(cwd, ".claude", "settings.json"));
701	const projectLocalSettings = readJson(path.join(cwd, ".claude", "settings.local.json"));
702	
703	const claudeDeny = claudeSettings?.permissions?.deny || [];
704	const projectAllow = [
705	    ...(projectSettings?.permissions?.allow || []),
706	    ...(projectLocalSettings?.permissions?.allow || []),
707	];
708	
709	console.log("MCP Server Status (" + cwd + ")\n");
710	
711	if (claudeJson?.mcpServers) {
712	    console.log("Claude Code:");
713	    const servers = claudeJson.mcpServers;
714	    for (const [name, cfg] of Object.entries(servers)) {
715	        const transport = cfg.type === "http" || cfg.url ? "http" : "stdio";
716	        const denyPattern = "MCP(" + name + ")";
717	        const denied = claudeDeny.includes(denyPattern);
718	        const allowed = projectAllow.includes(denyPattern);
719	        const status = denied && !allowed ? "disabled" : "enabled";
720	        const pad = name.length < 16 ? " ".repeat(16 - name.length) : " ";
721	        console.log("  " + name + pad + status.padEnd(10) + "(user)   " + transport);
722	    }
723	
724	    // Show project overrides if any
725	    const overrides = [];
726	    for (const rule of projectAllow) {
727	        const match = rule.match(/^MCP\((.+)\)$/);
728	        if (match) {
729	            const source = projectLocalSettings?.permissions?.allow?.includes(rule)
730	                ? ".claude/settings.local.json"
731	                : ".claude/settings.json";
732	            overrides.push({ name: match[1], source });
733	        }
734	    }
735	    if (overrides.length > 0) {
736	        console.log("  Project overrides:");
737	        for (const o of overrides) {
738	            const pad = o.name.length < 16 ? " ".repeat(16 - o.name.length) : " ";
739	            console.log("    " + o.name + pad + "enabled   (" + o.source + ")");
740	        }
741	    }
742	} else {
743	    console.log("Claude Code: no user-level MCP config found (~/.claude.json)");
744	}
745	
746	console.log("");
747	
748	// --- Cursor ---
749	const cursorJson = readJson(path.join(home, ".cursor", "mcp.json"));
750	const projectCursorJson = readJson(path.join(cwd, ".cursor", "mcp.json"));
751	
752	if (cursorJson?.mcpServers) {
753	    console.log("Cursor:");
754	    const servers = cursorJson.mcpServers;
755	    for (const [name, cfg] of Object.entries(servers)) {
756	        const transport = cfg.url ? "http" : "stdio";
757	        // We cannot programmatically detect Cursor disable state from JSON alone
758	        const pad = name.length < 16 ? " ".repeat(16 - name.length) : " ";
759	        console.log("  " + name + pad + "(user)   " + transport);
760	    }
761	    if (projectCursorJson?.mcpServers) {
762	        console.log("  Project overrides (.cursor/mcp.json):");
763	        for (const [name, cfg] of Object.entries(projectCursorJson.mcpServers)) {
764	            const transport = cfg.url ? "http" : "stdio";
765	            const pad = name.length < 16 ? " ".repeat(16 - name.length) : " ";
766	            console.log("    " + name + pad + "enabled   " + transport);
767	        }
768	    }
769	} else {
770	    console.log("Cursor: no user-level MCP config found (~/.cursor/mcp.json)");
771	}
772	'
773	    show_cloud_mcp mcp
774	    return 0
775	fi
776	
777	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
778	# dashboard — mission control dashboard lifecycle
779	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
780	
781	if $do_dashboard; then
782	    # Dashboard is a standalone script that handles its own logging and summary.
783	    # Dispatch to aitools-dashboard.sh (macOS) or aitools-dashboard.ps1 (Windows).
784	    case "$(uname -s)" in
785	        MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*)
786	            if ! command -v pwsh &>/dev/null; then
787	                log_error "pwsh (PowerShell 7) not found"
788	                return 1
789	            fi
790	            pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass \
791	                -File "$(cygpath -w "$repo_path/scripts/aitools-dashboard.ps1")" \
792	                "${dashboard_args[@]}"
793	            ;;
794	        *)
795	            bash "$repo_path/scripts/aitools-dashboard.sh" "${dashboard_args[@]}"
796	            ;;
797	    esac
798	    return $?
799	fi
800	
801	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
802	# --addmcp — enable MCP server(s) for current project
803	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
804	
805	if [ ${#addmcp_servers[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
806	    # Validate all server names first
807	    for name in "${addmcp_servers[@]}"; do
808	        url=$(mcp_server_url "$name")
809	        if [ -z "$url" ]; then
810	            log_error "unknown MCP server '$name'"
811	            echo "Supported servers: vercel, webflow"
812	            return 1
813	        fi
814	    done
815	
816	    # Warn if cwd doesn't look like a project
817	    if [ ! -d ".git" ] && [ ! -f "package.json" ] && [ ! -f "pyproject.toml" ]; then
818	        log_warn "current directory doesn't look like a project root"
819	        echo "  cwd: $(display_path "$(pwd)")"
820	        echo ""
821	    fi
822	
823	    for name in "${addmcp_servers[@]}"; do
824	        url=$(mcp_server_url "$name")
825	        echo "Enabling $name for this project..."
826	
827	        # --- Claude Code: .claude/settings.local.json (allow override) ---
828	        settings_local=".claude/settings.local.json"
829	        if command -v node &>/dev/null; then
830	            mkdir -p .claude
831	            node -e "
832	const fs = require('fs');
833	const f = process.argv[1];
834	let settings = {};
835	try { settings = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8')); } catch (e) { if (e.code !== 'ENOENT') console.error('Warning: ' + f + ' is invalid JSON, starting with empty config'); }
836	if (!settings.permissions) settings.permissions = {};
837	if (!Array.isArray(settings.permissions.allow)) settings.permissions.allow = [];
838	const rule = 'MCP($name)';
839	if (!settings.permissions.allow.includes(rule)) {
840	    settings.permissions.allow.push(rule);
841	}
842	fs.writeFileSync(f, JSON.stringify(settings, null, 2) + '\n');
843	
844	// Post-write validation
845	const _v = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8'));

52	    cat <<'USAGE'
53	aitools-install.sh — Install aitools command + configure environment
54	
55	Usage: bash scripts/aitools-install.sh [OPTIONS]
56	
57	Options:
58	  --repos-path PATH         Set repos directory without prompting (default: ~/repos)
59	  --skip-drive-detection    Skip Google Drive auto-detection
60	  --skip-gh-auth            Skip gh auth login
61	  --dry-run                 Preview mode -- show what would change without writing
62	  --help, -h                Show this help
63	
64	Interactive behavior:
65	  When stdin is a terminal, prompts for repos path and drive confirmation.
66	  When piped or run non-interactively, uses defaults and flags.
67	  When config.json already exists, uses saved values without prompting.
68	USAGE
69	    exit 0
70	fi
71	
72	# --- Windows forwarding (safety net for direct invocation) ---
73	case "$(uname -s)" in
74	    MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*)
75	        ps1_installer="$(dirname "$0")/aitools-install.ps1"
76	        if [ ! -f "$ps1_installer" ]; then
77	            echo "error: aitools-install.ps1 not found" >&2
78	            exit 1
79	        fi
80	        ps_args=()
81	        if $SKIP_GH_AUTH; then ps_args+=("-SkipGhAuth"); fi
82	        if $SKIP_DRIVE_DETECTION; then ps_args+=("-SkipDriveDetection"); fi
83	        if $DRY_RUN; then ps_args+=("-DryRun"); fi
84	        if [ -n "$REPOS_PATH" ]; then
85	            ps_args+=("-ReposPath" "$(cygpath -w "$REPOS_PATH")")
86	        fi
87	        echo "Windows detected -- forwarding to PowerShell installer..."
88	        # Bootstrap: if pwsh not installed, use powershell.exe to install it via winget
89	        if ! command -v pwsh &>/dev/null; then
90	            echo "pwsh (PowerShell 7) not found -- installing via winget..."
91	            powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command 'winget install --id Microsoft.PowerShell --source winget --accept-package-agreements --accept-source-agreements'
92	            # Refresh PATH hash so pwsh is found
93	            hash -r
94	            if ! command -v pwsh &>/dev/null; then
95	                echo "error: pwsh install succeeded but not in PATH. Restart terminal and re-run." >&2
96	                exit 1
97	            fi
98	        fi
99	        pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass \
100	            -File "$(cygpath -w "$ps1_installer")" "${ps_args[@]}"
101	        exit $?
102	        ;;
103	esac
104	
105	# --- Shared library ---
106	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
107	source "$SCRIPT_DIR/aitools-lib.sh"
108	logging_init "aitools-install"
109	
110	# JSONL logging (extends standard pattern with structured JSON)
111	LOG_JSONL="$LOG_DIR/deploy.jsonl"
112	RUN_ID="${AITOOLS_RUN_ID:-$(head -c 6 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')}"
113	HOST_NAME="$(hostname -s 2>/dev/null || hostname)"
114	OS_NAME="$(uname -s)"
115	
116	if $DRY_RUN; then export AITOOLS_DRY_RUN=1; fi
117	
118	# Override: JSONL dual-format (human-readable + structured JSON)
119	log() {
120	    local level="${2:-info}"
121	    local ts; ts="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
122	    printf '[%s] [%s] [%s] %s\n' "$ts" "$SCRIPT_NAME" "$level" "$1" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
123	    printf '{"ts":"%s","host":"%s","os":"%s","script":"%s","run_id":"%s","level":"%s","msg":"%s"}\n' \
124	        "$ts" "$HOST_NAME" "$OS_NAME" "$SCRIPT_NAME" "$RUN_ID" "$level" "$1" >> "$LOG_JSONL"
125	}
126	log_ok()    { log "$1" "ok"; }
127	log_error() { log "$1" "error"; ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1)); }
128	log_warn()  { log "$1" "warn"; WARNINGS=$((WARNINGS + 1)); }
129	
130	# --- Summary file init (if not already set by parent aitools invocation) ---
131	if [ -z "${AITOOLS_SUMMARY_FILE:-}" ]; then
132	    AITOOLS_SUMMARY_FILE="$HOME/.aitools/run-summary.txt"
133	    rm -f "$AITOOLS_SUMMARY_FILE"
134	    touch "$AITOOLS_SUMMARY_FILE"
135	    export AITOOLS_SUMMARY_FILE
136	fi
137	
138	# --- Script validation helper ---
139	# Validates bash syntax with bash -n before executing. Skips with warning on errors.
140	validate_and_run() {
141	    local script="$1"
142	    local name; name=$(basename "$script")
143	    if ! bash -n "$script" 2>/dev/null; then
144	        log_warn "$name has syntax errors -- skipping"
145	        return 0
146	    fi
147	    bash "$script" || log_error "$name failed"
148	}
149	
150	# display_path is provided by aitools-lib.sh
151	
152	# --- Post-write JSON validation ---
153	# Validates a JSON config file after writing: checks non-empty, valid JSON,
154	# required keys present, and no double-slash paths (excluding protocol prefixes).
155	$DRY_RUN && log "[DRY RUN] Preview mode -- no files will be written"
156	
157	validate_json_config() {
158	    local file="$1"; shift
159	    local required_keys=("$@")
160	    if [ ! -s "$file" ]; then
161	        log_error "Validation failed: $file is empty or missing"
162	        return 1
163	    fi
164	    local validator=""
165	    if command -v python3 &>/dev/null; then validator="python3"
166	    elif command -v node &>/dev/null; then validator="node"
167	    fi
168	    if [ -z "$validator" ]; then
169	        log_warn "Cannot validate JSON (no python3 or node)"
170	        return 0
171	    fi
172	    # Valid JSON check
173	    if [ "$validator" = "python3" ]; then
174	        if ! python3 -c "import json,sys; json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))" "$file" 2>/dev/null; then
175	            log_error "Validation failed: $file is not valid JSON"
176	            return 1
177	        fi
178	    else
179	        if ! node -e "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync(process.argv[1],'utf8'))" "$file" 2>/dev/null; then
180	            log_error "Validation failed: $file is not valid JSON"
181	            return 1
182	        fi
183	    fi
184	    # Required fields check
185	    for key in "${required_keys[@]}"; do
186	        if ! grep -q "\"$key\"" "$file"; then
187	            log_error "Validation failed: $file missing required field '$key'"
188	            return 1
189	        fi
190	    done
191	    # Double-slash path check (skip protocol prefixes like https://)
192	    if [ "$validator" = "python3" ]; then
193	        local ds_result
194	        ds_result=$(python3 -c "
195	import json,sys
196	def check(o,p=''):
197	    if isinstance(o,str):
198	        s=o.replace('https://','').replace('http://','')
199	        if '//' in s: print(f'double-slash at {p}: {o}',file=sys.stderr); sys.exit(1)
200	    elif isinstance(o,dict):
201	        for k,v in o.items(): check(v,f'{p}.{k}')
202	    elif isinstance(o,list):
203	        for i,v in enumerate(o): check(v,f'{p}[{i}]')
204	check(json.load(open(sys.argv[1])))
205	" "$file" 2>&1)
206	        if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
207	            log_error "Validation failed: $file contains double-slash in path value"
208	            return 1
209	        fi
210	    fi
211	    return 0
212	}
213	
214	# --- Config helpers (pure-bash, no python3 dependency) ---
215	
216	# Read a top-level string value from a JSON config file.
217	# Handles UTF-8 BOM (PowerShell 5.x writes one) and JSON-escaped backslashes.
218	read_config_key() {
219	    local file="$1" key="$2"
220	    [ -f "$file" ] || return 1
221	    local val
222	    val=$(tr -d '\357\273\277' < "$file" \
223	        | grep -o "\"$key\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\"[^\"]*\"" | head -1 | cut -d'"' -f4 || true)
224	    [ -n "$val" ] || return 1
225	    # Unescape JSON backslashes: \\ -> \
226	    printf '%b' "$val"
227	}
228	
229	# Read the raw googleDrives JSON array from a config file.
230	# Returns "[]" if not found or empty.
231	read_config_drives() {
232	    local file="$1"
233	    [ -f "$file" ] || { echo "[]"; return; }
234	    local result
235	    result=$(tr -d '\357\273\277\r' < "$file" \
236	        | sed -n '/"googleDrives"/,/^[[:space:]]*\]/p' \
237	        | sed '1s/.*\[/[/' \
238	        | sed '$s/],*/]/')
239	    if [ -z "$result" ] || [ "$result" = "[]" ]; then
240	        echo "[]"
241	    else
242	        printf '%s' "$result"
243	    fi
244	}

246	# --- Config file setup ---
247	CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.aitools"
248	CONFIG_FILE="$CONFIG_DIR/config.json"
249	mkdir -p "$CONFIG_DIR"
250	
251	# Auto-detect aitools repo path from this script's location
252	# SCRIPT_DIR is set at top (lib sourcing)
253	AITOOLS_REPO="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
254	
255	# ============================================================
256	# 0. System prerequisites
257	# ============================================================
258	# Windows long path check is in aitools-install.ps1 (Step 0).
259	# macOS/Linux: ensure Homebrew is on PATH so brew- and node-dependent steps work
260	# even when invoked non-interactively (no profile sourced). Mirrors bootstrap.sh.
261	if [ "$OS_NAME" = "Darwin" ] && ! command -v brew >/dev/null 2>&1; then
262	    if [ -x /opt/homebrew/bin/brew ]; then
263	        eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
264	    elif [ -x /usr/local/bin/brew ]; then
265	        eval "$(/usr/local/bin/brew shellenv)"
266	    fi
267	fi

269	# ============================================================
270	# 1. Install/update gh CLI
271	# ============================================================
272	log "Step 1: gh CLI"
273	
274	gh_script="$SCRIPT_DIR/setup-gh-cli.sh"
275	if [ -f "$gh_script" ]; then
276	    validate_and_run "$gh_script"
277	else
278	    log_warn "setup-gh-cli.sh not found — skipping (MDM deploy)"
279	fi
280	
281	# ============================================================
282	# 2. Authenticate gh
283	# ============================================================
284	log "Step 2: gh authentication"
285	
286	if $SKIP_GH_AUTH; then
287	    log "Skipping gh auth (--skip-gh-auth)"
288	elif ! command -v gh &>/dev/null; then
289	    log_warn "gh not installed, skipping auth"
290	elif gh auth status &>/dev/null; then
291	    log_ok "gh already authenticated"
292	elif [ -t 0 ]; then
293	    log "Not authenticated. Starting gh auth login..."
294	    gh auth login || log_error "gh auth login failed"
295	else
296	    log_warn "Not authenticated and not interactive — skipping gh auth (use --skip-gh-auth to suppress)"
297	fi
298	
299	# ============================================================
300	# 3. Configure repos directory
301	# ============================================================
302	log "Step 3: repos directory"
303	
304	if [ -n "$REPOS_PATH" ]; then
305	    # Flag provided — use it
306	    REPOS_PATH="${REPOS_PATH/#\~/$HOME}"
307	    log "Using repos path from flag: $REPOS_PATH"
308	elif REPOS_PATH=$(read_config_key "$CONFIG_FILE" "reposPath"); then
309	    log "Using repos path from config: $REPOS_PATH"
310	fi
311	if [ -z "$REPOS_PATH" ]; then
312	    if [ -t 0 ]; then
313	        # Interactive — prompt
314	        printf 'Where should new repos live? [~/repos]: '
315	        read -r user_path
316	        if [ -n "$user_path" ]; then
317	            REPOS_PATH="${user_path/#\~/$HOME}"
318	        else
319	            REPOS_PATH="$HOME/repos"
320	        fi
321	    else
322	        # Non-interactive — use default
323	        REPOS_PATH="$HOME/repos"
324	    fi
325	fi
326	
327	mkdir -p "$REPOS_PATH"
328	log_ok "Repos directory: $REPOS_PATH"

330	# ============================================================
331	# 4. Detect Google Drive mounts
332	# ============================================================
333	log "Step 4: Google Drive detection"
334	
335	DRIVES_JSON="[]"
336	
337	if $SKIP_DRIVE_DETECTION; then
338	    log "Skipping drive detection (--skip-drive-detection)"
339	else
340	    DRIVE_LIST=""
341	
342	    if [ "$OS_NAME" = "Darwin" ]; then
343	        # macOS: scan ~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-*/
344	        for dir in "$HOME/Library/CloudStorage"/GoogleDrive-*/; do
345	            [ -d "$dir" ] || continue
346	            account=$(basename "$dir" | sed 's/^GoogleDrive-//')
347	            my_drive="${dir%/}/My Drive"
348	            if [ -d "$my_drive" ]; then
349	                DRIVE_LIST="${DRIVE_LIST}${account}|${my_drive}\n"
350	                log_ok "Detected Google Drive: $account → $my_drive"
351	            fi
352	        done
353	    else
354	        # Linux/WSL: check if any Google Drive mounts exist via known paths
355	        # (Google Drive for Desktop on Linux is rare — mostly a no-op)
356	        log "Non-macOS detected — Google Drive auto-detection not supported on this platform via bash"
357	        log "Use aitools-install.ps1 on Windows for drive detection"
358	    fi
359	
360	    # Build JSON array
361	    if [ -n "$DRIVE_LIST" ]; then
362	        DRIVES_JSON="["
363	        first=true
364	        while IFS='|' read -r account path; do
365	            [ -z "$account" ] && continue
366	            if $first; then
367	                first=false
368	            else
369	                DRIVES_JSON="${DRIVES_JSON},"
370	            fi
371	            # Escape backslashes for JSON
372	            escaped_path=$(printf '%s' "$path" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g')
373	            DRIVES_JSON="${DRIVES_JSON}{\"path\":\"${escaped_path}\",\"account\":\"${account}\",\"label\":\"\"}"
374	        done < <(printf "$DRIVE_LIST")
375	        DRIVES_JSON="${DRIVES_JSON}]"
376	    fi
377	fi
378	
379	# ============================================================
380	# 5. Write config file
381	# ============================================================
382	log "Step 5: Writing config"
383	
384	# Convert MSYS paths to native Windows paths for config.json
385	if command -v cygpath &>/dev/null; then
386	    REPOS_PATH_NATIVE=$(cygpath -w "$REPOS_PATH")
387	    AITOOLS_NATIVE=$(cygpath -w "$AITOOLS_REPO")
388	else
389	    REPOS_PATH_NATIVE="$REPOS_PATH"
390	    AITOOLS_NATIVE="$AITOOLS_REPO"
391	fi
392	
393	# Escape backslashes for JSON
394	REPOS_PATH_JSON=$(printf '%s' "$REPOS_PATH_NATIVE" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g')
395	AITOOLS_JSON=$(printf '%s' "$AITOOLS_NATIVE" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g')
396	
397	# If config already exists, preserve fields we don't manage
398	USER_REPO_LINE=""
399	MACHINE_ALIAS_LINE=""
400	if [ -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
401	    # Preserve googleDrives if we didn't detect any
402	    if [ "$DRIVES_JSON" = "[]" ]; then
403	        EXISTING_DRIVES=$(read_config_drives "$CONFIG_FILE")
404	        if [ "$EXISTING_DRIVES" != "[]" ]; then
405	            DRIVES_JSON="$EXISTING_DRIVES"
406	            log "Preserved existing Google Drive entries from config"
407	        fi
408	    fi
409	    # Preserve userRepoPath (set by 'aitools user init')
410	    # `|| true`: read_config_key returns nonzero when the key is absent (pre user-init);
411	    # without the guard, set -e aborts the install on a fresh/unpersonalized machine.
412	    EXISTING_USER_REPO=$(read_config_key "$CONFIG_FILE" "userRepoPath") || true
413	    if [ -n "$EXISTING_USER_REPO" ]; then
414	        # printf -v preserves trailing \n ($() command substitution strips it)
415	        printf -v USER_REPO_LINE '  "userRepoPath": "%s",\n' "$EXISTING_USER_REPO"
416	    fi
417	    # Preserve machineAlias (set by 'aitools user init')
418	    EXISTING_MACHINE_ALIAS=$(read_config_key "$CONFIG_FILE" "machineAlias") || true
419	    if [ -n "$EXISTING_MACHINE_ALIAS" ]; then
420	        printf -v MACHINE_ALIAS_LINE '  "machineAlias": "%s",\n' "$EXISTING_MACHINE_ALIAS"
421	    fi
422	fi
423	
424	cat > "$CONFIG_FILE" << CONFIGEOF
425	{
426	  "version": 2,
427	  "reposPath": "$REPOS_PATH_JSON",
428	  "repoPath": "$AITOOLS_JSON",
429	${USER_REPO_LINE}${MACHINE_ALIAS_LINE}  "googleDrives": $DRIVES_JSON
430	}
431	CONFIGEOF
432	
433	log_ok "Config written to $(display_path "$CONFIG_FILE")"
434	validate_json_config "$CONFIG_FILE" version reposPath repoPath || true
435

437	# 6. Install aitools command
438	# ============================================================
439	log "Step 6: Install aitools command"
440	
441	AITOOLS_SRC="$SCRIPT_DIR/aitools"
442	AITOOLS_DST="$HOME/.local/bin/aitools"
443	mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
444	if [ -f "$AITOOLS_SRC" ]; then
445	    cp "$AITOOLS_SRC" "$AITOOLS_DST"
446	    chmod +x "$AITOOLS_DST"
447	    log_ok "Installed aitools to $(display_path "$AITOOLS_DST")"
448	else
449	    log_warn "aitools source not found at $(display_path "$AITOOLS_SRC") (MDM deploy — skipping)"
450	fi

452	# Honest harness (hh): status + aitools
453	HH_SRC="$SCRIPT_DIR/hh.sh"
454	HH_DST="$HOME/.local/bin/hh"
455	if [ -f "$HH_SRC" ]; then
456	    cp "$HH_SRC" "$HH_DST"
457	    chmod +x "$HH_DST"
458	    log_ok "Installed hh to $(display_path "$HH_DST")"
459	else
460	    log_warn "hh.sh not found — skipping"
461	fi

463	# ============================================================
464	# 7. Shell integration
465	# ============================================================
466	log "Step 7: Shell integration"
467	
468	ALIASES_PATH="$SCRIPT_DIR/../shared/shell/aliases.sh"
469	if [ -f "$ALIASES_PATH" ]; then
470	    ALIASES_ABS=$(cd "$(dirname "$ALIASES_PATH")" && pwd)/$(basename "$ALIASES_PATH")
471	    OLD_MARKER="# ai-tooling shell integration"
472	    MARKER="# aitools shell integration"
473	    for rcfile in "$HOME/.bashrc" "$HOME/.zshrc"; do
474	        # Only add to files that exist OR create .bashrc as fallback
475	        if [ "$rcfile" = "$HOME/.bashrc" ] || [ -f "$rcfile" ]; then
476	            # Remove old marker block if present
477	            if grep -qF "$OLD_MARKER" "$rcfile" 2>/dev/null; then
478	                perl -i -0777 -pe 's/\n?# ai-tooling shell integration\nsource "[^\n]*"\n?//g' "$rcfile"
479	                log "Removed old shell integration marker from $(display_path "$rcfile")"
480	            fi
481	            if ! grep -qF "$MARKER" "$rcfile" 2>/dev/null; then
482	                printf '\n%s\nsource "%s"\n' "$MARKER" "$ALIASES_ABS" >> "$rcfile"
483	                log_ok "Added shell integration to $(display_path "$rcfile")"
484	            else
485	                log_ok "Shell integration already in $(display_path "$rcfile")"
486	            fi
487	        fi
488	    done
489	else
490	    log_warn "aliases.sh not found — skipping shell integration (MDM deploy)"
491	fi

497	
498	if command -v node &>/dev/null; then
499	    log_ok "Node.js already installed ($(node --version))"
500	    write_summary OK "node.js" "$(node --version)"
501	else
502	    case "$OS_NAME" in
503	        Darwin)
504	            if command -v brew &>/dev/null; then
505	                log "Installing Node.js via Homebrew..."
506	                if ! brew install node@22 2>&1 | while IFS= read -r line; do log "$line"; done; then
507	                    log_error "brew install node@22 failed"
508	                    write_summary ERROR "node.js" "brew install failed"
509	                fi
510	                if command -v node &>/dev/null; then
511	                    log_ok "Node.js installed ($(node --version))"
512	                    write_summary OK "node.js" "$(node --version)"
513	                else
514	                    log_error "brew install completed but 'node' not found in PATH"
515	                    write_summary ERROR "node.js" "installed but not on PATH"
516	                fi
517	            else
518	                log_error "Homebrew not found. Install Node.js manually: https://nodejs.org"
519	                write_summary ERROR "node.js" "Homebrew not found"
520	            fi
521	            ;;
522	        MINGW*|MSYS*)
523	            log "Windows detected — install Node.js via winget (use aitools-install.ps1)"
524	            ;;
525	        *)
526	            log_warn "Install Node.js manually: https://nodejs.org"
527	            write_summary WARN "node.js" "install manually (https://nodejs.org)"
528	            ;;
529	    esac
530	fi
531	
532	# ============================================================
533	# 9. Claude Code CLI
534	# ============================================================
535	# Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup
536	log "Step 9: Claude Code CLI"
537	
538	if command -v claude &>/dev/null; then
539	    log_ok "Claude Code already installed ($(claude --version 2>/dev/null | head -1))"
540	    write_summary OK "claude code" "$(claude --version 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
541	    log "Running claude update..."
542	    UPDATE_OUTPUT=$(claude update 2>&1) || true
543	    if printf '%s\n' "$UPDATE_OUTPUT" | grep -qi 'already.*up.to.date\|no update'; then
544	        log_ok "Already up to date"
545	    else
546	        printf '%s\n' "$UPDATE_OUTPUT" | while IFS= read -r line; do log "$line"; done
547	        if printf '%s\n' "$UPDATE_OUTPUT" | grep -qi 'error\|fatal'; then
548	            log_warn "claude update returned unexpected output (see log above)"
549	        fi
550	    fi
551	else
552	    log "Installing Claude Code CLI..."
553	    case "$OS_NAME" in
554	        MINGW*|MSYS*)
555	            # WinGet works from Git Bash
556	            if command -v winget &>/dev/null; then
557	                # Suppress winget progress noise; install success checked via command -v below
558	                winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode --accept-package-agreements --accept-source-agreements 2>/dev/null
559	                if command -v claude &>/dev/null; then
560	                    log_ok "Claude Code installed ($(claude --version 2>/dev/null | head -1))"
561	                    write_summary OK "claude code" "$(claude --version 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
562	                else
563	                    log_warn "Claude Code installed — restart terminal to use"
564	                    write_summary WARN "claude code" "installed -- restart terminal to use"
565	                fi
566	            else
567	                log "winget not available — install manually:"
568	                log "  PowerShell: irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex"
569	            fi
570	            ;;
571	        *)
572	            if ! curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash 2>&1 | while IFS= read -r line; do log "$line"; done; then
573	                log_error "Claude Code install script failed"
574	                write_summary ERROR "claude code" "install failed"
575	            fi
576	            if command -v claude &>/dev/null; then
577	                log_ok "Claude Code installed ($(claude --version 2>/dev/null | head -1))"
578	                write_summary OK "claude code" "$(claude --version 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
579	            else
580	                log_error "Claude Code install failed"
581	                write_summary ERROR "claude code" "install failed"
582	            fi
583	            ;;
584	    esac
585	fi

591	
592	vercel_script="$SCRIPT_DIR/setup-vercelcli.sh"
593	if [ -f "$vercel_script" ]; then
594	    validate_and_run "$vercel_script"

596	    log_warn "setup-vercelcli.sh not found — skipping (MDM deploy)"
597	fi

599	# ============================================================
600	# 11. Pandoc
601	# ============================================================
602	log "Step 11: Pandoc"
