1	# aitools-lib.sh -- shared helpers for all aitools bash scripts
2	# Sourced, not executed directly. No shebang, no set -euo pipefail (caller sets it).
3	#
4	# Provides: platform detection, display_path, read_config_key, logging_init,
5	# log/log_ok/log_error/log_warn/log_detail, invoke_ai, write_summary,
6	# show_summary, SORT_KEYS_JS, normalize_json.
7	#
8	# Usage:
9	#   source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/aitools-lib.sh"
10	#   logging_init "script-name"
11	#
12	# Entry points (aitools, aitools-install) override log functions after sourcing
13	# for specialized logging (file-only, JSONL, etc.).
14	
15	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
16	# Platform detection
17	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
18	IS_MACOS=false
19	IS_WINDOWS=false
20	case "$(uname -s)" in
21	    Darwin*)              IS_MACOS=true ;;
22	    MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) IS_WINDOWS=true ;;
23	esac
24	
25	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
26	# Log directory (platform-aware)
27	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
28	AITOOLS_LOG_DIR="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/aitools"
29	$IS_MACOS && AITOOLS_LOG_DIR="$HOME/Library/Logs/aitools"
30	
31	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
32	# Module-level counters (safe for sourcing without logging_init under set -u)
33	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
34	ERRORS=0
35	WARNINGS=0
36	
37	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
38	# Display-friendly path (native Windows on MSYS, no-op elsewhere)
39	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
40	display_path() {
41	    if command -v cygpath &>/dev/null; then
42	        cygpath -w "$1"
43	    else
44	        printf '%s' "$1"
45	    fi
46	}
47	
48	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
49	# Config reader (pure bash, handles UTF-8 BOM)
50	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
51	# Read a top-level string value from a JSON config file.
52	# Handles UTF-8 BOM (PowerShell 5.x writes one) and JSON-escaped backslashes.
53	read_config_key() {
54	    local file="$1" key="$2"
55	    [ -f "$file" ] || return 1
56	    local val
57	    val=$(tr -d '\357\273\277' < "$file" \
58	        | grep -o "\"$key\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\"[^\"]*\"" \
59	        | head -1 \
60	        | cut -d'"' -f4)
61	    [ -n "$val" ] || return 1
62	    # Unescape JSON backslashes: \\ -> \
63	    printf '%b' "$val"
64	}
65	
66	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
67	# Logging init
68	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
69	# Sets SCRIPT_NAME, LOG_DIR, LOG_FILE; resets ERRORS, WARNINGS; creates log dir.
70	# Usage: logging_init "setup-foo"
71	logging_init() {
72	    SCRIPT_NAME="${1:?logging_init requires a script name}"
73	    LOG_DIR="$AITOOLS_LOG_DIR"
74	    LOG_FILE="$LOG_DIR/deploy.log"
75	    mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
76	    ERRORS=0
77	    WARNINGS=0
78	}
79	
80	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
81	# Standard logging (Pattern A: console + log file, with [level] tag)
82	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
83	log() {
84	    local level="${2:-info}"
85	    local ts; ts="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
86	    local line="[$ts] [$SCRIPT_NAME] [$level] $1"
87	    printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$LOG_FILE"
88	    case "$level" in
89	        error) printf '\033[31m%s\033[0m\n' "$line" ;;
90	        warn)  printf '\033[33m%s\033[0m\n' "$line" ;;
91	        *)     printf '%s\n' "$line" ;;
92	    esac
93	}
94	log_ok()    { log "$1" "ok"; }
95	log_error() { log "$1" "error"; ERRORS=$((ERRORS + 1)); }
96	log_warn()  { log "$1" "warn"; WARNINGS=$((WARNINGS + 1)); }
97	log_detail() {
98	    local ts; ts="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
99	    printf '[%s] [%s] [detail] %s\n' "$ts" "$SCRIPT_NAME" "$1" >> "$LOG_FILE"
100	}
101	
102	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
103	# Agentic AI invocation -- generalized wrapper for claude/agent CLI
104	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
105	# Purpose: Standardized AI CLI invocation with speed/permission tiers,
106	#   validation callbacks, automatic retry, and telemetry logging.
107	# Inputs: SPEED (fast/balanced/quality), PERMISSIONS (none/readonly/full/
108	#   dangerous), VALIDATE_FN (function name, receives output as $1),
109	#   MAX_RETRIES (retry count on validation failure). Prompt from stdin.
110	# Expected output: Raw AI-generated text on stdout.
111	# Validation: Caller-provided VALIDATE_FN must return 0 (pass) or 1 (fail)
112	#   and set AI_REJECT_REASON on failure.
113	# Known limitations: Agent CLI has no --model flag; speed is hint-only via
114	#   prompt prefix. Retry prepends rejection reason but may not fix structural
115	#   issues (e.g., model always wrapping in code fences).
116	
117	# File-only AI telemetry logging (avoids stdout capture interference when
118	# invoke_ai output is captured via $()). Does not increment ERRORS/WARNINGS --
119	# callers decide whether to count invoke_ai failures.
120	_ai_log() {
121	    local ts; ts="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
122	    printf '[%s] [%s] [%s] %s\n' "$ts" "$SCRIPT_NAME" "${2:-info}" "$1" >> "${LOG_FILE:-/dev/null}"
123	}
124	
125	AI_REJECT_REASON=""
126	
127	invoke_ai() {
128	    local speed="${1:-balanced}"
129	    local permissions="${2:-none}"
130	    local validate_fn="${3:-}"
131	    local max_retries="${4:-0}"
132	
133	    AI_REJECT_REASON=""
134	
135	    # Read prompt from stdin
136	    local prompt
137	    prompt=$(cat)
138	
139	    # Detect backend
140	    # command -v exempt: existence check with explicit fallback chain
141	    local cli_cmd=""
142	    if command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1; then
143	        cli_cmd="claude"
144	    elif $IS_WINDOWS; then
145	        # Windows Git Bash: agent may be on PowerShell PATH only
146	        local agent_path
147	        agent_path=$(pwsh -NoProfile -Command \
148	            'Get-Command agent -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Source' \
149	            2>/dev/null) || true  # pwsh may not be installed; fallback is no agent CLI
150	        if [ -n "$agent_path" ]; then cli_cmd="agent"; fi
151	    elif command -v agent >/dev/null 2>&1; then
152	        cli_cmd="agent"
153	    fi
154	
155	    if [ -z "$cli_cmd" ]; then
156	        AI_REJECT_REASON="No AI CLI available (claude or agent)"
157	        _ai_log "AI invocation: no CLI available (claude or agent)" "error"
158	        return 1
159	    fi
160	
161	    # Build CLI flags
162	    local -a flags=()
163	
164	    if [ "$cli_cmd" = "claude" ]; then
165	        flags+=("-p" "--no-session-persistence")
166	        # Speed mapping (claude CLI: explicit model + effort)
167	        case "$speed" in
168	            fast)     flags+=("--model" "haiku" "--effort" "low") ;;
169	            balanced) flags+=("--model" "sonnet") ;;
170	            quality)  flags+=("--model" "opus" "--effort" "high") ;;
171	        esac
172	        # Permission mapping
173	        case "$permissions" in
174	            none)      flags+=("--allowedTools" "") ;;
175	            readonly)  flags+=("--allowedTools" "Read Glob Grep") ;;
176	            full)      ;; # default -- no restriction
177	            dangerous) flags+=("--dangerously-skip-permissions") ;;
178	        esac
179	        # System prompt hints for speed tiers
180	        case "$speed" in
181	            fast)    flags+=("--append-system-prompt" "Be concise and direct.") ;;
182	            quality) flags+=("--append-system-prompt" "Take your time. Be thorough.") ;;
183	        esac
184	    else
185	        # Agent CLI -- no --model flag; speed via prompt prefix only
186	        flags+=("-p" "--trust")
187	        # Permission mapping
188	        case "$permissions" in
189	            none)      flags+=("--mode" "ask") ;;
190	            readonly)  flags+=("--mode" "plan") ;;
191	            full)      ;; # default
192	            dangerous) flags+=("--force") ;;
193	        esac
194	    fi
195	
196	    # Speed prefix for agent CLI (no model flag available)
197	    local speed_prefix=""
198	    if [ "$cli_cmd" = "agent" ]; then
199	        case "$speed" in
200	            fast)    speed_prefix="Be concise and direct. Prioritize speed.\n\n" ;;
201	            quality) speed_prefix="Take your time. Be thorough and precise.\n\n" ;;
202	        esac
203	    fi
204	
205	    # Retry loop
206	    local attempt=0
207	    local current_prompt="$prompt"
208	
209	    while [ "$attempt" -le "$max_retries" ]; do
210	        attempt=$((attempt + 1))
211	
212	        _ai_log "AI invocation: speed=$speed backend=$cli_cmd attempt=$attempt"
213	
214	        local full_prompt
215	        full_prompt=$(printf '%b%s' "$speed_prefix" "$current_prompt")
216	
217	        local output
218	        # Suppress set -e abort; CLI may exit non-zero on model errors
219	        output=$(printf '%s' "$full_prompt" | "$cli_cmd" "${flags[@]}" 2>&1) || true
220	
221	        if [ -z "$output" ]; then
222	            AI_REJECT_REASON="Empty output from $cli_cmd"
223	            _ai_log "AI invocation: speed=$speed backend=$cli_cmd attempt=$attempt result=empty" "warn"
224	            if [ "$attempt" -le "$max_retries" ]; then
225	                current_prompt=$(printf 'Your previous output was empty. Try again.\n\n%s' "$prompt")
226	                continue
227	            fi
228	            return 1
229	        fi
230	
231	        # Validate if function provided
232	        if [ -n "$validate_fn" ]; then
233	            if ! "$validate_fn" "$output"; then
234	                [ -z "$AI_REJECT_REASON" ] && AI_REJECT_REASON="Validation failed"
235	                _ai_log "AI invocation: speed=$speed backend=$cli_cmd attempt=$attempt result=rejected reason=$AI_REJECT_REASON" "warn"
236	                while IFS= read -r _rej_line; do
237	                    log_detail "ai-rejected: $_rej_line"
238	                done <<< "$output"
239	                if [ "$attempt" -le "$max_retries" ]; then
240	                    current_prompt=$(printf 'Your previous output was rejected: %s. Try again.\n\n%s' \
241	                        "$AI_REJECT_REASON" "$prompt")
242	                    continue
243	                fi
244	                _ai_log "AI invocation: speed=$speed backend=$cli_cmd exhausted after $attempt attempts" "warn"
245	                return 1
246	            fi
247	        fi
248	
249	        # Success
250	        _ai_log "AI invocation: speed=$speed backend=$cli_cmd attempt=$attempt result=accepted"
251	        printf '%s' "$output"
252	        return 0
253	    done
254	
255	    return 1
256	}
257	
258	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
259	# Summary writer (3-arg: category, tool, detail)
260	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
261	write_summary() {
262	    if [ -n "${AITOOLS_SUMMARY_FILE:-}" ]; then
263	        local cat="$1"
264	        # Auto-promote OK to WARN when warnings have been logged
265	        if [ "$cat" = "OK" ] && [ "${WARNINGS:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
266	            cat="WARN"
267	        fi
268	        printf '%s|%s|%s\n' "$cat" "$2" "$3" >> "$AITOOLS_SUMMARY_FILE"
269	    fi
270	}
271	
272	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
273	# Backup a file before overwriting. Keeps at most $max_backups copies.
274	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
275	backup_file() {
276	    local file="$1" max_backups=20
277	    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
278	    local ts
279	    ts=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H%M%SZ)
280	    cp "$file" "${file}.bak.${ts}"
281	    # Prune oldest beyond limit
282	    ls -1t "${file}.bak."* 2>/dev/null | tail -n +$((max_backups + 1)) | xargs rm -f 2>/dev/null
283	    log "Backed up $(display_path "$file")"
284	}
285	
286	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
287	# Backup a directory before modifying managed files. Keeps at most $max_backups copies.
288	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
289	backup_dir() {
290	    local dir="$1" max_backups=5
291	    [ -d "$dir" ] || return 0
292	    local file_count
293	    file_count=$(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.md' -type f | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
294	    if [ "$file_count" -eq 0 ]; then
295	        return 0
296	    fi
297	    local ts
298	    ts=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H%M%SZ)
299	    if ! cp -R "$dir" "${dir}.bak.${ts}"; then
300	        log_warn "Could not back up $(display_path "$dir") -- proceeding without backup"
301	        return 0
302	    fi
303	    local old_backups
304	    old_backups=$(find "$(dirname "$dir")" -maxdepth 1 -name "$(basename "$dir").bak.*" -type d \
305	        | sort -r | tail -n +$((max_backups + 1)))
306	    if [ -n "$old_backups" ]; then
307	        printf '%s\n' "$old_backups" | while IFS= read -r old_dir; do
308	            rm -rf "$old_dir"
309	            log "Pruned old backup: $(display_path "$old_dir")"
310	        done
311	    fi
312	    log "Backed up $(display_path "$dir") ($file_count managed files)"
313	}
314	
315	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
316	# Deploy state tracking: manifest + shadow copies for auto-deploy detection.
317	# Tracks what was last deployed to each managed file.
318	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
319	_DEPLOY_STATE_DIR="$HOME/.aitools/deploy-state"
320	_DEPLOY_MANIFEST=""
321	
322	get_content_hash() {
323	    printf '%s' "$1" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1
324	}
325	
326	_deploy_state_key() {
327	    local file_path="$1"
328	    # Normalize: strip $HOME prefix, use forward slashes
329	    printf '%s' "$file_path" | perl -pe "s{^\Q$HOME\E/}{}"
330	}
331	
332	initialize_deploy_state() {
333	    local manifest_path="$_DEPLOY_STATE_DIR/manifest.json"
334	    if [ -f "$manifest_path" ]; then
335	        _DEPLOY_MANIFEST=$(cat "$manifest_path")
336	    else
337	        _DEPLOY_MANIFEST='{"version":1,"files":{}}'
338	    fi
339	}
340	
341	get_deploy_state_hash() {
342	    local file_path="$1"
343	    if [ -z "$_DEPLOY_MANIFEST" ]; then initialize_deploy_state; fi
344	    local key
345	    key=$(_deploy_state_key "$file_path")
346	    # node is already a dependency (used by read_config_key)
347	    printf '%s' "$_DEPLOY_MANIFEST" | node -e "
348	        const m = JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/dev/stdin','utf8'));
349	        const f = m.files || {};
350	        const e = f[process.argv[1]];
351	        if (e && e.hash) process.stdout.write(e.hash);
352	    " "$key" 2>/dev/null
353	}
354	
355	update_deploy_state() {
356	    local file_path="$1"
357	    local content="$2"
358	    if [ -z "$_DEPLOY_MANIFEST" ]; then initialize_deploy_state; fi
359	    local key hash ts
360	    key=$(_deploy_state_key "$file_path")
361	    hash=$(get_content_hash "$content")
362	    ts=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
363	
364	    mkdir -p "$_DEPLOY_STATE_DIR"
365	
366	    # Update manifest via node
367	    _DEPLOY_MANIFEST=$(printf '%s' "$_DEPLOY_MANIFEST" | node -e "
368	        const m = JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/dev/stdin','utf8'));
369	        if (!m.files) m.files = {};
370	        m.files[process.argv[1]] = { hash: process.argv[2], deployedAt: process.argv[3] };
371	        process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(m, null, 2));
372	    " "$key" "$hash" "$ts" 2>/dev/null)
373	
374	    printf '%s\n' "$_DEPLOY_MANIFEST" > "$_DEPLOY_STATE_DIR/manifest.json"
375	
376	    # Write shadow copy
377	    local shadow_path="$_DEPLOY_STATE_DIR/shadows/$key"
378	    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$shadow_path")"
379	    printf '%s' "$content" > "$shadow_path"
380	}
381	
382	get_deploy_shadow() {
383	    local file_path="$1"
384	    local key
385	    key=$(_deploy_state_key "$file_path")
386	    local shadow_path="$_DEPLOY_STATE_DIR/shadows/$key"
387	    if [ -f "$shadow_path" ]; then
388	        cat "$shadow_path"
389	    fi
390	}
391	
392	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
393	# Non-agentic 3-way merge using shadow as common ancestor.
394	# Backend: git merge-file (guaranteed prerequisite -- no discovery needed).
395	# Sets AUTO_MERGED_CONTENT on clean merge. Returns 0 on success, 1 on failure.
396	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
397	AUTO_MERGED_CONTENT=""
398	try_auto_merge() {
399	    local local_content="$1"
400	    local ancestor_content="$2"
401	    local source_content="$3"
402	    AUTO_MERGED_CONTENT=""
403	
404	    local tmp_local tmp_ancestor tmp_source
405	    tmp_local=$(mktemp)
406	    tmp_ancestor=$(mktemp)
407	    tmp_source=$(mktemp)
408	    printf '%s' "$local_content" > "$tmp_local"
409	    printf '%s' "$ancestor_content" > "$tmp_ancestor"
410	    printf '%s' "$source_content" > "$tmp_source"
411	
412	    local merged
413	    # 2>/dev/null: git merge-file writes conflict markers to stderr on exit 1;
414	    # we only want stdout. Exit code checked via $rc immediately below.
415	    merged=$(git merge-file -p "$tmp_local" "$tmp_ancestor" "$tmp_source" 2>/dev/null)
416	    local rc=$?
417	    rm -f "$tmp_local" "$tmp_ancestor" "$tmp_source"
418	
419	    if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
420	        AUTO_MERGED_CONTENT="$merged"
421	        return 0
422	    fi
423	    return 1
424	}
425	
426	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
427	# Merge file description lookup
428	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
429	# Purpose: Returns a human-readable description of a managed file for AI merge
430	#   prompts, providing context about the file's role in the config system.
431	# Inputs: $1 = file path
432	# Expected output: Single-line description string on stdout.
433	_get_merge_file_description() {
434	    case "$(basename "$1")" in
435	        CLAUDE.md) printf 'User-scope CLAUDE.md -- personal preferences and instructions for Claude Code' ;;
436	        *.md)      printf 'Configuration rule: %s' "$(basename "$1")" ;;
437	        *.json)    printf 'JSON config: %s' "$(basename "$1")" ;;
438	        *)         printf 'Managed file: %s' "$(basename "$1")" ;;
439	    esac
440	}
441	
442	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
443	# AI merge prompt builder (initial merge)
444	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
445	# Purpose: Builds a structured merge prompt following the Role/Context/Task/
446	#   Constraints/Format pattern for merging managed configuration files.
447	# Inputs: $1=file_path, $2=source_content, $3=local_content, $4=diff_output
448	# Expected output: Complete prompt string on stdout, suitable for invoke_ai.
449	# Validation: validate_ai_merge_output (5 checks: conversational, fences,
450	#   refusal, truncation, header preservation)
451	# Known limitations: Very large files may hit model context limits. Files with
452	#   no markdown headers rely on Check 4 (length) for rewrite detection.
453	_ai_prompt_merge() {
454	    local file_path="$1"
455	    local source_content="$2"
456	    local local_content="$3"
457	    local diff_output="$4"
458	
459	    local file_desc
460	    file_desc=$(_get_merge_file_description "$file_path")
461	
462	    printf '%s' "You are merging a managed configuration file during automated deployment.
463	
464	## What you are merging
465	${file_desc}
466	
467	## Where changes come from
468	SOURCE: The canonical template, synced across machines -- the updated version being deployed
469	LOCAL: The user's current file on this machine, with their customizations
470	
471	## What is happening
472	Updated configuration is being deployed. Source has changed and needs to be
473	incorporated without losing local customizations.
474	
475	## Differences (unified diff: local vs source)
476	${diff_output}
477	
478	## Full local file (start from this)
479	<LOCAL>
480	${local_content}
481	</LOCAL>
482	
483	## Rules
484	1. Start with LOCAL as your base -- preserve all user customizations
485	2. Apply ONLY the changes shown in the diff
486	3. If a change conflicts with a local customization (contradicts its intent), keep local
487	4. If a change adds new content not in LOCAL, add it in the appropriate location
488	5. If a change updates content the user hasn't customized, apply it
489	6. CRITICAL: Do NOT wrap your output in markdown code fences (\`\`\`). Output raw file content ONLY
490	7. No commentary, no explanation, no preamble -- just the merged file content"
491	}
492	
493	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
494	# AI merge prompt builder (refinement)
495	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
496	# Purpose: Builds a refinement prompt for iterating on a previous merge result
497	#   based on user feedback.
498	# Inputs: $1=source_content, $2=local_content, $3=current_merge, $4=feedback
499	# Expected output: Complete prompt string on stdout, suitable for invoke_ai.
500	# Validation: Same as initial merge (validate_ai_merge_output).
501	_ai_prompt_merge_refine() {
502	    local source_content="$1"
503	    local local_content="$2"
504	    local current_merge="$3"
505	    local feedback="$4"
506	
507	    printf '%s' "You are refining a merged configuration file based on user feedback.
508	
509	## Context
510	A previous merge produced CURRENT_MERGE from SOURCE + LOCAL. The user wants changes.
511	
512	## SOURCE (original template)
513	<SOURCE>
514	${source_content}
515	</SOURCE>
516	
517	## LOCAL (original user file)
518	<LOCAL>
519	${local_content}
520	</LOCAL>
521	
522	## CURRENT MERGE (previous result)
523	<CURRENT_MERGE>
524	${current_merge}
525	</CURRENT_MERGE>
526	
527	## User Feedback
528	${feedback}
529	
530	## Rules
531	- Apply the user's feedback to CURRENT_MERGE
532	- Keep all content from CURRENT_MERGE not affected by the feedback
533	- Output the revised merged file content ONLY -- no preamble, no explanation, no markdown fences"
534	}
535	
536	# Merge validation wrapper for invoke_ai -- captures source/local context
537	# via module-level variables set by _invoke_ai_merge before calling invoke_ai.
538	_MERGE_VALIDATE_SOURCE=""
539	_MERGE_VALIDATE_LOCAL=""
540	_merge_validate() {
541	    validate_ai_merge_output "$1" "$_MERGE_VALIDATE_SOURCE" "$_MERGE_VALIDATE_LOCAL"
542	    AI_REJECT_REASON="$MERGE_REJECT_REASON"
543	}
544	
545	MERGE_REJECT_REASON=""
546	
547	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
548	# Validate AI merge output before accepting it.
549	# Returns 0 if valid, 1 if invalid. Sets MERGE_REJECT_REASON on failure.
550	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
551	validate_ai_merge_output() {
552	    local output="$1"
553	    local source_content="$2"
554	    local local_content="$3"
555	    MERGE_REJECT_REASON=""
556	
557	    # Check 1: conversational patterns (first non-empty line)
558	    local first_line
559	    first_line=$(printf '%s' "$output" | perl -ne 'if (/\S/) { print; exit }')
560	    if printf '%s' "$first_line" | perl -ne 'exit 0 if /^(I |Here|Sure|Certainly|Let me)/i; exit 1'; then
561	        MERGE_REJECT_REASON="AI responded conversationally instead of producing merged content"
562	        return 1
563	    fi
564	
565	    # Check 2: markdown code fences
566	    if printf '%s\n' "$output" | perl -ne 'exit 0 if /^```/; END { exit 1 }'; then
567	        MERGE_REJECT_REASON="AI wrapped output in code fences -- need raw content"
568	        return 1
569	    fi
570	
571	    # Check 3: conversational refusal patterns (not bare keywords -- content may
572	    # legitimately contain "permission", "access", etc.)
573	    if printf '%s' "$output" | perl -ne 'exit 0 if /(?:I don.t have permission|I cannot access|I.m not authorized|I need (?:your )?approval|permission denied|access denied|I.m unable to|I can.t (?:read|write|access|open|modify))/i; END { exit 1 }'; then
574	        MERGE_REJECT_REASON="AI indicated it couldn't perform the merge"
575	        return 1
576	    fi
577	
578	    # Check 4: minimum length (output >= 50% of shorter input when shorter > 40 chars)
579	    local out_len src_len local_len min_input_len threshold
580	    out_len=$(printf '%s' "$output" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')
581	    src_len=$(printf '%s' "$source_content" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')
582	    local_len=$(printf '%s' "$local_content" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')
583	    if [ "$src_len" -le "$local_len" ]; then min_input_len=$src_len; else min_input_len=$local_len; fi
584	    threshold=$((min_input_len / 2))
585	    if [ "$min_input_len" -gt 40 ] && [ "$out_len" -lt "$threshold" ]; then
586	        MERGE_REJECT_REASON="Output too short ($out_len chars, expected ${threshold}+) -- likely truncated"
587	        return 1
588	    fi
589	
590	    # Check 5: header preservation — deduplicated headers from source+local must
591	    # be >=60% preserved in output. Files with 0 headers pass (Check 4 handles truncation).
592	    local combined_headers
593	    combined_headers=$(printf '%s\n%s' "$source_content" "$local_content" \
594	        | grep -E '^#{1,6} ' | sort -u)
595	    local total preserved=0
596	    total=$(printf '%s\n' "$combined_headers" | grep -c '^' || true)  # count lines; may be 0
597	    if [ "$total" -gt 0 ]; then
598	        while IFS= read -r header; do
599	            [ -z "$header" ] && continue
600	            printf '%s' "$output" | grep -qF "$header" && preserved=$((preserved + 1))
601	        done <<< "$combined_headers"
602	        local threshold=$(( (total * 60 + 99) / 100 ))
603	        [ "$threshold" -lt 1 ] && threshold=1
604	        if [ "$preserved" -lt "$threshold" ]; then
605	            MERGE_REJECT_REASON="Rewrote too much ($preserved/$total section headers preserved, need 60%+)"
606	            return 1
607	        fi
608	    fi
609	
610	    return 0
611	}
612	
613	MERGED_CONTENT=""
614	
615	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
616	# Spinner for AI operations (visual progress indicator)
617	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
618	_AI_SPINNER_PID=""
619	
620	_start_spinner() {
621	    local msg="${1:-working...}"
622	    (
623	        local chars='/-\|'
624	        local i=0
625	        while true; do
626	            printf '\r  %s %s' "${chars:$((i % 4)):1}" "$msg" > /dev/tty
627	            i=$((i + 1))
628	            sleep 0.2
629	        done
630	    ) &
631	    _AI_SPINNER_PID=$!
632	}
633	
634	_stop_spinner() {
635	    if [ -n "$_AI_SPINNER_PID" ] && kill -0 "$_AI_SPINNER_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
636	        kill "$_AI_SPINNER_PID" 2>/dev/null
637	        wait "$_AI_SPINNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true  # reap; exit code irrelevant for spinner
638	    fi
639	    _AI_SPINNER_PID=""
640	    printf '\r  \033[K' > /dev/tty  # clear spinner line
641	}
642	
643	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
644	# Agentic merge via invoke_ai with refinement loop.
645	# Uses structured prompts from _ai_prompt_merge / _ai_prompt_merge_refine.
646	# Sets DIFF_REVIEW_RESULT="merge" + MERGED_CONTENT, or falls back.
647	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
648	_invoke_ai_merge() {
649	    local file_path="$1"
650	    local source_content="$2"
651	    local local_content="${3:-}"
652	    local diff_output="${4:-}"
653	
654	    # Read local from disk if not provided (backward compat)
655	    if [ -z "$local_content" ] && [ -f "$file_path" ]; then
656	        local_content=$(cat "$file_path")
657	    fi
658	
659	    # Detect backend for transparency display
660	    local ai_backend="unknown"
661	    if command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1; then
662	        ai_backend="claude"
663	    elif command -v agent >/dev/null 2>&1; then
664	        ai_backend="agent"
665	    fi
666	    local display_name
667	    display_name=$(basename "$file_path")
668	    printf '  >> AI merge: %s (balanced) -- merging %s...\n' "$ai_backend" "$display_name" > /dev/tty
669	
670	    # Set validation context for _merge_validate wrapper
671	    _MERGE_VALIDATE_SOURCE="$source_content"
672	    _MERGE_VALIDATE_LOCAL="$local_content"
673	
674	    local current_merge=""
675	    local iteration=0
676	
677	    while true; do
678	        iteration=$((iteration + 1))
679	        local prompt_text
680	
681	        if [ -z "$current_merge" ]; then
682	            prompt_text=$(_ai_prompt_merge "$file_path" "$source_content" "$local_content" "$diff_output")
683	        else
684	            local feedback
685	            printf '  refinement feedback: ' > /dev/tty
686	            IFS= read -r feedback < /dev/tty
687	            prompt_text=$(_ai_prompt_merge_refine "$source_content" "$local_content" "$current_merge" "$feedback")
688	        fi
689	
690	        local merged
691	        _start_spinner "merging $display_name (attempt $iteration)..."
692	        # invoke_ai returns 1 on failure with no stdout; || true suppresses set -e abort
693	        merged=$(printf '%s' "$prompt_text" | invoke_ai balanced none _merge_validate 1) || true
694	        _stop_spinner
695	
696	        # Defense-in-depth: strip leading/trailing code fences if AI ignored instructions
697	        if [ -n "$merged" ]; then
698	            merged=$(printf '%s' "$merged" | perl -0777 -pe 's/\A```[^\n]*\n//; s/\n```\s*\z//')
699	        fi
700	
701	        if [ -z "$merged" ]; then
702	            printf '  >> AI merge failed (iteration %d): %s\n' "$iteration" "${AI_REJECT_REASON:-unknown error}" > /dev/tty
703	            log_error "AI merge failed (iteration $iteration): ${AI_REJECT_REASON:-unknown error}"
704	            printf '  fallback [o]verwrite / [s]kip: ' > /dev/tty
705	            local fb
706	            read -r fb < /dev/tty
707	            case "$(printf '%s' "$fb" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" in
708	                s) DIFF_REVIEW_RESULT="skip" ;;
709	                *) DIFF_REVIEW_RESULT="overwrite" ;;
710	            esac
711	            return 0
712	        fi
713	
714	        # Show merge preview
715	        printf '\n  --- merged result preview (first 30 lines) ---\n' > /dev/tty
716	        printf '%s\n' "$merged" | head -30 | while IFS= read -r line; do
717	            printf '  | %s\n' "$line" > /dev/tty
718	        done
719	        local total_lines
720	        total_lines=$(printf '%s\n' "$merged" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
721	        if [ "$total_lines" -gt 30 ]; then
722	            printf '  | ... (%d more lines)\n' "$((total_lines - 30))" > /dev/tty
723	        fi
724	        printf '\n  [y]es accept / [r]efine / [n]o reject: ' > /dev/tty
725	        local accept
726	        read -r accept < /dev/tty
727	        case "$(printf '%s' "$accept" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" in
728	            y)
729	                MERGED_CONTENT="$merged"
730	                DIFF_REVIEW_RESULT="merge"
731	                printf '  >> merged: AI-merged content accepted (iteration %d)\n' "$iteration" > /dev/tty
732	                return 0
733	                ;;
734	            r)
735	                current_merge="$merged"
736	                printf '  >> refining merge (iteration %d)...\n' "$iteration" > /dev/tty
737	                continue
738	                ;;
739	            *)
740	                printf '  >> merge rejected, falling back to overwrite\n' > /dev/tty
741	                DIFF_REVIEW_RESULT="overwrite"
742	                return 0
743	                ;;
744	        esac
745	    done
746	}
747	
748	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
749	# Prompt user before overwriting a managed file with different content.
750	# Shows diff, attempts diff3 auto-merge, offers interactive options.
751	#
752	# Args:
753	#   $1 = file path (deployed file on disk)
754	#   $2 = new content that would be written (from source template)
755	#   $3 = adopt target label (e.g., "profile", "shared/") or "" to hide adopt
756	#   $4 = current content of local file (optional, read from disk if empty)
757	#   $5 = ancestor content from shadow (optional, enables diff3 merge)
758	#
759	# Sets global DIFF_REVIEW_RESULT to: "overwrite", "adopt", "merge", or "skip"
760	# When "merge": also sets MERGED_CONTENT with the merged result.
761	# Exits with code 2 on abort.
762	# Non-interactive / --force: sets "overwrite" and returns.
763	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
764	DIFF_REVIEW_RESULT=""
765	prompt_diff_review() {
766	    local file_path="$1"
767	    local new_content="$2"
768	    local adopt_label="${3:-}"
769	    local cur_content="${4:-}"
770	    local ancestor_content="${5:-}"
771	
772	    DIFF_REVIEW_RESULT="overwrite"
773	    MERGED_CONTENT=""
774	
775	    # --force or AITOOLS_FORCE: auto-overwrite
776	    if [ "${AITOOLS_FORCE:-}" = "1" ] || [ "${FORCE:-}" = "true" ]; then
777	        log_warn "Diff in $(display_path "$file_path") -- overwriting (--force)"
778	        return 0
779	    fi
780	
781	    # Non-interactive: auto-overwrite
782	    if ! (printf '' > /dev/tty) 2>/dev/null; then
783	        log_warn "Diff in $(display_path "$file_path") -- overwriting (non-interactive)"
784	        return 0
785	    fi
786	
787	    # Read current file if not provided
788	    if [ -z "$cur_content" ] && [ -f "$file_path" ]; then
789	        cur_content=$(cat "$file_path")
790	    fi
791	
792	    # Context header
793	    printf '\n\033[33m[REVIEW]\033[0m %s differs from source.\n' \
794	        "$(display_path "$file_path")" > /dev/tty
795	    printf '  source = template (would deploy)\n' > /dev/tty
796	    printf '  local  = current file on disk\n\n' > /dev/tty
797	
798	    # Show diff
799	    local diff_output
800	    # diff exits 1 on differences (expected), suppress set -e abort
801	    diff_output=$(diff -u <(printf '%s' "$new_content") <(printf '%s' "$cur_content") \
802	        --label "source (would deploy)" --label "local (on disk)" 2>&1) || true
803	    local diff_lines
804	    diff_lines=$(printf '%s\n' "$diff_output" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
805	    if [ "$diff_lines" -le 40 ]; then
806	        printf '%s\n' "$diff_output" > /dev/tty
807	    else
808	        printf '%s\n' "$diff_output" | head -30 > /dev/tty
809	        printf '  ... (%d more lines -- full diff in deploy log)\n' \
810	            "$((diff_lines - 30))" > /dev/tty
811	        printf '%s\n' "$diff_output" >> "${LOG_FILE:-/dev/null}"
812	    fi
813	
814	    # Attempt automatic merge if ancestor available
815	    if [ -n "$ancestor_content" ]; then
816	        printf '\n  Attempting automatic merge...\n' > /dev/tty
817	        if try_auto_merge "$cur_content" "$ancestor_content" "$new_content"; then
818	            printf '  Clean merge -- no conflicts.\n\n' > /dev/tty
819	            local total_m_lines preview_count
820	            total_m_lines=$(printf '%s\n' "$AUTO_MERGED_CONTENT" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
821	            preview_count=$total_m_lines
822	            if [ "$preview_count" -gt 30 ]; then preview_count=30; fi
823	            printf '  --- merged result preview (first %d lines) ---\n' "$preview_count" > /dev/tty
824	            printf '%s\n' "$AUTO_MERGED_CONTENT" | head -"$preview_count" | while IFS= read -r line; do
825	                printf '  | %s\n' "$line" > /dev/tty
826	            done
827	            if [ "$total_m_lines" -gt 30 ]; then
828	                printf '  | ... (%d more lines)\n' "$((total_m_lines - 30))" > /dev/tty
829	            fi
830	            printf '\n' > /dev/tty
831	            if [ -n "$adopt_label" ]; then
832	                printf '  [a]ccept    : deploy merge + update %s\n' "$adopt_label" > /dev/tty
833	            else
834	                printf '  [a]ccept\n' > /dev/tty
835	            fi
836	            printf '  [o]verwrite\n' > /dev/tty
837	            printf '  [s]kip\n' > /dev/tty
838	            printf '  [x]abort\n' > /dev/tty
839	            printf '  choice [a/o/s/x]: ' > /dev/tty
840	            local merge_choice
841	            read -r merge_choice < /dev/tty
842	            case "$(printf '%s' "$merge_choice" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" in
843	                a)  MERGED_CONTENT="$AUTO_MERGED_CONTENT"
844	                    if [ -n "$adopt_label" ]; then
845	                        printf '  >> accepted: merge deployed + %s updated\n' "$adopt_label" > /dev/tty
846	                        DIFF_REVIEW_RESULT="merge-adopt"
847	                    else
848	                        printf '  >> accepted: merge deployed\n' > /dev/tty
849	                        DIFF_REVIEW_RESULT="merge"
850	                    fi
851	                    return 0 ;;
852	                s)  printf '  >> skipped: local file unchanged\n' > /dev/tty
853	                    DIFF_REVIEW_RESULT="skip"
854	                    return 0 ;;
855	                x)  log_error "Aborted by user"
856	                    exit 2 ;;
857	                *)  printf '  >> overwritten: source deployed to local (backup kept)\n' > /dev/tty
858	                    DIFF_REVIEW_RESULT="overwrite"
859	                    return 0 ;;
860	            esac
861	        else
862	            printf '  Merge has conflicts -- manual choice required.\n' > /dev/tty
863	        fi
864	    fi
865	
866	    # Options (no auto-merge or merge had conflicts)
867	    printf '\n' > /dev/tty
868	    if [ -n "$adopt_label" ]; then
869	        printf '  [o]verwrite : source wins -> deploy to local (backup kept)\n' > /dev/tty
870	        printf '  [a]dopt     : local wins -> copy back to %s\n' "$adopt_label" > /dev/tty
871	        printf '  [m]erge     : AI-assisted merge of source + local\n' > /dev/tty
872	        printf '  [s]kip      : keep local as-is (no changes)\n' > /dev/tty
873	        printf '  [x]abort    : stop deployment\n' > /dev/tty
874	        printf '  choice [o/a/m/s/x]: ' > /dev/tty
875	    else
876	        printf '  [o]verwrite : source wins -> deploy to local (backup kept)\n' > /dev/tty
877	        printf '  [m]erge     : AI-assisted merge of source + local\n' > /dev/tty
878	        printf '  [s]kip      : keep local as-is (no changes)\n' > /dev/tty
879	        printf '  [x]abort    : stop deployment\n' > /dev/tty
880	        printf '  choice [o/m/s/x]: ' > /dev/tty
881	    fi
882	
883	    local choice
884	    read -r choice < /dev/tty
885	    case "$(printf '%s' "$choice" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')" in
886	        a)  if [ -n "$adopt_label" ]; then
887	                printf '  >> adopted: local version copied back to %s\n' "$adopt_label" > /dev/tty
888	                DIFF_REVIEW_RESULT="adopt"
889	            else
890	                printf '  >> overwritten: source deployed to local (backup kept)\n' > /dev/tty
891	                DIFF_REVIEW_RESULT="overwrite"
892	            fi ;;
893	        m)  _invoke_ai_merge "$file_path" "$new_content" "$cur_content" "$diff_output" ;;
894	        s)  printf '  >> skipped: local file unchanged\n' > /dev/tty
895	            DIFF_REVIEW_RESULT="skip" ;;
896	        x)  log_error "Aborted by user"
897	            exit 2 ;;
898	        *)  printf '  >> overwritten: source deployed to local (backup kept)\n' > /dev/tty
899	            DIFF_REVIEW_RESULT="overwrite" ;;
900	    esac
901	    return 0
902	}
903	
904	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
905	# Deploy a managed file with diff review and deploy state tracking.
906	# Uses manifest to auto-deploy when user hasn't edited the local file.
907	# Falls back to interactive review with merge options when both sides differ.
908	#
909	# Args:
910	#   $1 = source content (string to deploy)
911	#   $2 = dest file path (deployed location)
912	#   $3 = tool name (for summary, e.g., "claude rules")
913	#   $4 = item name (for DETAIL summary, e.g., "concurrent-agents.md")
914	#   $5 = adopt label ("profile", "shared/", or "" to hide adopt option)
915	#
916	# Sets MANAGED_FILE_RESULT to: "created", "updated", "verified", "accept & adopt", "skipped"
917	# Exits with code 2 on abort (from prompt_diff_review).
918	# On "accept & adopt"/"skipped": does NOT write the file (caller decides).
919	# On "created"/"updated": writes src_content to dest + updates deploy state.
920	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
921	MANAGED_FILE_RESULT=""
922	deploy_managed_file() {
923	    local src_content="$1"
924	    local dest="$2"
925	    local tool_name="$3"
926	    local item_name="$4"
927	    local adopt_label="${5:-}"
928	
929	    # Normalize trailing whitespace for consistent comparison.
930	    # Prevents round-trip diff noise (deploy -> adopt strips trailing blanks -> deploy sees diff).
931	    src_content=$(printf '%s' "$src_content" | perl -0777 -pe 's/[\r\n]+$/\n/')
932	
933	    MANAGED_FILE_RESULT="verified"
934	
935	    # Dry run: report what would happen without writing
936	    if [ "${DRY_RUN:-}" = "true" ]; then
937	        if [ -f "$dest" ]; then
938	            local _dr_existing
939	            _dr_existing=$(cat "$dest")
940	            _dr_existing=$(printf '%s' "$_dr_existing" | perl -0777 -pe 's/[\r\n]+$/\n/')
941	            if [ "$_dr_existing" = "$src_content" ]; then
942	                log "[DRY RUN] Unchanged: $item_name"
943	            else
944	                log "[DRY RUN] Would update: $item_name -> $(display_path "$dest")"
945	            fi
946	        else
947	            log "[DRY RUN] Would create: $item_name -> $(display_path "$dest")"
948	        fi
949	        return 0
950	    fi
951	
952	    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
953	
954	    if [ -f "$dest" ]; then
955	        local existing
956	        existing=$(cat "$dest")
957	        existing=$(printf '%s' "$existing" | perl -0777 -pe 's/[\r\n]+$/\n/')
958	        if [ "$existing" = "$src_content" ]; then
959	            # Content identical — update deploy state (bootstraps manifest)
960	            update_deploy_state "$dest" "$src_content"
961	            MANAGED_FILE_RESULT="verified"
962	            return 0
963	        fi
964	
965	        # Content differs — check deploy state for auto-deploy eligibility
966	        local state_hash existing_hash
967	        state_hash=$(get_deploy_state_hash "$dest")
968	        if [ -n "$state_hash" ]; then
969	            existing_hash=$(get_content_hash "$existing")
970	            if [ "$existing_hash" = "$state_hash" ]; then
971	                # User didn't edit since last deploy → auto-deploy silently
972	                backup_file "$dest"
973	                printf '%s\n' "$src_content" > "$dest"
974	                update_deploy_state "$dest" "$src_content"
975	                log "Auto-deployed: $item_name (no local edits detected)"
976	                MANAGED_FILE_RESULT="updated"
977	                return 0
978	            fi
979	        fi
980	
981	        # User edited AND source changed — backup + interactive review
982	        backup_file "$dest"
983	        local ancestor_content
984	        ancestor_content=$(get_deploy_shadow "$dest")
985	        # Bootstrap: seed shadow from current deployed content if empty
986	        if [ -z "$ancestor_content" ]; then
987	            log "Bootstrapping deploy shadow from existing: $(display_path "$dest")"
988	            ancestor_content="$existing"
989	        fi
990	        prompt_diff_review "$dest" "$src_content" "$adopt_label" "$existing" "$ancestor_content"
991	        case "$DIFF_REVIEW_RESULT" in
992	            adopt)
993	                MANAGED_FILE_RESULT="accept & adopt"
994	                return 0
995	                ;;
996	            skip)
997	                log_warn "Skipped: $item_name"
998	                MANAGED_FILE_RESULT="skipped"
999	                return 0
1000	                ;;
1001	            merge-adopt)
1002	                src_content="$MERGED_CONTENT"
1003	                printf '%s' "$src_content" > "$dest"
1004	                update_deploy_state "$dest" "$src_content"
1005	                log_ok "Updated (merge-adopt): $item_name"
1006	                MANAGED_FILE_RESULT="accept & adopt"
1007	                return 0
1008	                ;;
1009	            merge)
1010	                src_content="$MERGED_CONTENT"
1011	                ;;
1012	        esac
1013	        # overwrite or merge: write content to dest
1014	        printf '%s\n' "$src_content" > "$dest"
1015	        update_deploy_state "$dest" "$src_content"
1016	        MANAGED_FILE_RESULT="updated"
1017	        log_ok "Updated: $item_name -> $(display_path "$dest")"
1018	    else
1019	        # New file — create
1020	        printf '%s\n' "$src_content" > "$dest"
1021	        update_deploy_state "$dest" "$src_content"
1022	        MANAGED_FILE_RESULT="created"
1023	        log_ok "Created: $item_name -> $(display_path "$dest")"
1024	    fi
1025	}

1027	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1028	# Deploy tracker: centralizes outcome counting and summary writing for
1029	# loops that deploy multiple managed files (rules, skills, hooks).
1030	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1031	
1032	# Reset all deploy tracker counters. Call before a deploy loop.
1033	_DT_ADDED=0; _DT_UPDATED=0; _DT_VERIFIED=0
1034	_DT_ACCEPTED=0; _DT_SKIPPED=0; _DT_PRESERVED=0
1035	DEPLOY_TRACKER_TEXT=""
1036	
1037	deploy_tracker_init() {
1038	    _DT_ADDED=0; _DT_UPDATED=0; _DT_VERIFIED=0
1039	    _DT_ACCEPTED=0; _DT_SKIPPED=0; _DT_PRESERVED=0
1040	    DEPLOY_TRACKER_TEXT=""
1041	}
1042	
1043	# Record a single file outcome. Increments counter and writes DETAIL summary.
1044	# Args: $1=outcome $2=tool_name $3=item_name
1045	deploy_tracker_record() {
1046	    local outcome="$1" tool_name="$2" item_name="$3"
1047	    case "$outcome" in
1048	        added|created) _DT_ADDED=$((_DT_ADDED + 1))
1049	                   write_summary DETAIL "$tool_name" "added: $item_name" ;;
1050	        updated)   _DT_UPDATED=$((_DT_UPDATED + 1))
1051	                   write_summary DETAIL "$tool_name" "updated: $item_name" ;;
1052	        "accept & adopt") _DT_ACCEPTED=$((_DT_ACCEPTED + 1))
1053	                       write_summary DETAIL "$tool_name" "accept & adopt: $item_name" ;;
1054	        skipped)   _DT_SKIPPED=$((_DT_SKIPPED + 1))
1055	                   write_summary DETAIL "$tool_name" "skipped: $item_name" ;;
1056	        verified)  _DT_VERIFIED=$((_DT_VERIFIED + 1)) ;;
1057	        preserved) _DT_PRESERVED=$((_DT_PRESERVED + 1)) ;;
1058	    esac
1059	}
1060	
1061	# Write aggregate summary for a deploy loop. Uses non-zero counts.
1062	# Sets DEPLOY_TRACKER_TEXT for use in log lines.
1063	# Args: $1=tool_name
1064	deploy_tracker_summary() {
1065	    local tool_name="$1"
1066	    local parts=""
1067	    [ "$_DT_ADDED" -gt 0 ]     && parts="$_DT_ADDED added"
1068	    [ "$_DT_UPDATED" -gt 0 ]   && parts="${parts:+$parts, }$_DT_UPDATED updated"
1069	    [ "$_DT_ACCEPTED" -gt 0 ]  && parts="${parts:+$parts, }$_DT_ACCEPTED accepted"
1070	    [ "$_DT_VERIFIED" -gt 0 ]  && parts="${parts:+$parts, }$_DT_VERIFIED verified"
1071	    [ -z "$parts" ] && parts="verified"
1072	    DEPLOY_TRACKER_TEXT="$parts"
1073	
1074	    if [ "$_DT_SKIPPED" -gt 0 ]; then
1075	        write_summary WARN "$tool_name" "$_DT_SKIPPED skipped (user review)"
1076	    else
1077	        write_summary OK "$tool_name" "$parts"
1078	    fi
1079	}

1081	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1082	# Repair broken uv tool environment (cross-platform)
1083	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1084	# When `uv tool upgrade <tool>` fails with "missing a valid environment",
1085	# find a working Python via `uv python find` (fallback: system python/python3)
1086	# and reinstall with --force --python <path>.
1087	# Returns 0 if repaired, 1 if not applicable or failed.
1088	repair_uv_tool_env() {
1089	    local tool_name="$1"
1090	    local upgrade_output="${2:-}"
1091	
1092	    if ! printf '%s\n' "$upgrade_output" | grep -q 'missing a valid environment'; then
1093	        return 1
1094	    fi
1095	
1096	    log_warn "$tool_name uv environment is broken (Python removed?) -- repairing..."
1097	
1098	    # Find a working Python -- uv's own Pythons first, then system
1099	    local working_python=""
1100	    local uv_python
1101	    uv_python=$(uv python find 2>/dev/null) || true
1102	    if [ -n "$uv_python" ] && [ -x "$uv_python" ]; then
1103	        working_python="$uv_python"
1104	    elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
1105	        working_python=$(command -v python3)
1106	    elif command -v python >/dev/null 2>&1; then
1107	        working_python=$(command -v python)
1108	    fi
1109	
1110	    if [ -z "$working_python" ]; then
1111	        log_error "Cannot repair $tool_name -- no working Python found"
1112	        return 1
1113	    fi
1114	
1115	    log "Repairing with: uv tool install --force --python $working_python $tool_name"
1116	    local repair_output
1117	    repair_output=$(uv tool install --force --python "$working_python" "$tool_name" 2>&1) || true
1118	    printf '%s\n' "$repair_output" | while IFS= read -r line; do
1119	        [ -n "$line" ] && log "$line"
1120	    done
1121	
1122	    if printf '%s\n' "$repair_output" | grep -qi 'error.*failed'; then
1123	        log_error "$tool_name environment repair failed"
1124	        return 1
1125	    fi
1126	
1127	    log_ok "Repaired $tool_name uv environment"
1128	    return 0
1129	}

1131	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1132	# Parse CHANGED: lines from a node merge result and emit DETAIL summary entries.
1133	# Usage: emit_merge_details "$MERGE_RESULT" "tool_name"
1134	# Only processes lines prefixed with "CHANGED: " -- ignores status and other output.
1135	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1136	emit_merge_details() {
1137	    local merge_result="$1" tool_name="$2"
1138	    local changed_keys
1139	    changed_keys=$(echo "$merge_result" | perl -ne 'print if s/^CHANGED: //')
1140	    if [ -n "$changed_keys" ]; then
1141	        while IFS= read -r key_change; do
1142	            log "  $key_change"
1143	            write_summary DETAIL "$tool_name" "$key_change"
1144	        done <<< "$changed_keys"
1145	    fi
1146	}

1148	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1149	# JSON normalization for comparison (sorted keys, deterministic output)
1150	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1151	# JavaScript JSON.stringify preserves insertion order, which may differ
1152	# between runs or between PS1/bash variants writing the same file. Sorting
1153	# keys before comparison ensures identical content produces identical JSON.
1154	#
1155	# SORT_KEYS_JS: minified sortKeys function for embedding in node -e blocks.
1156	#   Usage: node -e "$SORT_KEYS_JS; ..."
1157	#
1158	# normalize_json: pipe-based wrapper for standalone use.
1159	#   Usage: NORMALIZED=$(echo "$json_string" | normalize_json)
1160	SORT_KEYS_JS='function sortKeys(o){if(o===null||typeof o!=="object")return o;if(Array.isArray(o))return o.map(sortKeys);var s={};Object.keys(o).sort().forEach(function(k){s[k]=sortKeys(o[k])});return s}'
1161	
1162	normalize_json() {
1163	    node -e "
1164	        var input = require('fs').readFileSync('/dev/stdin', 'utf8');
1165	        $SORT_KEYS_JS
1166	        try {
1167	            console.log(JSON.stringify(sortKeys(JSON.parse(input)), null, 2));
1168	        } catch(e) {
1169	            process.stderr.write('normalize_json: ' + e.message + '\n');
1170	            process.exit(1);
1171	        }
1172	    "
1173	}

1175	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1176	# Go install provenance detection (macOS)
1177	# Returns: "homebrew", "pkg-installer", "goenv", "manual", "none", or "unknown"
1178	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1179	detect_go_provenance() {
1180	    local go_path
1181	    go_path=$(command -v go 2>/dev/null) || { echo "none"; return; }
1182	    case "$go_path" in
1183	        /opt/homebrew/*/go|/usr/local/Cellar/*/go)
1184	            echo "homebrew" ;;
1185	        /usr/local/go/bin/go)
1186	            # Check if installed via macOS .pkg installer (pkgutil) or manual tarball
1187	            if pkgutil --pkg-info=org.golang.go >/dev/null 2>&1; then
1188	                echo "pkg-installer"
1189	            else
1190	                echo "manual"
1191	            fi ;;
1192	        */.goenv/*)
1193	            echo "goenv" ;;
1194	        *)
1195	            echo "unknown" ;;
1196	    esac
1197	}

1200	# Ensure GOPATH/bin is on PATH for current session
1201	# Returns 0 if already on PATH, 1 if added (caller should warn re persistence)
1202	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1203	ensure_gopath_bin_on_path() {
1204	    local gopath_bin="${GOPATH:-$HOME/go}/bin"
1205	    case ":$PATH:" in
1206	        *":$gopath_bin:"*) return 0 ;;
1207	    esac

1210	}

1212	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1213	# Summary panel renderer
1214	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1215	# Reads AITOOLS_SUMMARY_FILE, displays colored panel, cleans up.
1216	# Silent no-op if file unset, missing, or empty.
1217	show_summary() {
1218	    local sfile="${AITOOLS_SUMMARY_FILE:-}"
1219	    [ -n "$sfile" ] || return 0
1220	    [ -f "$sfile" ] || return 0
1221	    [ -s "$sfile" ] || { rm -f "$sfile"; return 0; }
1222	
1223	    # Dedup by tool name: highest severity wins (ERROR > WARN > OK).
1224	    # ACTIONs (empty tool name) are never deduped. DETAIL lines collected separately.
1225	    # Output is pre-sorted: OK+details, WARN+details, ERROR+details, ACTIONs.
1226	    local deduped
1227	    deduped=$(perl -F'\|' -lane '
1228	        BEGIN { %rank = (OK => 1, WARN => 2, ERROR => 3); }
1229	        $cat = $F[0]; $tool = $F[1]; $det = join("|", @F[2..$#F]);
1230	        if ($cat eq "DETAIL") {
1231	            push @{$details{$tool}}, $det; next;
1232	        }
1233	        if ($cat eq "ACTION" || $tool eq "") {
1234	            push @actions, $_; next;
1235	        }
1236	        $r = $rank{$cat} // 0;
1237	        if (!exists $best{$tool}) {
1238	            push @order, $tool;
1239	            $best{$tool} = $cat; $detail{$tool} = $det;
1240	        } elsif ($r > ($rank{$best{$tool}} // 0)) {
1241	            $best{$tool} = $cat; $detail{$tool} = $det;
1242	        }
1243	        END {
1244	            my (@ok, @warn, @err);
1245	            for my $t (@order) {
1246	                my @g = ("$best{$t}|$t|$detail{$t}",
1247	                         map { "DETAIL|$t|$_" } @{$details{$t} // []});
1248	                if    ($best{$t} eq "OK")    { push @ok,   @g }
1249	                elsif ($best{$t} eq "WARN")  { push @warn, @g }
1250	                elsif ($best{$t} eq "ERROR") { push @err,  @g }
1251	            }
1252	            print for @ok, @warn, @err, @actions;
1253	        }
1254	    ' "$sfile")
1255	
1256	    # Single-pass display: Perl output is pre-sorted by severity.
1257	    # DETAIL lines inherit the color of their preceding parent entry.
1258	    echo ""
1259	    echo "────────────────────────────────────────────────────────"
1260	    local last_color="" first_action=true
1261	    while IFS='|' read -r cat tool detail; do
1262	        case "$cat" in
1263	            OK)
1264	                last_color='\033[32m'
1265	                printf '\033[32m  [ok]  %-16s %s\033[0m\n' "$tool" "$detail"
1266	                ;;
1267	            WARN)
1268	                last_color='\033[33m'
1269	                printf '\033[33m  [!]   %-16s %s\033[0m\n' "$tool" "$detail"
1270	                ;;
1271	            ERROR)
1272	                last_color='\033[31m'
1273	                printf '\033[31m  [ERR] %-16s %s\033[0m\n' "$tool" "$detail"
1274	                ;;
1275	            DETAIL)
1276	                printf '%b                          %s\033[0m\n' "$last_color" "$detail"
1277	                ;;
1278	            ACTION)
1279	                if [ "$first_action" = true ]; then
1280	                    echo ""
1281	                    printf '\033[1;35m  ACTION REQUIRED -- run before tools are ready:\033[0m\n'
1282	                    first_action=false
1283	                fi
1284	                printf '\033[1;35m  >>  %s\033[0m\n' "$detail"
1285	                ;;
1286	        esac
1287	    done <<< "$deduped"
1288	    echo "────────────────────────────────────────────────────────"
1289	
1290	    # Preserve summary for log compliance checks
1291	    if [ "${AITOOLS_PRESERVE_SUMMARY:-}" = "1" ]; then
1292	        # cp may fail if log dir was cleaned up; non-blocking (summary already displayed)
1293	        if ! cp "$sfile" "$LOG_DIR/last-summary.txt" 2>/dev/null; then
1294	            printf 'warning: could not preserve summary file\n' >&2
1295	        fi
1296	    fi
1297	    # Cleanup summary file (already displayed; rm -f ignores nonexistent files)
1298	    rm -f "$sfile"
1299	}

1302	# Build prerequisite checking
1303	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1304	
1305	# ensure_tool_on_path: Verify a tool is findable after installation.
1306	# Tries: 1) command -v (current PATH), 2) hash -r (cache refresh),
1307	# 3) known paths fallback (filesystem check + session PATH update).
1308	# Usage: ensure_tool_on_path "nasm" "/usr/local/bin/nasm" "/opt/homebrew/bin/nasm"
1309	# Returns 0 if tool is now on PATH, 1 otherwise.
1310	ensure_tool_on_path() {
1311	    local tool_name="$1"
1312	    shift
1313	    local known_paths=("$@")
1314	
1315	    # Already on PATH?
1316	    if command -v "$tool_name" >/dev/null 2>&1; then return 0; fi
1317	
1318	    # Refresh command cache (picks up tools installed earlier in the same session)
1319	    hash -r 2>/dev/null  # expected to succeed; some shells don't support it
1320	    if command -v "$tool_name" >/dev/null 2>&1; then return 0; fi
1321	
1322	    # Fallback: check known install locations on disk
1323	    for kp in "${known_paths[@]}"; do
1324	        if [ -x "$kp" ]; then
1325	            local parent_dir
1326	            parent_dir=$(dirname "$kp")
1327	            export PATH="$parent_dir:$PATH"
1328	            log "$tool_name found at $kp (added to session PATH)"
1329	            return 0
1330	        fi
1331	    done
1332	    return 1
1333	}
1334	
1335	# Check known build prerequisites for an ecosystem.
1336	# Usage: check_build_prereqs "cargo"
1337	#   Outputs missing prereq info to stdout (one per line: NAME|INSTALL_INSTRUCTION).
1338	#   Returns 0 if all present, 1 if any missing.
1339	check_build_prereqs() {
1340	    local ecosystem="$1"
1341	    local missing=0
1342	
1343	    # Refresh shell command cache (picks up tools installed earlier in the same session)
1344	    hash -r 2>/dev/null  # expected to succeed; some shells don't support it
1345	
1346	    case "$ecosystem" in
1347	        cargo)
1348	            # NASM -- required by aws-lc-sys on x86_64
1349	            if [ "$(uname -m)" = "x86_64" ] && ! command -v nasm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
1350	                # Fallback: check known install locations
1351	                if ensure_tool_on_path "nasm" /usr/local/bin/nasm /opt/homebrew/bin/nasm /usr/bin/nasm; then
1352	                    : # Found via fallback -- ensure_tool_on_path already added to PATH
1353	                else
1354	                    echo "NASM|brew install nasm (macOS) or apt-get install nasm (Linux)"
1355	                    missing=1
1356	                fi
1357	            fi
1358	            # cmake -- required by some crates
1359	            # Official: cmake.org/download lists pip, ZIP, MSI (not winget)
1360	            # macOS: brew install cmake (user-level, no sudo)
1361	            # Windows: uv tool install cmake (user-level, see reference/tool-evaluation-playbook.md)
1362	            if ! command -v cmake >/dev/null 2>&1; then
1363	                if ensure_tool_on_path "cmake" /usr/local/bin/cmake /opt/homebrew/bin/cmake /usr/bin/cmake /Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake; then
1364	                    : # Found via fallback
1365	                else
1366	                    echo "CMake|brew install cmake (macOS) / uv tool install cmake (Windows) -- see cmake.org/download"
1367	                    missing=1
1368	                fi
1369	            fi
1370	            ;;
1371	        pip)
1372	            # Add pip-specific prereqs here as discovered
1373	            ;;
1374	        go)
1375	            # Add go-specific prereqs here as discovered
1376	            ;;
1377	    esac
1378	
1379	    return $missing
1380	}

1382	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1383	# Build failure diagnosis
1384	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1385	
1386	# Scan build output for known failure signatures.
1387	# Usage: diagnose_build_failure "$output"
1388	#   Prints "NAME|REMEDY" if a known signature is found.
1389	#   Returns 0 if found, 1 if no match.
1390	diagnose_build_failure() {
1391	    local output="$1"
1392	
1393	    # Table of known failure patterns -> remediation
1394	    # Add new entries here when new build failures are discovered.
1395	    local -a patterns=(
1396	        "NASM command not found|NASM|brew install nasm / apt-get install nasm"
1397	        "linker.*not found|Linker|Install build-essential (Linux) or Xcode CLI tools (macOS)"
1398	        "cmake.*not found|CMake|brew install cmake / uv tool install cmake (see cmake.org/download)"
1399	        "pkg-config.*not found|pkg-config|brew install pkg-config / apt-get install pkg-config"
1400	        "Python\.h.*not found|Python headers|Install python3-dev or python3-devel"
1401	        "openssl.*not found|OpenSSL|brew install openssl / apt-get install libssl-dev"
1402	    )
1403	
1404	    for entry in "${patterns[@]}"; do
1405	        local pattern="${entry%%|*}"
1406	        local rest="${entry#*|}"
1407	        if printf '%s\n' "$output" | grep -qiE "$pattern"; then
1408	            echo "$rest"
1409	            return 0
1410	        fi
1411	    done
1412	    return 1
1413	}

3	#
4	# Output goes to deploy/ only. There is no separate build/ directory in this repo;

13	# during `aitools` / `aitools install` (see scripts/aitools deploy_configs).
14	#
15	# Usage: bash scripts/build-deploy.sh   (run from repo root)
16	#
17	# CROSS-PLATFORM NOTE: This script is intentionally bash-only (no .ps1 variant).
18	# It's a build step that produces platform-independent output (both .sh and .ps1
19	# deploy scripts). The result is committed to git, so both platforms get identical
20	# deploy/ contents. A parallel PS1 would double maintenance for no output difference.

112	# inline_lib_bash: replaces `source.*aitools-lib.sh` line with lib content (stdin -> stdout)
113	# Uses perl for performance (single process vs ~2 subprocesses per line with while-read)
114	inline_lib_bash() {
115	    perl -e '
116	        open my $lib, "<", $ARGV[0] or die "Cannot open lib: $!";
117	        my $content = do { local $/; <$lib> };
118	        close $lib;
119	        while (<STDIN>) {
120	            if (/source.*aitools-lib\.sh/) {
121	                print $content;
122	            } else {
123	                print;
124	            }
125	        }
126	    ' "$SCRIPTS_DIR/aitools-lib.sh"

218	    let prof, ident;

253	    console.log('CLAUDE_EFFORT_LEVEL=' + JSON.stringify(claudePrefs.effortLevel || ''));

278	# ============================================================
279	# Sentinel-based extraction helper (Perl)
280	# ============================================================
281	# Extracts lines between two sentinel markers (exclusive of markers themselves).
282	# Uses Perl flip-flop operator for clean range extraction.
283	# Usage: extract_between FILE START_REGEX END_REGEX [--crlf]
284	#   --crlf: convert LF output to CRLF (for PS1 deploy scripts)
285	extract_between() {
286	    local file="$1" start="$2" end="$3" crlf="${4:-}"
287	    local result
288	    # Use m!...! as Perl regex delimiter to avoid conflicts with / in sentinels
289	    if [ "$crlf" = "--crlf" ]; then
290	        result=$(perl -ne '
291	            s/\r\n?$/\n/;
292	            if (m!'"$start"'! .. m!'"$end"'!) {
293	                next if m!'"$start"'! || m!'"$end"'!;
294	                s/\n$/\r\n/; print;
295	            }' "$file")
296	    else
297	        result=$(perl -ne '
298	            if (m!'"$start"'! .. m!'"$end"'!) {
299	                print unless m!'"$start"'! || m!'"$end"'!;
300	            }' "$file")
301	    fi
302	    if [ -z "$result" ]; then
303	        blog_error "Extraction failed: sentinels not found in $(basename "$file") (start: $start, end: $end)"
304	        exit 1
305	    fi
306	    printf '%s\n' "$result"
307	}

312	blog "Generating deploy/setup-user-claude.sh"
313	
314	{
315	    echo '#!/usr/bin/env bash'
316	    echo "$HEADER_COMMENT_BASH"
317	    cat <<'BLOCK'
318	# setup-user-claude.sh — Creates user-level ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and deploys user rules
319	# Self-contained: shared preferences and user rules are embedded below. No repo needed.
320	# Safe to re-run — replaces existing file with latest version.
321	#
322	# Managed: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (sole owner, overwrite)
323	# Managed: ~/.claude/rules/*.md (additive deploy from embedded rules)
324	# Preserved: ~/.claude/rules/ files not in embedded source
325	
326	set -euo pipefail
327	
328	BLOCK
329	    extract_between "$SCRIPTS_DIR/setup-user-claude.sh" \
330	        '^# --- BEGIN preamble' '^# --- END preamble'
331	    cat <<'BLOCK'
332	
333	# --- Auto-detect machine info ---
334	OS_NAME=$(uname -s)
335	ARCH=$(uname -m)
336	HOSTNAME=$(hostname -s 2>/dev/null || hostname)
337	SHELL_NAME=$(basename "${SHELL:-/bin/bash}")
338	
339	CLAUDE_DIR="$HOME/.claude"
340	CLAUDE_MD="$CLAUDE_DIR/CLAUDE.md"
341	
342	mkdir -p "$CLAUDE_DIR"
343	log "Ensuring $CLAUDE_DIR exists"
344	
345	# --- Embedded shared preferences (from shared/claude-shared.md) ---
346	BLOCK
347	    echo 'read -r -d "" SHARED_CONTENT <<'"'"'__EMBEDDED_CLAUDE_SHARED__'"'"' || true'
348	    echo "$CLAUDE_SHARED_CONTENT"
349	    echo '__EMBEDDED_CLAUDE_SHARED__'
350	    cat <<'BLOCK'
351	
352	# --- Build content ---
353	NEW_CONTENT="${SHARED_CONTENT}
354	
355	## Machine-Specific
356	
357	- Machine: ${OS_NAME} ${ARCH} (${HOSTNAME})
358	- Shell: ${SHELL_NAME}"
359	
360	if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "true" ]; then
361	    EXISTING_LINES=0
362	    [ -f "$CLAUDE_MD" ] && EXISTING_LINES=$(wc -l < "$CLAUDE_MD")
363	    NEW_LINES=$(echo "$NEW_CONTENT" | wc -l)
364	    log "[DRY RUN] $CLAUDE_MD: overwrite (sole owner)"
365	    log "  Template source: embedded (build-time)"
366	    log "  Existing: ${EXISTING_LINES} lines"
367	    log "  New: ${NEW_LINES} lines"
368	    if [ -f "$CLAUDE_MD" ]; then
369	        if [ "$(cat "$CLAUDE_MD")" = "$NEW_CONTENT" ]; then
370	            log "[DRY RUN] Content unchanged"
371	        else
372	            log "[DRY RUN] Content differs -- would overwrite"
373	        fi
374	    else
375	        log "[DRY RUN] File does not exist -- would create"
376	    fi
377	else
378	    backup_file "$CLAUDE_MD"
379	    # Capture existing content for post-write comparison
380	    OLD_CONTENT=""
381	    if [ -f "$CLAUDE_MD" ]; then
382	        OLD_CONTENT=$(cat "$CLAUDE_MD")
383	    fi
384	    if [ -f "$CLAUDE_MD" ]; then
385	        rm "$CLAUDE_MD"
386	        log "Removed existing $CLAUDE_MD"
387	    fi
388	
389	    # --- Write CLAUDE.md ---
390	    cat > "$CLAUDE_MD" << CLAUDE_EOF
391	${SHARED_CONTENT}
392	
393	## Machine-Specific
394	
395	- Machine: ${OS_NAME} ${ARCH} (${HOSTNAME})
396	- Shell: ${SHELL_NAME}
397	CLAUDE_EOF
398	
399	BLOCK
400	    # Extract: post-write validation from scripts/ (single source of truth)
401	    extract_between "$SCRIPTS_DIR/setup-user-claude.sh" \
402	        '^\s*# --- BEGIN post-write validation' '^\s*# --- END post-write validation'
403	    cat <<'BLOCK'
404	
405	    log_ok "Wrote $(display_path "$CLAUDE_MD")"
406	    if [ "$ERRORS" -eq 0 ]; then
407	        write_summary OK "claude.md" "deployed"
408	    else
409	        write_summary ERROR "claude.md" "validation failed"
410	    fi
411	    log "Machine: $OS_NAME $ARCH ($HOSTNAME), Shell: $SHELL_NAME"
412	    # Log whether content actually changed
413	    if [ -z "$OLD_CONTENT" ]; then
414	        log "Content: new file"
415	    elif [ "$OLD_CONTENT" = "$NEW_CONTENT" ]; then
416	        log "Content unchanged (no differences)"
417	    else
418	        log "Content updated"
419	        # Log unified diff to deploy log (not console)
420	        diff -u <(echo "$OLD_CONTENT") <(echo "$NEW_CONTENT") \
421	            --label "previous/CLAUDE.md" --label "new/CLAUDE.md" \
422	            >> "$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 || true  # diff exits 1 on differences (expected)
423	    fi
424	fi
425	
426	BLOCK
427	    # --- Embedded user rules deployment ---
428	    if [ "$USER_RULE_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
429	        # Set up embedded rules: write to temp dir, then use extracted deploy logic
430	        cat <<'BLOCK'
431	# --- Embedded user rules (from user repo at build time) ---
432	RULES_SRC=$(mktemp -d)
433	_cleanup_rules() { rm -rf "$RULES_SRC"; }
434	trap _cleanup_rules EXIT
435	BLOCK
436	        # Emit heredocs for each embedded rule file
437	        for i in $(seq 0 $((USER_RULE_COUNT - 1))); do
438	            local_name="${USER_RULE_NAMES[$i]}"
439	            # Sanitize name for heredoc delimiter: replace - and . with _
440	            safe_name=$(echo "$local_name" | perl -pe 's/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/_/g')
441	            echo "cat > \"\$RULES_SRC/$local_name\" <<'__RULE_${safe_name}__'"
442	            echo "${USER_RULE_CONTENTS[$i]}"
443	            echo "__RULE_${safe_name}__"
444	        done
445	        cat <<'BLOCK'
446	RULES_DEST="$CLAUDE_DIR/rules"
447	BLOCK
448	        # Extract deploy logic from scripts/ (single source of truth)
449	        extract_between "$SCRIPTS_DIR/setup-user-claude.sh" \
450	            '^# --- BEGIN rules deploy logic' '^# --- END rules deploy logic'
451	        cat <<'BLOCK'
452	
453	# Clean up temp source dir
454	rm -rf "$RULES_SRC"
455	trap - EXIT
456	BLOCK
457	    else
458	        cat <<'BLOCK'
459	log "No user rules embedded at build time -- ~/.claude/rules/ not managed by this script"
460	BLOCK
461	    fi
462	    extract_between "$SCRIPTS_DIR/setup-user-claude.sh" \
463	        '^# --- BEGIN exit' '^# --- END exit'
464	} | inline_lib_bash > "$DEPLOY_DIR/setup-user-claude.sh"
465	
466	chmod +x "$DEPLOY_DIR/setup-user-claude.sh"
467	GENERATED=$((GENERATED + 1))

477	# setup-user-claude.ps1 — Creates user-level ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and deploys user rules

2	# aitools-dashboard.sh -- Mission control dashboard lifecycle management (macOS/Linux)
3	# Safe to re-run. Manages the live dashboard server for running estimates.
4	#
5	# Usage:
6	#   bash scripts/aitools-dashboard.sh [OPTIONS]
7	#
8	# Options:
9	#   --background        Start server in background (for hooks)
10	#   --stop              Stop running server(s)
11	#     --port PORT         Stop specific port only
12	#     --all               Stop all instances
13	#   --status            Show all running instances with health
14	#   --health-check      Liveness + data quality check for all instances
15	#   --snapshot          Generate static HTML snapshot
16	#   --port PORT         Custom port (default: 8411)
17	#   --estimate PATH     Explicit estimate path (default: auto-detect)
18	#
19	# Multi-instance: PID files stored in ~/.aitools/dashboard-pids/<port>.pid
20	#
21	# Called by: aitools dashboard (entry point dispatch)
22	# Called by: SessionStart hook (dashboard-serve.sh) via aitools dashboard --background
23	# See: reference/tool-registry.md (Python managed tool)
24	
25	set -euo pipefail
26	
27	# --- Shared library ---
28	source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/aitools-lib.sh"
29	logging_init "aitools-dashboard"
30	
31	# --- OS guard ---
32	case "$(uname -s)" in
33	    MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*)
34	        log_error "This script is for macOS/Linux. On Windows, use aitools-dashboard.ps1 instead."
35	        exit 1 ;;
36	esac
37	
38	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
39	# Defaults
40	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
41	PORT=8411
42	ESTIMATE=""
43	ACTION="start"      # start | stop | status | snapshot | health-check
44	BACKGROUND=false
45	OPEN_BROWSER=false
46	PROJECT_ROOT=""
47	STOP_ALL=false
48	
49	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
50	# Argument parsing
51	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
52	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
53	    case "$1" in
54	        --background)   BACKGROUND=true; shift ;;
55	        --stop)         ACTION="stop"; shift ;;
56	        --status)       ACTION="status"; shift ;;
57	        --health-check) ACTION="health-check"; shift ;;
58	        --snapshot)     ACTION="snapshot"; shift ;;
59	        --open)         OPEN_BROWSER=true; shift ;;
60	        --all)          STOP_ALL=true; shift ;;
61	        --port)
62	            shift
63	            if [[ $# -eq 0 ]]; then
64	                log_error "--port requires a value"
65	                exit 1
66	            fi
67	            PORT="$1"; shift ;;
68	        --estimate)
69	            shift
70	            if [[ $# -eq 0 ]]; then
71	                log_error "--estimate requires a path"
72	                exit 1
73	            fi
74	            ESTIMATE="$1"; shift ;;
75	        --project-root)
76	            shift
77	            if [[ $# -eq 0 ]]; then
78	                log_error "--project-root requires a path"
79	                exit 1
80	            fi
81	            PROJECT_ROOT="$1"; shift ;;
82	        *)
83	            log_error "unknown option '$1'"
84	            exit 1 ;;
85	    esac
86	done
87	
88	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
89	# Resolve project root
90	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
91	if [ -z "$PROJECT_ROOT" ]; then
92	    PROJECT_ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)
93	fi
94	
95	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
96	# PID registry directory (multi-instance)
97	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
98	PID_REGISTRY_DIR="$HOME/.aitools/dashboard-pids"
99	mkdir -p "$PID_REGISTRY_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
100	
101	# Legacy PID file location (for migration)
102	LEGACY_PID_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/.aitools"
103	LEGACY_PID_FILE="$LEGACY_PID_DIR/.dashboard-pid"
104	
105	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
106	# Expected fields for health checks (shared with generate-dashboard.py)
107	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
108	EXPECTED_TOP_FIELDS="delegationLog findings openThreads"
109	EXPECTED_SITUATION_FIELDS="decisions assumptions deviations facts"
110	
111	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
112	# Find python3
113	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
114	find_python() {
115	    if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
116	        printf 'python3'
117	    elif command -v python >/dev/null 2>&1; then
118	        printf 'python'
119	    else
120	        return 1
121	    fi
122	}
123	
124	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
125	# Find the generator script
126	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
127	find_generator() {
128	    local repo_path=""
129	    repo_path=$(read_config_key "$HOME/.aitools/config.json" "repoPath" 2>/dev/null || true)
130	    repo_path="${repo_path:-$HOME/repos/aitools}"
131	
132	    if [ -f "$repo_path/scripts/generate-dashboard.py" ]; then
133	        printf '%s' "$repo_path/scripts/generate-dashboard.py"
134	    elif [ -f "$PROJECT_ROOT/scripts/generate-dashboard.py" ]; then
135	        printf '%s' "$PROJECT_ROOT/scripts/generate-dashboard.py"
136	    else
137	        return 1
138	    fi
139	}

141	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
142	# Auto-detect running estimate
143	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
144	find_estimate() {
145	    # 1. Check .aitools/channel/ for tracked running estimate
146	    if [ -f "$PROJECT_ROOT/.aitools/channel/running-estimate.json" ]; then
147	        printf '%s' "$PROJECT_ROOT/.aitools/channel/running-estimate.json"
148	        return 0
149	    fi
150	
151	    # 2. Check session-specific channel dirs
152	    if [ -d "$PROJECT_ROOT/.aitools/channel/" ]; then
153	        local dir est
154	        for dir in "$PROJECT_ROOT"/.aitools/channel/session-*/; do
155	            [ -d "$dir" ] || continue
156	            for est in "$dir"/*running-estimate*.json; do
157	                [ -f "$est" ] || continue
158	                printf '%s' "$est"
159	                return 0
160	            done
161	        done
162	    fi
163	
164	    # 3. Check .scratch/ for session estimates (most recently modified)
165	    if [ -d "$PROJECT_ROOT/.scratch" ]; then
166	        local best=""
167	        local dir est
168	        for dir in "$PROJECT_ROOT"/.scratch/session-*/; do
169	            [ -d "$dir" ] || continue
170	            for est in "$dir"/*running-estimate*.json; do
171	                [ -f "$est" ] || continue
172	                if [ -z "$best" ]; then
173	                    best="$est"
174	                elif [ "$est" -nt "$best" ]; then
175	                    best="$est"
176	                fi
177	            done
178	        done
179	        if [ -n "$best" ]; then
180	            printf '%s' "$best"
181	            return 0
182	        fi
183	    fi
184	
185	    # 4. Check .aitools/scratch/ (workspace namespace)
186	    if [ -d "$PROJECT_ROOT/.aitools/scratch" ]; then
187	        local best=""
188	        local dir est
189	        for dir in "$PROJECT_ROOT"/.aitools/scratch/session-*/; do
190	            [ -d "$dir" ] || continue
191	            for est in "$dir"/*running-estimate*.json; do
192	                [ -f "$est" ] || continue
193	                if [ -z "$best" ]; then
194	                    best="$est"
195	                elif [ "$est" -nt "$best" ]; then
196	                    best="$est"
197	                fi
198	            done
199	        done
200	        if [ -n "$best" ]; then
201	            printf '%s' "$best"
202	            return 0
203	        fi
204	    fi
205	
206	    return 1
207	}
