209	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
210	# PID registry helpers (multi-instance)
211	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
212	
213	# Get PID file path for a specific port
214	pid_file_for_port() {
215	    local port="$1"
216	    printf '%s/%s.pid' "$PID_REGISTRY_DIR" "$port"
217	}
218	
219	# Check if a specific port's server is running; prints PID if so
220	is_port_server_running() {
221	    local port="$1"
222	    local pf
223	    pf=$(pid_file_for_port "$port")
224	    if [ -f "$pf" ]; then
225	        local pid
226	        pid=$(cat "$pf" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
227	        if [ -n "$pid" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
228	            printf '%s' "$pid"
229	            return 0
230	        fi
231	        # Stale PID file -- clean up
232	        rm -f "$pf"
233	    fi
234	    return 1
235	}
236	
237	# Migrate legacy single PID file to registry (one-time)
238	migrate_legacy_pid() {
239	    if [ -f "$LEGACY_PID_FILE" ]; then
240	        local pid
241	        pid=$(cat "$LEGACY_PID_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
242	        if [ -n "$pid" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
243	            # Legacy server is running -- migrate its PID to the registry
244	            # We assume default port 8411 for legacy instances
245	            local new_pf
246	            new_pf=$(pid_file_for_port "8411")
247	            if [ ! -f "$new_pf" ]; then
248	                cp "$LEGACY_PID_FILE" "$new_pf"
249	                log "Migrated legacy PID $pid to port registry (8411)"
250	            fi
251	        fi
252	        rm -f "$LEGACY_PID_FILE"
253	    fi
254	}
255	
256	# List all running instances. Prints: port pid (one per line)
257	list_running_instances() {
258	    local found=false
259	    for pf in "$PID_REGISTRY_DIR"/*.pid; do
260	        [ -f "$pf" ] || continue
261	        local port_name pid
262	        port_name=$(basename "$pf" .pid)
263	        pid=$(cat "$pf" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
264	        if [ -n "$pid" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
265	            printf '%s %s\n' "$port_name" "$pid"
266	            found=true
267	        else
268	            # Stale PID file -- clean up
269	            rm -f "$pf"
270	        fi
271	    done
272	    if [ "$found" = false ]; then
273	        return 1
274	    fi
275	    return 0
276	}
277	
278	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
279	# Check if port is in use
280	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
281	is_port_in_use() {
282	    local port="$1"
283	    if command -v lsof >/dev/null 2>&1; then
284	        lsof -iTCP:"$port" -sTCP:LISTEN -t >/dev/null 2>&1
285	    elif command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
286	        ss -tlnp 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":${port} " 2>/dev/null
287	    else
288	        return 1
289	    fi
290	}
291	
292	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
293	# Health check helper: check one instance
294	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
295	check_instance_health() {
296	    local port="$1"
297	    local pid="$2"
298	    local healthy=true
299	    local details=""
300	
301	    # 1. HTTP liveness check
302	    local http_status=""
303	    if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
304	        http_status=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://localhost:${port}/" 2>/dev/null || echo "000")
305	    else
306	        # No curl -- skip HTTP check, just verify process is alive
307	        http_status="skip"
308	    fi
309	
310	    if [ "$http_status" = "skip" ]; then
311	        details="no curl available, process alive (PID $pid)"
312	    elif [ "$http_status" != "200" ]; then
313	        healthy=false
314	        details="HTTP $http_status (expected 200)"
315	    fi
316	
317	    # 2. Data quality check: read the estimate the dashboard is serving
318	    # Try the API endpoint first
319	    local estimate_json=""
320	    if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
321	        estimate_json=$(curl -s "http://localhost:${port}/api/estimate" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
322	    fi
323	
324	    if [ -n "$estimate_json" ]; then
325	        # Use python to check fields (available since we need it for the dashboard)
326	        local python_cmd=""
327	        python_cmd=$(find_python 2>/dev/null || echo "")
328	        if [ -n "$python_cmd" ]; then
329	            local check_result=""
330	            check_result=$("$python_cmd" -c "
331	import json, sys
332	try:
333	    d = json.loads(sys.stdin.read())
334	except:
335	    print('PARSE_ERROR')
336	    sys.exit(0)
337	missing = []
338	for f in ['delegationLog', 'findings', 'openThreads']:
339	    if f not in d:
340	        missing.append(f)
341	sit = d.get('situation')
342	if sit is None:
343	    missing.append('situation')
344	elif isinstance(sit, dict):
345	    for f in ['decisions', 'assumptions', 'deviations', 'facts']:
346	        if f not in sit:
347	            missing.append('situation.' + f)
348	delegations = len(d.get('delegationLog', []))
349	findings = len(d.get('findings', []))
350	threads = len(d.get('openThreads', []))
351	if missing:
352	    print('MISSING:' + ','.join(missing) + '|' + str(delegations) + '|' + str(findings) + '|' + str(threads))
353	else:
354	    print('OK|' + str(delegations) + '|' + str(findings) + '|' + str(threads))
355	" <<< "$estimate_json" 2>/dev/null || echo "CHECK_FAILED")
356	
357	            if [ "$check_result" = "PARSE_ERROR" ]; then
358	                healthy=false
359	                details="${details:+$details, }estimate JSON parse error"
360	            elif [ "$check_result" = "CHECK_FAILED" ]; then
361	                details="${details:+$details, }field check unavailable"
362	            elif printf '%s' "$check_result" | grep -q "^MISSING:"; then
363	                healthy=false
364	                local missing_fields=""
365	                missing_fields=$(printf '%s' "$check_result" | perl -pe 's/^MISSING:([^|]+)\|.*/$1/')
366	                local counts=""
367	                counts=$(printf '%s' "$check_result" | perl -pe 's/^MISSING:[^|]+\|//')
368	                local del_count=""
369	                del_count=$(printf '%s' "$counts" | cut -d'|' -f1)
370	                local find_count=""
371	                find_count=$(printf '%s' "$counts" | cut -d'|' -f2)
372	                local thread_count=""
373	                thread_count=$(printf '%s' "$counts" | cut -d'|' -f3)
374	                details="${details:+$details, }missing fields: $missing_fields ($del_count delegations, $find_count findings, $thread_count threads)"
375	            elif printf '%s' "$check_result" | grep -q "^OK|"; then
376	                local counts=""
377	                counts=$(printf '%s' "$check_result" | perl -pe 's/^OK\|//')
378	                local del_count=""
379	                del_count=$(printf '%s' "$counts" | cut -d'|' -f1)
380	                local find_count=""
381	                find_count=$(printf '%s' "$counts" | cut -d'|' -f2)
382	                local thread_count=""
383	                thread_count=$(printf '%s' "$counts" | cut -d'|' -f3)
384	                details="${details:+$details, }$del_count delegations, $find_count findings, $thread_count threads"
385	            fi
386	        else
387	            details="${details:+$details, }python not available for field check"
388	        fi
389	    elif [ "$http_status" = "200" ]; then
390	        details="${details:+$details, }no /api/estimate endpoint (static mode?)"
391	    fi
392	
393	    if [ "$healthy" = true ]; then
394	        log_ok "Dashboard on port $port: HEALTHY ($details)"
395	    else
396	        log_warn "Dashboard on port $port: UNHEALTHY ($details)"
397	    fi
398	
399	    if [ "$healthy" = true ]; then
400	        return 0
401	    else
402	        return 1
403	    fi
404	}

406	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
407	# Migrate legacy PID file on every invocation
408	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
409	migrate_legacy_pid
410	
411	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
412	# ACTION: status
413	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
414	if [ "$ACTION" = "status" ]; then
415	    local_found=false
416	    while IFS=' ' read -r inst_port inst_pid; do
417	        local_found=true
418	        log_ok "Dashboard server running (PID $inst_pid) on port $inst_port"
419	        log "  URL: http://localhost:$inst_port/"
420	        log "  PID file: $(pid_file_for_port "$inst_port")"
421	    done < <(list_running_instances 2>/dev/null || true)
422	
423	    if [ "$local_found" = false ]; then
424	        log "No dashboard instances running"
425	        if is_port_in_use "$PORT"; then
426	            log_warn "Port $PORT is in use by another process (not a managed dashboard)"
427	        fi
428	    fi
429	    exit 0
430	fi
431	
432	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
433	# ACTION: health-check
434	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
435	if [ "$ACTION" = "health-check" ]; then
436	    local_found=false
437	    local_unhealthy=0
438	    while IFS=' ' read -r inst_port inst_pid; do
439	        local_found=true
440	        if ! check_instance_health "$inst_port" "$inst_pid"; then
441	            local_unhealthy=$((local_unhealthy + 1))
442	        fi
443	    done < <(list_running_instances 2>/dev/null || true)
444	
445	    if [ "$local_found" = false ]; then
446	        log_warn "No dashboard instances running"
447	        exit 1
448	    fi
449	
450	    if [ "$local_unhealthy" -gt 0 ]; then
451	        exit 1
452	    fi
453	    exit 0
454	fi
455	
456	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
457	# ACTION: stop
458	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
459	if [ "$ACTION" = "stop" ]; then
460	    if [ "$STOP_ALL" = true ]; then
461	        # Stop all instances
462	        local_found=false
463	        while IFS=' ' read -r inst_port inst_pid; do
464	            local_found=true
465	            kill "$inst_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
466	            rm -f "$(pid_file_for_port "$inst_port")"
467	            log_ok "Stopped dashboard on port $inst_port (PID $inst_pid)"
468	        done < <(list_running_instances 2>/dev/null || true)
469	
470	        if [ "$local_found" = false ]; then
471	            log "No dashboard instances running"
472	        fi
473	    else
474	        # Stop specific port
475	        if pid=$(is_port_server_running "$PORT"); then
476	            kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
477	            rm -f "$(pid_file_for_port "$PORT")"
478	            log_ok "Stopped dashboard on port $PORT (PID $pid)"
479	        else
480	            log "No dashboard running on port $PORT"
481	        fi
482	    fi
483	    exit 0
484	fi
485	
486	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
487	# ACTION: snapshot
488	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
489	if [ "$ACTION" = "snapshot" ]; then
490	    PYTHON=$(find_python) || {
491	        log_error "python3 not found -- install Python to use the dashboard"
492	        write_summary ERROR "dashboard" "python3 not found"
493	        exit 1
494	    }
495	
496	    GENERATOR=$(find_generator) || {
497	        log_error "generate-dashboard.py not found"
498	        write_summary ERROR "dashboard" "generator not found"
499	        exit 1
500	    }
501	
502	    if [ -z "$ESTIMATE" ]; then
503	        ESTIMATE=$(find_estimate) || {
504	            log_error "no running estimate found"
505	            write_summary WARN "dashboard" "no estimate found"
506	            exit 1
507	        }
508	    fi
509	
510	    log "Generating static dashboard snapshot..."
511	    local_args=("--estimate" "$ESTIMATE")
512	    if [ "$OPEN_BROWSER" = true ]; then
513	        local_args+=("--open")
514	    fi
515	
516	    if "$PYTHON" "$GENERATOR" "${local_args[@]}"; then
517	        log_ok "Dashboard snapshot generated"
518	        write_summary OK "dashboard" "snapshot generated"
519	    else
520	        log_error "Dashboard generation failed"
521	        write_summary ERROR "dashboard" "generation failed"
522	        exit 1
523	    fi
524	    exit 0
525	fi
526	
527	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
528	# ACTION: start (default)
529	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
530	
531	# Check if this port already has a running instance
532	if pid=$(is_port_server_running "$PORT"); then
533	    log "Dashboard server already running on port $PORT (PID $pid)"
534	    if ! $BACKGROUND; then
535	        log "URL: http://localhost:$PORT/"
536	    fi
537	    write_summary OK "dashboard" "http://localhost:$PORT/ (already running)"
538	    exit 0
539	fi
540	
541	# Check if port is in use by something else
542	if is_port_in_use "$PORT"; then
543	    log_warn "Port $PORT is already in use by another process"
544	    write_summary WARN "dashboard" "port $PORT in use"
545	    exit 1
546	fi
547	
548	# Find dependencies
549	PYTHON=$(find_python) || {
550	    log_error "python3 not found -- install Python to use the dashboard"
551	    write_summary ERROR "dashboard" "python3 not found"
552	    exit 1
553	}
554	
555	GENERATOR=$(find_generator) || {
556	    log_error "generate-dashboard.py not found"
557	    write_summary ERROR "dashboard" "generator not found"
558	    exit 1
559	}
560	
561	# Resolve estimate path
562	if [ -z "$ESTIMATE" ]; then
563	    ESTIMATE=$(find_estimate) || {
564	        if $BACKGROUND; then
565	            # Background mode: no estimate is not an error, just skip
566	            exit 0
567	        fi
568	        log_error "no running estimate found"
569	        log "Create a running estimate in .aitools/channel/running-estimate.json or .scratch/session-*/running-estimate*.json"
570	        write_summary WARN "dashboard" "no estimate found"
571	        exit 1
572	    }
573	fi
574	
575	log "Starting dashboard server on port $PORT..."
576	log "Estimate: $ESTIMATE"
577	
578	PORT_PID_FILE=$(pid_file_for_port "$PORT")
579	
580	if $BACKGROUND; then
581	    # Background mode: nohup + disown for hook usage
582	    nohup "$PYTHON" "$GENERATOR" --estimate "$ESTIMATE" --serve --port "$PORT" \
583	        >/dev/null 2>&1 &
584	    SERVER_PID=$!
585	    disown "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
586	
587	    # Write PID to port-keyed registry
588	    printf '%d' "$SERVER_PID" > "$PORT_PID_FILE"
589	
590	    # Brief pause to let the server bind
591	    sleep 0.3
592	
593	    # Verify server started
594	    if kill -0 "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
595	        log_ok "Dashboard server started in background (PID $SERVER_PID) on port $PORT"
596	        log "URL: http://localhost:$PORT/"
597	        write_summary OK "dashboard" "http://localhost:$PORT/"
598	    else
599	        rm -f "$PORT_PID_FILE"
600	        log_error "Dashboard server failed to start"
601	        write_summary ERROR "dashboard" "failed to start"
602	        exit 1
603	    fi
604	else
605	    # Foreground mode: server runs until Ctrl+C
606	    # Write PID to port-keyed registry
607	    printf '%d' "$$" > "$PORT_PID_FILE"
608	
609	    # Trap to clean up PID file on exit
610	    cleanup() {
611	        rm -f "$PORT_PID_FILE"
612	    }
613	    trap cleanup EXIT
614	
615	    local_args=("--estimate" "$ESTIMATE" "--serve" "--port" "$PORT")
616	    if [ "$OPEN_BROWSER" = true ]; then
617	        local_args+=("--open")
618	    fi
619	
620	    write_summary OK "dashboard" "http://localhost:$PORT/"
621	    "$PYTHON" "$GENERATOR" "${local_args[@]}"
622	fi

   "content": "## Managed File Deployment (this repo)\n\nAll setup scripts that deploy files to user directories must follow the\ndeployment type matching the file format. Every type has the same\ncorrectness requirements: backup, logging, and validation. They differ\nonly in merge strategy.\n\n### Deployment types\n\n| Type | Merge strategy | Files |\n|------|---------------|-------|\n| Markdown | Interactive diff review via `deploy_managed_file` | CLAUDE.md, `~/.claude/rules/*.md`, skill SKILL.md files |\n| JSON config | Read-then-merge on managed fields only | settings.json, cli-config.json, mcp.json |\n| Shell script | Interactive diff review via `deploy_managed_file` | Hook scripts (`~/.claude/hooks/*.sh`) |\n\n`deploy_managed_file()` / `Deploy-ManagedFile` is defined in\n`@scripts/aitools-lib.sh` / `@scripts/aitools-lib.ps1`.\nFull state machine spec: `@reference/managed-file-deployment.md`.\n\n### Content sources\n\nDeployed content originates from two repos:\n\n| Source | Priority | What it provides |\n|--------|----------|-----------------|\n| Dotprofile repo (`aitools-<username>`) | Primary (wins if present) | CLAUDE.md template, user rules, profile.json (preferences, identity, machine profiles) |\n| aitools repo (`shared/`) | Fallback | claude-shared.md template, hook scripts, skills, shell aliases |\n\n- **Template interpolation**: `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` tokens in CLAUDE.md replaced with `profile.json` values at deploy time\n- **Machine profile selection**: `config.json` `machineAlias` → `profile.json` `profiles[alias]`. Fallback: hostname match, then first profile\n- **Rules**: additive deploy from `<userRepoPath>/claude/rules/` — managed files updated, unmanaged files in target preserved\n- **Skills**: vendored from upstream in `shared/skills/`, deployed to `~/.claude/skills/` and `~/.cursor/skills/`\n- **Hooks**: canonical source in `shared/hooks/`, deployed to `~/.claude/hooks/`\n\nFull spec: `@reference/user-repo.md`\n\n### Shared requirements (all types)\n\nThese apply equally regardless of file type:\n\n1. **Backup before write**: call `backup_file` / `Backup-File` before\n   writing to an existing file. For markdown and shell script types,\n   `deploy_managed_file` handles this internally. For JSON config type,\n   the caller MUST call it explicitly.\n2. **Diff logging**: log what changed to deploy.log before writing.\n   Markdown/shell: handled by `deploy_managed_file`. JSON config: log\n   changed fields with old → new values.\n3. **Post-write validation**: verify the written file immediately.\n   JSON: valid parse + required keys. Markdown: non-empty + required\n   sections. Shell: non-empty + executable bit.\n4. **Three-outcome tracking**: every deployment must resolve to\n   created, updated, or unchanged — and report via `write_summary`.\n\n### Platform-specific config values\n\nJSON config files may contain values that differ by platform. OS guards\nin setup scripts ensure the correct variant is deployed. Examples:\n\n| Config | Field | Windows | macOS |\n|--------|-------|---------|-------|\n| mcp.json | chrome-devtools command | `cmd /c npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest --isolated` | `npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest --isolated` |\n| settings.json | hook paths | `bash \"C:/Users/.../hooks/session-archive.sh\"` | `bash \"/Users/.../hooks/session-archive.sh\"` |\n\nScripts must NEVER write cross-platform values (e.g., macOS paths on\nWindows). The OS guard + platform dispatch pattern prevents this — see\n`@.claude/rules/cross-platform.md`.\n\n### Updating this table\n\nAdding a row (new file type) or column (new attribute) requires updating:\nthis rule, `@reference/managed-file-deployment.md`,\n`@.cursor/rules/managed-file-deployment.mdc`, and\nthe `/incident` skill if there are implementation gaps. See\n`@.claude/rules/tool-lifecycle.md` \"Deployment pattern updates\".\n\n### Cross-references\n\n- State machine + detail: `@reference/managed-file-deployment.md`\n- Text + JSON menus: `@.claude/rules/interactive-menus.md`\n- JSON write safety: `@.claude/rules/config-file-safety.md`\n- AI merge: `@.claude/rules/agentic-standards.md`\n- Content sources: `@reference/user-repo.md`\n- Known incidents: `/incident` skill\n",

   "path": "/Users/new-jose/repos/aitools/.claude/rules/web-sources.md",
   "type": "Project",
   "content": "## Web Source Reading (this repo)\n\nWhen reading web content that will feed into source-of-truth files\n(install commands, config steps, lifecycle fields, setup procedures),\nuse the Chrome DevTools MCP skill (`chrome-devtools`) instead of WebFetch.\n\n### Why\n\nWebFetch converts HTML to markdown via a smaller model -- two layers of\ninformation loss (rendering + summarization). Official docs sites are\noften JS-rendered SPAs with tabbed interfaces and platform toggles that\nWebFetch misses. When accuracy matters, use the real browser.\n\n### When to use Chrome DevTools MCP skill\n\n- Reading official tool docs to extract install commands for the `/tool-registry` skill\n- Verifying config requirements, post-install steps, or dependencies\n- Checking release notes or changelogs for lifecycle field updates\n- Any page whose content will be recorded verbatim in a protected file\n\n### When WebFetch is fine\n\n- General web searches and research (use WebSearch for queries)\n- Blog posts, tutorials, Stack Overflow -- low-stakes reference\n- Quick fact-checks that don't feed into protected files\n- Static pages where JS rendering isn't needed (plain GitHub READMEs)\n\n### Cross-reference\n\nBefore reading a tool's docs, check via the `/tool-registry` skill first --\nit may already have verified information. If proposing changes to an existing\nentry, re-verify using Chrome DevTools MCP skill before editing.\n",

   "type": "Project",
   "content": "## Tool Lifecycle (this repo)\n\n**Intent**: **Purpose**: Govern the lifecycle gates and onboarding\nrequirements for managed tools — ensuring tools pass evaluation\nbefore integration, and all onboarding artifacts are completed.\n**Scope**: Phase 2 gate, Under Evaluation guard, onboarding\nchecklist, bundled dependency graduation. NOT evaluation principles\n(`@.claude/rules/tool-evaluation.md`). NOT the evaluation process\n(`/tool-eval` skill). NOT registry data (`/tool-registry` skill).\n**Audience**: Every agent adding, modifying, or removing a managed\ntool.\n\n### Phase 2 gate\n\n**Hard stop.** After installing and providing a test command, MUST\nwait for the user's explicit approval before writing integration\ncode.\n\n- Do not plan Phase 3+ until Phase 2 is approved\n- Do not batch Phase 2 approval with Phase 3+ work\n- If rejected: uninstall, remove \"Under Evaluation\" entry, stop\n- If approved: promote to full entry, proceed to Phase 3+\n- Plans that include Phases 3-5 MUST note the gate\n\n### Under Evaluation guard\n\nTools with `evaluating` status on ALL platforms MUST NOT have:\n- Setup scripts in `scripts/`\n- Entries in `aitools-install.sh/.ps1`\n- Aliases in `shared/shell/`\n- Build pipeline entries in `build-deploy.sh`\n- Entry in CLAUDE.md Managed CLI Tools table\n\n### Bundled dependency graduation\n\nBundled tools used incidentally may remain as dependencies. If a\nbundled tool becomes a project requirement (USO, standing order,\nor widespread script dependency), it MUST graduate to a full\nmanaged tool via the standard lifecycle phases.\n\n### PATH refresh after install\n\nWhen installed via a package manager, the binary may not be on\nPATH. Do not hardcode package manager paths. Ask the user to\nrelaunch Claude Code, then verify.\n\n### Install cleanup\n\nSetup scripts installing via a preferred method SHOULD detect and\nremove old installs from non-preferred sources. Prevents PATH\nshadowing.\n\n### Install method discovery\n\nInstall methods and `BuildPrereqs` entries in setup scripts MUST\nbe derived from official tool documentation via the `/tool-eval`\nskill — never chosen from assumption or memory. The `/tool-eval`\nskill uses the chrome-devtools skill to navigate to the tool's\nofficial documentation and extract verified install commands.\n\n### Onboarding checklist\n\nWhen approved (Phase 2 passed), complete ALL steps. Use the\n`/tool-eval` skill for evaluation and the `/tool-registry` skill\nfor registry writes.\n\n#### Prerequisite\n- Verify upstream install method via `/tool-eval` skill\n- Record via `/tool-registry` skill (protected)\n\n#### Non-protected (implement directly)\n- `scripts/setup-<tool>.sh` + `.ps1`\n- `@scripts/aitools-install.sh` + `.ps1` — add step\n- `@scripts/build-deploy.sh` — add copy block pair\n- If auth required: add status check in setup scripts\n\n#### Protected (present for review)\n- Registry entry via `/tool-registry` skill\n- `@shared/claude-shared.md` — Managed CLI Tools table\n- `<userRepoPath>/claude/CLAUDE.md` — same row\n- `CLAUDE.md` — deploy list\n- Check script entries (`TOOL_CMDS` dictionaries)\n- Deployment types table if new file type\n\n#### Rebuild + propagate\n1. `bash scripts/build-deploy.sh` — verify count increments by 2\n2. `bash scripts/setup-user-claude.sh` — propagate CLAUDE.md\n3. `bash scripts/check-post-push.sh` — all checks pass\n4. Commit + push both repos\n\n### Dotprofile priority\n\n`setup-user-claude.sh/.ps1` reads dotprofile first. Rows added to\n`@shared/claude-shared.md` MUST also be added to the dotprofile\ntemplate.\n\n### When to invoke /tool-registry\n\nInvoke the `/tool-registry` skill when ANY of these arise:\n\n- Checking a tool's install method, version, or health status\n- Adding a new tool entry (after `/tool-eval` completes)\n- Updating an existing entry's fields or version\n- User says /tool-registry or /tools\n\nThe skill provides the governed process for reading and writing\nthe tool registry JSON. Accessing the registry data directly\nbypasses that process.\n\n### Cross-references\n\n- Evaluation principles: `@.claude/rules/tool-evaluation.md`\n- Evaluation process: `/tool-eval` skill\n- Registry access: `/tool-registry` skill\n- Discovery playbook: `@reference/tool-evaluation-playbook.md`\n- Evaluation criteria: `@reference/tool-evaluation-criteria.md`\n- Registry data: `/tool-registry` skill\n",

   "path": "/Users/new-jose/repos/aitools/.claude/rules/tool-evaluation.md",
   "type": "Project",
   "content": "## Tool Evaluation (this repo)\n\n**Intent**: **Purpose**: Govern how install methods are chosen and\nhow tool health is maintained for all managed tools. **Scope**:\nEvaluation gates, principle enforcement, and skill delegation.\nNOT the evaluation process (`/tool-eval` skill). NOT flag criteria\n(`/tool-eval` skill). NOT registry data (`/tool-registry` skill).\nNOT lifecycle gates (`@.claude/rules/tool-lifecycle.md`).\n**Audience**: Every agent making install method decisions.\n\n### Governing principle\n\naitools exists to give developers the best possible cross-platform\ntooling experience. Every managed tool is first-class — there are\nno second-class tools. An agent that recommends a degraded install\nmethod — system-bundled, unverified, stale — has violated this rule.\nAn agent that assumes a limited use case to justify a lesser method\nhas the evaluation backwards. Requirements determine the method,\nnot assumptions about how the tool will be used.\n\n### Evaluation principles (ranked)\n\nAll install method decisions MUST follow these, in order.\nHigher-ranked override lower when they conflict. Rationale and\ndetail: `@reference/tool-evaluation-criteria.md`.\n\n1. Official endorsement\n2. Verified provenance and security\n3. Latest stable version\n4. Cross-platform delivery — don't rebuild what exists\n5. Same upstream distribution across platforms\n6. Automation and deployment\n7. Maintenance health\n8. Build time\n\n### Gates\n\n- All evaluations MUST go through the `/tool-eval` skill\n- Every install method decision MUST be documented in\n  `reference/evaluations/`\n- Every tool MUST have per-platform health flags — `/tool-eval`\n  skill defines the criteria\n- Red flags MUST have a linked evaluation with migration plan\n- Yellow flags MUST be reviewed within 90 days\n\n### Cross-references\n\n- Evaluation process and flag criteria: `/tool-eval` skill\n- Registry access: `/tool-registry` skill\n- Evaluation criteria detail: `@reference/tool-evaluation-criteria.md`\n- Discovery process: `@reference/tool-evaluation-playbook.md`\n- Lifecycle gates: `@.claude/rules/tool-lifecycle.md`\n",
   "globs": [
    "scripts",
    "deploy",
    "shared",
    "reference",
    "plans"
   ],
   "contentDiffersFromDisk": true,

   "content": "## Documentation Standards (this repo)\n\n### RELEASE_NOTES.md format\n\nEach version entry follows this structure:\n\n```\n## vX.Y -- Title (YYYY-MM-DD)\n\n### Bug fixes           (table: #, Severity, Fix)\n### New features        (table: #, Change)\n### Improvements        (table: #, Change)\n### Documentation       (table: #, Change)\n### Files created       (table: File, Purpose)\n\n**Verified on:** platform notes\n```\n\nSections are optional -- include only those that apply. Number items sequentially across all sections within a release.\n\n### Version numbering\n\n`major.minor.patch` -- not semver, but follows the same spirit:\n\n- **Major** (v0 -> v1): structural changes to CLI commands, architecture, or project layout\n- **Minor** (v0.14): new features, new managed tools, batches of improvements\n- **Patch** (v0.14.1): isolated bug fixes with no new functionality\n\nMultiple changes on the same day roll into one release. Bug fixes ship alongside features in the same minor if they land together.\n\n### ROADMAP.md format\n\nThree sections: **In Progress**, **Planned**, **Completed**.\n\nEach section uses a table: `| Item | Plan | Priority | Summary |`\n\n- In Progress items must link to `plans/*.md`\n- Completed items move to RELEASE_NOTES.md (with version reference)\n\n### Reference doc threshold\n\nContent exceeding ~20 lines of detail belongs in `reference/`, not `CLAUDE.md`. Keep `CLAUDE.md` under 200 lines.\n\n### When to create a plan\n\nCreate a `plans/*.md` file when work:\n- Spans multiple sessions\n- Has phased gates or dependencies\n- Needs detailed design beyond a roadmap row\n\n### Layered reference architecture\n\n- **Rules** (`.claude/rules/`) = concise behavioral directives, ~40-100 lines\n- **References** (`reference/`) = implementation detail, unlimited length\n- **No duplication** — one authoritative location per fact\n- **Tool configs** documented per-tool via `/tool-registry` skill\n- **Specs vs state** — rules and references are specs;\n  the `/incident` skill tracks out-of-spec code.\n  See `@.claude/rules/incident-governance.md` for lifecycle and classification\n\n### Skill placement\n\n- **User-level** (`shared/skills/` → deployed to `~/.claude/skills/`):\n  managed tool patterns, project-agnostic conventions, USO enablement.\n  Content must be factual (patterns, gotchas, platform behavior), not\n  project-specific opinions.\n- **Project-level** (`.claude/skills/` in repo): project-specific\n  frameworks, governance workflows, development patterns. Auto-discovered\n  by Claude Code, not deployed.\n- **Split threshold**: A tool needs both user and project skills only\n  when it serves two distinct personas (end user vs developer). Use\n  `<name>` for user-level and `<name>-dev` for project-level.\n- **No project overrides of user skills**: User-level takes priority\n  in Claude Code. Never create same-name skills at both levels.\n- Full inventory and architecture:\n  `@plans/governance-and-compliance-framework.md`\n\n### `@` link convention\n\n- `@` can reference ANY repo file: `@reference/`, `@.claude/rules/`,\n  `@shared/`, `@scripts/`, `@plans/`\n- In `.claude/rules/*.md`: `@path/file.md` is NOT resolved — it remains\n  plain text. Use `@` consistently for all cross-references to signal\n  \"this is a linked file\" and enable grep-based link auditing\n- In `CLAUDE.md`: `@path/file.md` IS resolved at load time and pulls the\n  file into context. Only use `@` for files you want auto-loaded. Use\n  plain paths for references you want to keep lazy (most references)\n- Standardize existing rules files to use `@` for all cross-refs\n\n### Function and library attribution\n\n- When referencing shared library functions (`deploy_managed_file()`,\n  `backup_file()`, `invoke_ai()`, etc.), cite file + function name:\n  `deploy_managed_file()` in `@scripts/aitools-lib.sh` /\n  `Deploy-ManagedFile` in `@scripts/aitools-lib.ps1`\n- Never cite line numbers in rules or reference files — they drift.\n  Function names are stable identifiers\n- Plan files may use line numbers for one-time edit instructions\n",

  "content": {
   "path": "/Users/new-jose/repos/aitools/.claude/rules/hook-rollout.md",
   "type": "Project",
   "content": "## Hook Rollout Practice (this repo)\n\nAll PreToolUse hooks must go through an observe-then-enforce cycle before blocking.\n\n### Phases\n\n1. **Observe** (1+ week): Deploy with `MODE=\"observe\"`. Hook logs what it would\n   block to `~/.claude/hooks/logs/<hook-name>.log` but always exits 0.\n2. **Review**: Audit the log for false positives. Fix matching logic.\n3. **Enforce**: Switch to `MODE=\"enforce\"`. Hook blocks violations (exit 2).\n\n### Pre-deploy verification\n\nBefore deploying any hook change (new rule, mode promotion, or matching logic fix):\n\n1. **Syntax check**: `bash -n shared/hooks/<hook>.sh` — catches parse errors only\n2. **Smoke-test**: run the hook against a clean input and verify exit 0:\n   ```bash\n   echo '{\"tool_name\":\"Bash\",\"tool_input\":{\"command\":\"git status\"}}' \\\n     | bash shared/hooks/standing-order-guard.sh\n   echo \"exit: $?\"\n   ```\n3. **Violation test**: run against a known-bad input and verify the expected outcome\n   (exit 2 in enforce, log entry in observe):\n   ```bash\n   echo '{\"tool_name\":\"Bash\",\"tool_input\":{\"command\":\"git status && git log\"}}' \\\n     | bash shared/hooks/standing-order-guard.sh\n   echo \"exit: $?\"\n   ```\n\n`bash -n` is not sufficient for hooks using `set -euo pipefail` — it passes syntax\nbut cannot catch unset variable errors (`-u`) or runtime failures. Always smoke-test.\n(I12: stale `$MODE` reference caused crash-on-every-call after a refactor; `bash -n` passed.)\n\n### When to reset to observe\n\n- After adding new rules or patterns to an existing hook\n- After changing matching logic (e.g., adding pipeline exemptions)\n- After Claude Code version upgrades that may change tool input formats\n\n### Implementation\n\nEvery PreToolUse hook uses the `violation()` helper and declares mode variables:\n- `violation \"message\" \"$MODE_VAR\"` — mode drives observe vs. enforce\n- Log location: `~/.claude/hooks/logs/`\n- Global default `MODE_REST=\"observe\"` covers all checks not yet promoted\n- Per-check overrides (`MODE_AND`, `MODE_SUBSHELL`, etc.) allow granular rollout:\n  - `\"enforce\"` — zero false positives confirmed in log; blocks violations (exit 2)\n  - `\"observe\"` — logs what would be blocked; always exits 0\n\n**Current enforcement state (standing-order-guard.sh):**\n\n| Check | Variable | State | Notes |\n|-------|----------|-------|-------|\n| `&&` | `MODE_AND` | enforce | Zero false positives in log |\n| `$()` | `MODE_SUBSHELL` | enforce | Zero false positives in log |\n| `\\|\\|` | `MODE_REST` | observe | No false positives but low sample count |\n| `;` | `MODE_REST` | observe | False positives: pwsh `-Command`, `perl -e` — fix matching before promoting |\n| backticks | `MODE_REST` | observe | No false positives but low sample count |\n\nReview logs with: `cat ~/.claude/hooks/logs/standing-order-guard.log`\n",
   "globs": [
    "scripts",
    "deploy",
    "shared",
    "reference",
    "plans",
    "rfcs",
    ".claude/rules",
    ".cursor/rules",
    "CLAUDE.md",
    "RELEASE_NOTES.md",
    "ROADMAP.md",
    "README.md"
   ],
   "contentDiffersFromDisk": true,
   "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - scripts/**\n  - deploy/**\n  - shared/**\n  - reference/**\n  - plans/**\n  - rfcs/**\n  - .claude/rules/**\n  - .cursor/rules/**\n  - CLAUDE.md\n  - RELEASE_NOTES.md\n  - ROADMAP.md\n  - README.md\n---\n\n## Hook Rollout Practice (this repo)\n\nAll PreToolUse hooks must go through an observe-then-enforce cycle before blocking.\n\n### Phases\n\n1. **Observe** (1+ week): Deploy with `MODE=\"observe\"`. Hook logs what it would\n   block to `~/.claude/hooks/logs/<hook-name>.log` but always exits 0.\n2. **Review**: Audit the log for false positives. Fix matching logic.\n3. **Enforce**: Switch to `MODE=\"enforce\"`. Hook blocks violations (exit 2).\n\n### Pre-deploy verification\n\nBefore deploying any hook change (new rule, mode promotion, or matching logic fix):\n\n1. **Syntax check**: `bash -n shared/hooks/<hook>.sh` — catches parse errors only\n2. **Smoke-test**: run the hook against a clean input and verify exit 0:\n   ```bash\n   echo '{\"tool_name\":\"Bash\",\"tool_input\":{\"command\":\"git status\"}}' \\\n     | bash shared/hooks/standing-order-guard.sh\n   echo \"exit: $?\"\n   ```\n3. **Violation test**: run against a known-bad input and verify the expected outcome\n   (exit 2 in enforce, log entry in observe):\n   ```bash\n   echo '{\"tool_name\":\"Bash\",\"tool_input\":{\"command\":\"git status && git log\"}}' \\\n     | bash shared/hooks/standing-order-guard.sh\n   echo \"exit: $?\"\n   ```\n\n`bash -n` is not sufficient for hooks using `set -euo pipefail` — it passes syntax\nbut cannot catch unset variable errors (`-u`) or runtime failures. Always smoke-test.\n(I12: stale `$MODE` reference caused crash-on-every-call after a refactor; `bash -n` passed.)\n\n### When to reset to observe\n\n- After adding new rules or patterns to an existing hook\n- After changing matching logic (e.g., adding pipeline exemptions)\n- After Claude Code version upgrades that may change tool input formats\n\n### Implementation\n\nEvery PreToolUse hook uses the `violation()` helper and declares mode variables:\n- `violation \"message\" \"$MODE_VAR\"` — mode drives observe vs. enforce\n- Log location: `~/.claude/hooks/logs/`\n- Global default `MODE_REST=\"observe\"` covers all checks not yet promoted\n- Per-check overrides (`MODE_AND`, `MODE_SUBSHELL`, etc.) allow granular rollout:\n  - `\"enforce\"` — zero false positives confirmed in log; blocks violations (exit 2)\n  - `\"observe\"` — logs what would be blocked; always exits 0\n\n**Current enforcement state (standing-order-guard.sh):**\n\n| Check | Variable | State | Notes |\n|-------|----------|-------|-------|\n| `&&` | `MODE_AND` | enforce | Zero false positives in log |\n| `$()` | `MODE_SUBSHELL` | enforce | Zero false positives in log |\n| `\\|\\|` | `MODE_REST` | observe | No false positives but low sample count |\n| `;` | `MODE_REST` | observe | False positives: pwsh `-Command`, `perl -e` — fix matching before promoting |\n| backticks | `MODE_REST` | observe | No false positives but low sample count |\n\nReview logs with: `cat ~/.claude/hooks/logs/standing-order-guard.log`\n"

   "path": "/Users/new-jose/repos/aitools/.claude/rules/relay-outbound.md",
   "type": "Project",
   "content": "## Relay outbound (git) — not managed deploy\n\n**`.aitools/channel/relay.md`** lives **inside this repo**. It is **not** a managed\nuser file like `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (those use `[REVIEW]` / `deploy_managed_file`\nduring deploy — see `@.claude/rules/managed-file-deployment.md`).\n\n**Inbound (pull):** `aitools` / `hh` runs `git pull` on the aitools clone, then\ndeploy and relay → `AGENTS.md` when Python is available.\n\n**Outbound (commit + push):** Only the commander (or a shell with credentials)\ncan publish. After **`aitools`** or **`hh -n`**, the harness may show a\n**`[RELAY]`** prompt when:\n\n- `relay.md` has **uncommitted** changes, or\n- the current branch is **ahead of `origin/main`** (unpushed commits).\n\nScript sources: `scripts/relay-outbound-prompt.sh` (bash / Git Bash),\n`scripts/relay-outbound-prompt.ps1` (PowerShell). Choices: **[c]** continue,\n**[q]** exit with code 2, **[s]** show `git status -sb`.\n\n**Skip automation:** `AITOOLS_SKIP_RELAY_PROMPT=1`. **CI / non-interactive:**\nshort hint only (or set `RELAY_PROMPT_FORCE=1` to force the full prompt when a\nTTY exists).\n\n**Agent behavior:** If you edited `relay.md`, propose **`git add` / `git commit` /\n`git push`** with a **`channel:`** subject (see relay.md). Do not claim push\nsucceeded without evidence. Do not put tokens or secrets in relay or commit\nmessages.\n",
   "globs": [
    ".aitools/channel/relay.md",
    "scripts/relay-outbound-prompt.sh",
    "scripts/relay-outbound-prompt.ps1",
    "scripts/aitools",
    "scripts/aitools.ps1",
    "scripts/hh.sh",
    "scripts/hh.ps1"
   ],
   "contentDiffersFromDisk": true,
   "rawContent": "---\npaths:\n  - .aitools/channel/relay.md\n  - scripts/relay-outbound-prompt.sh\n  - scripts/relay-outbound-prompt.ps1\n  - scripts/aitools\n  - scripts/aitools.ps1\n  - scripts/hh.sh\n  - scripts/hh.ps1\n---\n\n## Relay outbound (git) — not managed deploy\n\n**`.aitools/channel/relay.md`** lives **inside this repo**. It is **not** a managed\nuser file like `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (those use `[REVIEW]` / `deploy_managed_file`\nduring deploy — see `@.claude/rules/managed-file-deployment.md`).\n\n**Inbound (pull):** `aitools` / `hh` runs `git pull` on the aitools clone, then\ndeploy and relay → `AGENTS.md` when Python is available.\n\n**Outbound (commit + push):** Only the commander (or a shell with credentials)\ncan publish. After **`aitools`** or **`hh -n`**, the harness may show a\n**`[RELAY]`** prompt when:\n\n- `relay.md` has **uncommitted** changes, or\n- the current branch is **ahead of `origin/main`** (unpushed commits).\n\nScript sources: `scripts/relay-outbound-prompt.sh` (bash / Git Bash),\n`scripts/relay-outbound-prompt.ps1` (PowerShell). Choices: **[c]** continue,\n**[q]** exit with code 2, **[s]** show `git status -sb`.\n\n**Skip automation:** `AITOOLS_SKIP_RELAY_PROMPT=1`. **CI / non-interactive:**\nshort hint only (or set `RELAY_PROMPT_FORCE=1` to force the full prompt when a\nTTY exists).\n\n**Agent behavior:** If you edited `relay.md`, propose **`git add` / `git commit` /\n`git push`** with a **`channel:`** subject (see relay.md). Do not claim push\nsucceeded without evidence. Do not put tokens or secrets in relay or commit\nmessages.\n"
  },

 }

   "type": "Project",
   "content": "## Dual Deployment Paths (this repo)\n\nTwo deployment methods must produce equivalent results:\n\n1. **Dev/repo path** (`scripts/setup-*.sh/.ps1`): reads `shared/` and user repo at\n   runtime. Used by `aitools` CLI.\n2. **MDM path** (`<userRepoPath>/deploy/setup-*.sh/.ps1`): self-contained, personalized,\n   generated by `build-deploy.sh` into the user's dotprofile repo. Used for endpoint\n   deployment. The shared `aitools/deploy/` is frozen (no longer regenerated).\n\n### When changing `shared/` content\n\n1. Edit the `shared/` source file\n2. If the file has a user repo counterpart (e.g., `@shared/claude-shared.md` →\n   `<userRepoPath>/claude/CLAUDE.md`), update both\n3. Run `bash scripts/build-deploy.sh` to regenerate `<userRepoPath>/deploy/` (your dotprofile repo)\n4. Both paths now produce equivalent output\n\n### When changing `scripts/setup-*.sh/.ps1`\n\n1. Edit the `scripts/` source\n2. Run `bash scripts/build-deploy.sh` to regenerate the `<userRepoPath>/deploy/` counterpart\n3. Verify the dotprofile `deploy/` includes the change (the shared `aitools/deploy/` is frozen, so pre-commit deploy-drift steps 3+10 no longer apply to it)\n\n### Template sync\n\n`@shared/claude-shared.md` and `<userRepoPath>/claude/CLAUDE.md` must stay in sync.\nWhen one changes, update the other. The user repo template takes priority at runtime\n(scripts/ path reads it first, falls back to shared/).\n\n### Scripts with deploy templates (duplication risk)\n\nFour script pairs have **duplicated setup logic** between `scripts/` and\n`build-deploy.sh`. Fixing a bug in one requires manually porting to the other.\nRunning `build-deploy.sh` does NOT auto-fix stale template logic — it faithfully\nreproduces whatever is hardcoded in the template.\n\n| Script | Template in build-deploy.sh | What's duplicated |\n|--------|---------------------------|-------------------|\n| `setup-user-claude.sh/.ps1` | Sections 5-6 | Template interpolation, footer generation |\n| `setup-user-cursor.sh/.ps1` | Sections 7-8 | CLI config merge logic (Node.js/PS1) |\n| `setup-user-mcp.sh/.ps1` | Sections 11-12 | Settings.json merge, validation |\n| `setup-user-hooks.sh/.ps1` | Sections 13-14 | Settings.json hook merge, dedup, validation |\n\n**What IS auto-embedded** (safe — single source of truth):\n- `shared/hooks/*.sh` → read via `cat` at build time\n- `shared/skills/*.md` → read via `cat` at build time\n- `@shared/claude-shared.md` → read via `cat` at build time\n- `<userRepoPath>/claude/rules/*.md` → read via `cat` at build time\n\n**When changing setup logic in any of the 4 scripts above**:\n\n1. Fix the bug in `scripts/setup-*.sh` and/or `.ps1`\n2. **Find and fix the same logic in `build-deploy.sh`** (search for the function\n   name, variable name, or pattern)\n3. Run `bash scripts/build-deploy.sh`\n4. Verify `deploy/` output contains the fix (not just the old template output)\n5. Pre-commit step 13 will warn if step 2 was missed\n\nThis duplication is a known technical debt item (incident I6, see ROADMAP.md).\nThe structural fix is to refactor `build-deploy.sh` to extract setup logic from\n`scripts/` at build time instead of maintaining parallel copies.\n",

Used by `aitools` CLI.\n2. **MDM path** (`<userRepoPath>/deploy/setup-*.sh/.ps1`): self-contained, personalized,\n   generated by `build-deploy.sh` into the user's dotprofile repo. Used for endpoint\n   deployment. The shared `aitools/deploy/` is frozen (no longer regenerated).\n\n### When changing `shared/` content\n\n1. Edit the `shared/` source file\n2. Blind overwrites silently drop\nuser data and non-managed fields.\n\n### Default: read-then-merge\n\n1. Read the existing file\n2. Parse JSON (handle missing vs corrupt -- see below)\n3. Set only the fields the script manages\n4. Write the merged result\n\n### Managed vs preserved fields\n\nEvery config-writing script must document in its header comment which fields it\nowns (manages) and which it preserves. Example:\n\n```\n# Managed fields: mcpServers.chrome-devtools, mcpServers.vercel, mcpServers.webflow\n# Preserved: all other mcpServers entries, all other top-level keys\n```\n\n### Overwrite exceptions\n\nA script may overwrite (not merge) only when it is the **sole owner** of the entire\nfile (e.g., `setup-user-claude` owns `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`). The script header must\ndocument: `# Overwrites: yes (sole owner of this file)`.\n\n### Empty `catch {}` anti-pattern\n\nWhen reading JSON before merge, distinguish file-not-found (start fresh) from\nparse errors (warn the user). Never silently swallow parse errors:\n\n```javascript\nlet config = {};\ntry {\n    config = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8'));\n} catch (e) {\n    if (e.code !== 'ENOENT') {\n        console.error('Warning: ' + f + ' is invalid JSON, starting with empty config');\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Anti-patterns\n\n- `cat > file << EOF` for any JSON file not solely owned by the script\n- `ConvertTo-Json | WriteAllText` without reading existing content first\n- `try { ... } catch {}` that swallows both ENOENT and parse errors\n\n### Backup before overwrite\n\nScripts MUST back up targets before writing, regardless of ownership model\nor deployment type. This applies equally to all managed file types:\n\n- **Markdown files and shell scripts**: `deploy_managed_file` calls\n  `backup_file` internally — callers need not call it separately\n- **JSON config files**: caller MUST call `backup_file` / `Backup-File`\n  before the merge write\n\nRetention:\n- **Single files**: `<file>.bak.<TIMESTAMP>`, keep at most 20, auto-prune oldest\n- **Directories**: `<dir>.bak.<TIMESTAMP>/`, keep at most 5, auto-prune oldest\n- Skip if target doesn't exist (first run — nothing to back up)\n\nBackup failures are non-fatal (warn and proceed) — a failed backup should not\nblock deployment. A merge or copy without backup is a bug.\n\nSee `@.claude/rules/managed-file-deployment.md` for full deployment type\ndefinitions and `@reference/managed-file-deployment.md` \"Backup Policy\"\nfor details.\n\n### Diff logging on overwrite\n\nBefore overwriting an existing file, compare old and new content:\n\n- **Identical**: skip the write, log \"unchanged\"\n- **Different**: log unified diff to deploy log, then overwrite\n- **New file** (no target): log \"added\", no diff needed\n\nThis applies to both single-file overwrites and directory deployments.\nConsole shows summary counts; the deploy log captures full diffs.\n\n### Directory deployment (additive pattern)\n\nWhen a script manages a directory of files (not a single file), use the additive\npattern — deploy managed files, preserve everything else:\n\n1. 1491	                \$null = [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile('$(cygpath -w "$ps1_file")', [ref]\$null, [ref]\$e)
1492	                if (\$e.Count -gt 0) {
1493	                    foreach (\$err in \$e) { Write-Host \"  line \$(\$err.Extent.StartLineNumber): \$(\$err.Message)\" }
1494	                    exit 1
1495	                }
1496	            " 2>/dev/null; then
1497	                blog_error "$ps1_name has parse errors on this PowerShell version"
1498	                PS1_ERRORS=$((PS1_ERRORS + 1))

1502	            blog_error "$PS1_ERRORS PS1 file(s) failed validation"
1503	            exit 1

1521	                        exit 1
1522	                    }
1523	                " 2>&1) || {

1527	                }
1528	            done

96	# Check profile.json for issues and optionally prompt for fixes.
97	# Usage: Invoke-ProfileCheck -Mode "warn" or "interactive"
98	# Requires: node, $repoPath, $configFile
99	function Invoke-ProfileCheck {
100	    param([string]$Mode = "warn")
101	    if (-not (Get-Command node -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { return }
102	    if (-not (Test-Path $repoPath)) { return }
103	
104	    $checkScript = Join-Path $repoPath "scripts\profile-check.js"
105	    if (-not (Test-Path $checkScript)) { return }
106	
107	    try {
108	        $resultJson = node $checkScript --config $configFile 2>$null
109	    } catch { return }
110	    if (-not $resultJson) { return }
111	
112	    try {
113	        $result = $resultJson | ConvertFrom-Json
114	    } catch { return }
115	
116	    switch ($result.status) {
117	        "ok" { return }
118	        "unconfigured" { return }
119	        "error" {
120	            $msg = if ($result.issues -and $result.issues.Count -gt 0) { $result.issues[0].message } else { "profile.json has issues" }
121	            Write-Host "profile: $msg" -ForegroundColor Yellow
122	        }
123	        "warn" {
124	            foreach ($issue in $result.issues) {
125	                Write-Host "profile: $($issue.message)" -ForegroundColor Yellow
126	            }
127	            if ($Mode -eq "interactive" -and [Environment]::UserInteractive) {
128	                Write-Host "Run 'aitools user init' to fix." -ForegroundColor Yellow
129	            }
130	        }
131	        "migrate" {
132	            Write-Host "profile: profile.json is v1 (legacy). Migration to v2 recommended." -ForegroundColor Yellow
133	            if ($Mode -eq "interactive" -and [Environment]::UserInteractive) {
134	                $answer = Read-Host "Migrate profile.json to v2 now? [y/N]"
135	                if ($answer -match '^[Yy]') {
136	                    Invoke-ProfileMigration -CheckResult $result
137	                }
138	            }
139	        }
140	    }
141	}

271	# Version string from a git repo using tag-based scheme.
272	# v0.14.0              -> 0.14.0       (on tag exactly)
273	# v0.14.0-5-gabcdef    -> 0.14.0+5    (5 commits ahead of tag)
274	# The +N suffix indicates unreleased commits; it is never a real version.
275	function Get-RepoVersion {
276	    param([string]$RepoPath)
277	    try {
278	        $desc = git -C $RepoPath describe --tags --match "v*" 2>$null
279	        if ($desc) {
280	            $base = $desc.TrimStart("v")
281	            if ($base -match '^(.+)-(\d+)-g[0-9a-f]+$') {
282	                $tagPart = $Matches[1]       # 0.14.0
283	                $commits = $Matches[2]       # 5
284	                return "${tagPart}+${commits}"
285	            } else {
286	                return $base                 # 0.14.0
287	            }
288	        }
289	        # No tags -- fallback
290	        $log = git -C $RepoPath log -1 --format='%cd (%h)' --date=short 2>$null
291	        if ($log) { return $log } else { return "unknown" }
292	    } catch { return "unknown" }
293	}

306	            # Validate PS1 syntax before executing

308	            $null = [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile(
309	                $scriptPath, [ref]$null, [ref]$parseErrors)
310	            if ($parseErrors.Count -gt 0) {
311	                LogWarn "$script has parse errors -- skipping"
312	                $errors++
313	                continue

344	    Remove-Item Env:\AITOOLS_DRY_RUN -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

403	# Display cloud MCP servers from claude.ai configuration.
404	# Usage: Show-CloudMcp -Context "mcp" or "install" [-ScriptName "setup-user-mcp"]
405	# When ScriptName is provided, uses structured logging format for deploy sequence.
406	# Silent no-op if claude CLI unavailable or no cloud servers found.
407	function Show-CloudMcp {
408	    param(
409	        [string]$Context = "mcp",
410	        [string]$ScriptName = ""
411	    )
412	    if (-not (Get-Command claude -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { return }
413	
414	    $savedClaudeCode = $env:CLAUDECODE
415	    Remove-Item Env:\CLAUDECODE -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
416	
417	    try {
418	        $savedEncoding = [Console]::OutputEncoding
419	        [Console]::OutputEncoding = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8
420	        $raw = claude mcp list 2>$null
421	        [Console]::OutputEncoding = $savedEncoding
422	    } catch {
423	        $raw = $null
424	    }
425	
426	    if ($savedClaudeCode) {
427	        $env:CLAUDECODE = $savedClaudeCode
428	    }
429	
430	    if (-not $raw) { return }
431	
432	    $entries = @()
433	    foreach ($line in $raw) {
434	        $clean = $line -replace '\e\[[0-9;]*m', ''
435	        if ($clean -match '^claude\.ai\s+(.+?):\s+.+\s+-\s+(.+)$') {
436	            $name = $Matches[1].Trim()
437	            $status = $Matches[2].Trim()
438	            $entries += [PSCustomObject]@{ Name = $name; Status = $status }
439	        }
440	    }
441	
442	    if ($entries.Count -eq 0) { return }
443	
444	    if ($ScriptName) {
445	        # Structured logging for deploy sequence
446	        $ts = (Get-Date).ToUniversalTime().ToString("yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ")
447	        Write-Host "[$ts] [$ScriptName] Cloud MCP servers (configured at claude.ai):"
448	        foreach ($entry in $entries) {
449	            if ($entry.Name.Length -lt 24) {
450	                $pad = " " * (24 - $entry.Name.Length)
451	            } else {
452	                $pad = " "
453	            }
454	            $ts = (Get-Date).ToUniversalTime().ToString("yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ")
455	            Write-Host "[$ts] [$ScriptName]   $($entry.Name)$pad$($entry.Status)"
456	        }
457	    } else {
458	        Write-Host ""
459	        Write-Host "Cloud (claude.ai):"
460	        foreach ($entry in $entries) {
461	            if ($entry.Name.Length -lt 24) {
462	                $pad = " " * (24 - $entry.Name.Length)
463	            } else {
464	                $pad = " "
465	            }
466	            Write-Host "  $($entry.Name)$pad$($entry.Status)"
467	        }
468	    }
469	}

475	function Show-Usage {
476	    @"
477	Usage: aitools [COMMAND] [OPTIONS]
478	
479	Commands:
480	  (none)               Sync configs: pull + rebuild + deploy all configurations
481	  gitpull [--patch]    Update source: pull + rebuild + deploy + changelog + version tag
482	                       --patch: bump patch (v0.14.0 -> v0.14.1) instead of minor
483	  install              Full setup: pull + rebuild + install tools + deploy configs
484	  mcp                  Show MCP server status for current project
485	  user init            Set up user repo and configure session archiving hook
486	  sessions list [proj] List archived sessions (optionally filter by project)
487	  sessions archive ID  Manually archive a session by ID (full or prefix)
488	  sessions move F proj Refile an archived session under a different project
489	  dashboard            Start the live mission control dashboard server
490	                       --stop: stop the server  --status: show server status
491	                       --snapshot: generate static HTML  --background: for hooks
492	
493	Options:
494	  --addmcp <name...>   Enable MCP server(s) for current project (vercel, webflow)
495	  --dry-run            Preview what would change without writing any files
496	  --force              Overwrite all files without prompting for review
497	  --version, -v        Show installed and repo version
498	  --help, -h           Show this help
499	
500	Install flags (passed through to installer):
501	  --skip-gh-auth       Skip GitHub CLI authentication
502	  --repos-path PATH    Set repos directory without prompting
503	  --skip-drive-detection  Skip Google Drive auto-detection
504	"@
505	}

556	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

560	$oldConfigDir = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ".config\ai-tooling"
561	$newConfigDir = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ".aitools"

563	if ((Test-Path $oldConfigDir) -and -not (Test-Path $newConfigDir)) {
564	    Move-Item -Path $oldConfigDir -Destination $newConfigDir
565	} elseif ((Test-Path $oldConfigDir) -and (Test-Path $newConfigDir)) {
566	    LogWarn "both $oldConfigDir and $newConfigDir exist -- using $newConfigDir"
567	}

573	$configFile = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE ".aitools\config.json"
574	$repoPath = ""

576	$raw = Read-ConfigKey -File $configFile -Key "repoPath"
577	if (-not $raw) { $raw = Read-ConfigKey -File $configFile -Key "aiToolingRepoPath" }
578	if ($raw) { $repoPath = $raw }
579	if (-not $repoPath) { $repoPath = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE "repos\aitools" }
580	
581	# Auto-migrate: aiToolingRepoPath -> repoPath (repo renamed ai-tooling -> aitools)
582	$oldKey = Read-ConfigKey -File $configFile -Key "aiToolingRepoPath"
583	if ($oldKey) {
584	    try {
585	        $cfgObj = Get-Content $configFile -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
586	        if (-not $cfgObj.repoPath -and $cfgObj.aiToolingRepoPath) {
587	            $newVal = $cfgObj.aiToolingRepoPath -replace 'ai-tooling', 'aitools'
588	            $cfgObj | Add-Member -NotePropertyName "repoPath" -NotePropertyValue $newVal -Force
589	        }
590	        $cfgObj.PSObject.Properties.Remove("aiToolingRepoPath")
591	        $json = $cfgObj | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10
592	        $resolved = $ExecutionContext.SessionState.Path.GetUnresolvedProviderPathFromPSPath($configFile)
593	        [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($resolved, $json + "`n", [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))
594	        Log "Migrated config: aiToolingRepoPath -> repoPath"
595	        # Re-read after migration
596	        $repoPath = Read-ConfigKey -File $configFile -Key "repoPath"
597	    } catch {
598	        LogWarn "Config key migration failed: $_"
599	        # Non-fatal: continue with whatever repoPath was already resolved
600	    }
601	}

626	const fs = require("fs");
627	const path = require("path");
628	const os = require("os");
629	
630	const home = os.homedir();
631	const cwd = process.cwd();
632	
633	function readJson(f) {
634	    try { return JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(f, "utf8")); } catch { return null; }
635	}
636	
637	// --- Claude Code ---
638	const claudeJson = readJson(path.join(home, ".claude.json"));
639	const claudeSettings = readJson(path.join(home, ".claude", "settings.json"));
640	const projectSettings = readJson(path.join(cwd, ".claude", "settings.json"));
641	const projectLocalSettings = readJson(path.join(cwd, ".claude", "settings.local.json"));
642	
643	const claudeDeny = claudeSettings?.permissions?.deny || [];
644	const projectAllow = [
645	    ...(projectSettings?.permissions?.allow || []),
646	    ...(projectLocalSettings?.permissions?.allow || []),
647	];
648	
649	console.log("MCP Server Status (" + cwd + ")\n");
650	
651	if (claudeJson?.mcpServers) {
652	    console.log("Claude Code:");
653	    const servers = claudeJson.mcpServers;
654	    for (const [name, cfg] of Object.entries(servers)) {
655	        const transport = cfg.type === "http" || cfg.url ? "http" : "stdio";
656	        const denyPattern = "MCP(" + name + ")";
657	        const denied = claudeDeny.includes(denyPattern);
658	        const allowed = projectAllow.includes(denyPattern);
659	        const status = denied && !allowed ? "disabled" : "enabled";
660	        const pad = name.length < 16 ? " ".repeat(16 - name.length) : " ";
661	        console.log("  " + name + pad + status.padEnd(10) + "(user)   " + transport);
662	    }
663	
664	    // Show project overrides if any
665	    const overrides = [];
666	    for (const rule of projectAllow) {
667	        const match = rule.match(/^MCP\((.+)\)$/);
668	        if (match) {
669	            const source = projectLocalSettings?.permissions?.allow?.includes(rule)
670	                ? ".claude/settings.local.json"
671	                : ".claude/settings.json";
672	            overrides.push({ name: match[1], source });
673	        }
674	    }
675	    if (overrides.length > 0) {
676	        console.log("  Project overrides:");
677	        for (const o of overrides) {
678	            const pad = o.name.length < 16 ? " ".repeat(16 - o.name.length) : " ";
679	            console.log("    " + o.name + pad + "enabled   (" + o.source + ")");
680	        }
681	    }
682	} else {
683	    console.log("Claude Code: no user-level MCP config found (~/.claude.json)");
684	}
685	
686	console.log("");
687	
688	// --- Cursor ---
689	const cursorJson = readJson(path.join(home, ".cursor", "mcp.json"));
690	const projectCursorJson = readJson(path.join(cwd, ".cursor", "mcp.json"));
691	
692	if (cursorJson?.mcpServers) {
693	    console.log("Cursor:");
694	    const servers = cursorJson.mcpServers;
695	    for (const [name, cfg] of Object.entries(servers)) {
696	        const transport = cfg.url ? "http" : "stdio";
697	        const pad = name.length < 16 ? " ".repeat(16 - name.length) : " ";
698	        console.log("  " + name + pad + "(user)   " + transport);
699	    }
700	    if (projectCursorJson?.mcpServers) {
701	        console.log("  Project overrides (.cursor/mcp.json):");
702	        for (const [name, cfg] of Object.entries(projectCursorJson.mcpServers)) {
703	            const transport = cfg.url ? "http" : "stdio";
704	            const pad = name.length < 16 ? " ".repeat(16 - name.length) : " ";
705	            console.log("    " + name + pad + "enabled   " + transport);
706	        }
707	    }
708	} else {
709	    console.log("Cursor: no user-level MCP config found (~/.cursor/mcp.json)");
710	}
711	'@

713	    exit 0
714	}

765	const fs = require('fs');

1	# aitools-dashboard.ps1 -- Mission control dashboard lifecycle management (Windows)
2	# Safe to re-run. Manages the live dashboard server for running estimates.
3	#
4	# Usage:
5	#   pwsh -File scripts/aitools-dashboard.ps1 [OPTIONS]
6	#
7	# Options:
8	#   -Background         Start server in background (for hooks)
9	#   -Stop               Stop running server(s)
10	#     -Port PORT          Stop specific port only
11	#     -All                Stop all instances
12	#   -Status             Show all running instances with health
13	#   -HealthCheck        Liveness + data quality check for all instances
14	#   -Snapshot           Generate static HTML snapshot
15	#   -Port PORT          Custom port (default: 8411)
16	#   -Estimate PATH      Explicit estimate path (default: auto-detect)
17	#
18	# Multi-instance: PID files stored in ~/.aitools/dashboard-pids/<port>.pid
19	#
20	# Called by: aitools dashboard (entry point dispatch)

22	# See: reference/tool-registry.md (Python managed tool)

24	param(
25	    [switch]$Background,

95	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

97	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
98	function Find-Estimate {
99	    # 1. Check .aitools/channel/ for tracked running estimate
100	    $tracked = Join-Path $ProjectRoot ".aitools\channel\running-estimate.json"
101	    if (Test-Path $tracked) { return $tracked }
102	
103	    # 2. Check session-specific channel dirs
104	    $channelDir = Join-Path $ProjectRoot ".aitools\channel"
105	    if (Test-Path $channelDir) {
106	        $sessionDirs = Get-ChildItem -Path $channelDir -Directory -Filter "session-*" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
107	        foreach ($dir in $sessionDirs) {
108	            $estimates = Get-ChildItem -Path $dir.FullName -Filter "*running-estimate*.json" -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
109	            if ($estimates) { return $estimates[0].FullName }
110	        }
111	    }
112	
113	    # 3. Check .scratch/ for session estimates (most recently modified)
114	    $scratchDir = Join-Path $ProjectRoot ".scratch"
115	    if (Test-Path $scratchDir) {
116	        $best = $null
117	        $sessionDirs = Get-ChildItem -Path $scratchDir -Directory -Filter "session-*" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
118	        foreach ($dir in $sessionDirs) {
119	            $estimates = Get-ChildItem -Path $dir.FullName -Filter "*running-estimate*.json" -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
120	            foreach ($est in $estimates) {
121	                if (-not $best -or $est.LastWriteTime -gt $best.LastWriteTime) {
122	                    $best = $est
123	                }
124	            }
125	        }
126	        if ($best) { return $best.FullName }
127	    }
128	
129	    # 4. Check .aitools/scratch/ (workspace namespace)
130	    $asScratchDir = Join-Path $ProjectRoot ".aitools\scratch"
131	    if (Test-Path $asScratchDir) {
132	        $best = $null
133	        $sessionDirs = Get-ChildItem -Path $asScratchDir -Directory -Filter "session-*" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
134	        foreach ($dir in $sessionDirs) {
135	            $estimates = Get-ChildItem -Path $dir.FullName -Filter "*running-estimate*.json" -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
136	            foreach ($est in $estimates) {
137	                if (-not $best -or $est.LastWriteTime -gt $best.LastWriteTime) {
138	                    $best = $est
139	                }
140	            }
141	        }
142	        if ($best) { return $best.FullName }
143	    }
144	
145	    return $null
146	}

151	
152	function Get-PidFileForPort {
153	    param([int]$PortNum)
154	    return Join-Path $pidRegistryDir "$PortNum.pid"
155	}
156	
157	function Get-PortServerPid {
158	    param([int]$PortNum)
159	    $pf = Get-PidFileForPort -PortNum $PortNum
160	    if (Test-Path $pf) {
161	        $pidStr = Get-Content $pf -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
162	        if ($pidStr) {
163	            $pidStr = $pidStr.Trim()
164	            $pidInt = 0
165	            if ([int]::TryParse($pidStr, [ref]$pidInt)) {
166	                try {
167	                    $proc = Get-Process -Id $pidInt -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
168	                    if ($proc) { return $pidInt }
169	                } catch {}
170	            }
171	        }
172	        # Stale PID file -- clean up
173	        Remove-Item -Path $pf -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
174	    }
175	    return $null
176	}
177	
178	function Invoke-LegacyMigration {
179	    if (Test-Path $legacyPidFile) {
180	        $pidStr = Get-Content $legacyPidFile -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
181	        if ($pidStr) {
182	            $pidStr = $pidStr.Trim()
183	            $pidInt = 0
184	            if ([int]::TryParse($pidStr, [ref]$pidInt)) {
185	                try {
186	                    $proc = Get-Process -Id $pidInt -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
187	                    if ($proc) {
188	                        $newPf = Get-PidFileForPort -PortNum 8411
189	                        if (-not (Test-Path $newPf)) {
190	                            Copy-Item $legacyPidFile $newPf
191	                            Log "Migrated legacy PID $pidInt to port registry (8411)"
192	                        }
193	                    }
194	                } catch {}
195	            }
196	        }
197	        Remove-Item -Path $legacyPidFile -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
198	    }
199	}

201	function Get-RunningInstances {
202	    $instances = @()
203	    $pidFiles = Get-ChildItem -Path $pidRegistryDir -Filter "*.pid" -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
204	    foreach ($pf in $pidFiles) {
205	        $portName = $pf.BaseName
206	        $pidStr = Get-Content $pf.FullName -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
207	        if ($pidStr) {
208	            $pidStr = $pidStr.Trim()
209	            $pidInt = 0
210	            if ([int]::TryParse($pidStr, [ref]$pidInt)) {
211	                try {
212	                    $proc = Get-Process -Id $pidInt -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
213	                    if ($proc) {
214	                        $instances += [PSCustomObject]@{ Port = $portName; Pid = $pidInt }
215	                    } else {
216	                        Remove-Item -Path $pf.FullName -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
217	                    }
218	                } catch {
219	                    Remove-Item -Path $pf.FullName -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
220	                }
221	            }
222	        }
223	    }
224	    return $instances
225	}

243	function Test-InstanceHealth {

254	        }

260	    # 2. Data quality check: read the estimate via API
261	    $estimateJson = $null

263	        $apiResponse = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "http://localhost:$InstPort/api/estimate" -UseBasicParsing -TimeoutSec 5 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
264	        if ($apiResponse.StatusCode -eq 200) {
265	            $estimateJson = $apiResponse.Content
266	        }
267	    } catch {}
268	
269	    if ($estimateJson) {
270	        try {
271	            $d = $estimateJson | ConvertFrom-Json
272	            $missing = @()
273	            foreach ($f in @("delegationLog", "findings", "openThreads")) {
274	                if (-not ($d.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains $f)) {
275	                    $missing += $f
276	                }
277	            }
278	            if (-not ($d.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains "situation")) {
279	                $missing += "situation"
280	            } elseif ($d.situation) {
281	                foreach ($f in @("decisions", "assumptions", "deviations", "facts")) {
282	                    if (-not ($d.situation.PSObject.Properties.Name -contains $f)) {
283	                        $missing += "situation.$f"
284	                    }
285	                }
286	            }
287	
288	            $delCount = @($d.delegationLog).Count
289	            $findCount = @($d.findings).Count
290	            $threadCount = @($d.openThreads).Count
291	
292	            if ($missing.Count -gt 0) {
293	                $healthy = $false
294	                $missingStr = $missing -join ", "
295	                $details = "$details, missing fields: $missingStr ($delCount delegations, $findCount findings, $threadCount threads)".TrimStart(", ")
296	            } else {
297	                $details = "$details, $delCount delegations, $findCount findings, $threadCount threads".TrimStart(", ")
298	            }
299	        } catch {
300	            $details = "$details, estimate JSON parse error".TrimStart(", ")
301	            $healthy = $false
302	        }
303	    } elseif ($healthy) {
304	        $details = "$details, no /api/estimate endpoint (static mode?)".TrimStart(", ")
305	    }
306	
307	    if ($healthy) {
308	        LogOk "Dashboard on port ${InstPort}: HEALTHY ($details)"
309	    } else {
310	        LogWarn "Dashboard on port ${InstPort}: UNHEALTHY ($details)"
311	    }
312	
313	    return $healthy
314	}

372	                } catch {}
373	                $pf = Get-PidFileForPort -PortNum $inst.Port
374	                Remove-Item -Path $pf -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

376	            }
377	        }
378	    } else {
379	        # Stop specific port
380	        $pid = Get-PortServerPid -PortNum $Port
381	        if ($pid) {
382	            try {
383	                Stop-Process -Id $pid -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
384	            } catch {}
385	            $pf = Get-PidFileForPort -PortNum $Port
386	            Remove-Item -Path $pf -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
387	            LogOk "Stopped dashboard on port $Port (PID $pid)"
388	        } else {

390	        }
391	    }
392	    exit 0
393	}

395	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
396	# ACTION: Snapshot
397	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
398	if ($Snapshot) {
399	    $python = Find-Python
400	    if (-not $python) {
401	        LogError "python not found -- install Python to use the dashboard"
402	        Write-Summary "ERROR" "dashboard" "python not found"
403	        exit 1
404	    }
405	
406	    $generator = Find-Generator
407	    if (-not $generator) {
408	        LogError "generate-dashboard.py not found"
409	        Write-Summary "ERROR" "dashboard" "generator not found"
410	        exit 1
411	    }
412	
413	    if (-not $Estimate) {
414	        $Estimate = Find-Estimate
415	        if (-not $Estimate) {
416	            LogError "no running estimate found"
417	            Write-Summary "WARN" "dashboard" "no estimate found"
418	            exit 1
419	        }
420	    }
421	
422	    Log "Generating static dashboard snapshot..."
423	    $genArgs = @("$generator", "--estimate", "$Estimate")
424	    if ($OpenBrowser) { $genArgs += "--open" }
425	
426	    $result = & $python @genArgs 2>&1
427	    if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
428	        LogOk "Dashboard snapshot generated"
429	        Write-Summary "OK" "dashboard" "snapshot generated"
430	    } else {
431	        LogError "Dashboard generation failed"
432	        Write-Summary "ERROR" "dashboard" "generation failed"
433	        exit 1
434	    }
435	    exit 0
436	}
437	
438	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
439	# ACTION: Start (default)
440	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
441	
442	# Check if this port already has a running instance
443	$existingPid = Get-PortServerPid -PortNum $Port
444	if ($existingPid) {
445	    Log "Dashboard server already running on port $Port (PID $existingPid)"
446	    if (-not $Background) {
447	        Log "URL: http://localhost:$Port/"
448	    }
449	    Write-Summary "OK" "dashboard" "http://localhost:$Port/ (already running)"
450	    exit 0
451	}
452	
453	# Check if port is in use by something else
454	if (Test-PortInUse -TestPort $Port) {
455	    LogWarn "Port $Port is already in use by another process"
456	    Write-Summary "WARN" "dashboard" "port $Port in use"
457	    exit 1
458	}
459	
460	# Find dependencies
461	$python = Find-Python
462	if (-not $python) {
463	    LogError "python not found -- install Python to use the dashboard"
464	    Write-Summary "ERROR" "dashboard" "python not found"
465	    exit 1
466	}
467	
468	$generator = Find-Generator
469	if (-not $generator) {
470	    LogError "generate-dashboard.py not found"
471	    Write-Summary "ERROR" "dashboard" "generator not found"
472	    exit 1
473	}
474	
475	# Resolve estimate path
476	if (-not $Estimate) {
477	    $Estimate = Find-Estimate
478	    if (-not $Estimate) {
479	        if ($Background) {
480	            # Background mode: no estimate is not an error, just skip
481	            exit 0
482	        }
483	        LogError "no running estimate found"
484	        Log "Create a running estimate in .aitools\channel\running-estimate.json or .scratch\session-*\running-estimate*.json"
485	        Write-Summary "WARN" "dashboard" "no estimate found"
486	        exit 1
487	    }
488	}
489	
490	Log "Starting dashboard server on port $Port..."
491	Log "Estimate: $Estimate"
492	
493	$portPidFile = Get-PidFileForPort -PortNum $Port
494	
495	if ($Background) {
496	    # Background mode: Start-Process for detached process
497	    $proc = Start-Process -FilePath $python -ArgumentList @(
498	        "$generator", "--estimate", "$Estimate", "--serve", "--port", "$Port"
499	    ) -WindowStyle Hidden -PassThru -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
500	
501	    if ($proc) {
502	        # Write PID to port-keyed registry
503	        Set-Content -Path $portPidFile -Value $proc.Id -NoNewline
504	
505	        # Brief pause to let the server bind
506	        Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 300
507	
508	        # Verify server started
509	        try {
510	            $check = Get-Process -Id $proc.Id -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
511	            if ($check) {
512	                LogOk "Dashboard server started in background (PID $($proc.Id)) on port $Port"
513	                Log "URL: http://localhost:$Port/"
514	                Write-Summary "OK" "dashboard" "http://localhost:$Port/"
515	            } else {
516	                Remove-Item -Path $portPidFile -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
517	                LogError "Dashboard server failed to start"
518	                Write-Summary "ERROR" "dashboard" "failed to start"
519	                exit 1
520	            }
521	        } catch {
522	            Remove-Item -Path $portPidFile -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
523	            LogError "Dashboard server failed to start"
524	            Write-Summary "ERROR" "dashboard" "failed to start"
525	            exit 1
526	        }
527	    } else {
528	        LogError "Failed to launch dashboard server process"
529	        Write-Summary "ERROR" "dashboard" "launch failed"
530	        exit 1
531	    }
532	} else {
533	    # Foreground mode: server runs until Ctrl+C
534	    Set-Content -Path $portPidFile -Value $PID -NoNewline
535	
536	    # Register cleanup
537	    $cleanupBlock = {
538	        if (Test-Path $portPidFile) {
539	            Remove-Item -Path $portPidFile -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
540	        }
541	    }
542	    Register-EngineEvent -SourceIdentifier PowerShell.Exiting -Action $cleanupBlock | Out-Null
543	
544	    $genArgs = @("$generator", "--estimate", "$Estimate", "--serve", "--port", "$Port")
545	    if ($OpenBrowser) { $genArgs += "--open" }
546	
547	    Write-Summary "OK" "dashboard" "http://localhost:$Port/"
548	    & $python @genArgs
549	}

1	# aitools-install.ps1 -- Install aitools command + configure environment
2	# Run once for first-time setup, or re-run via `aitools` to stay current.
3	#
4	# Installs/updates gh CLI, configures repos directory, auto-detects Google
5	# Drive mounts, writes ~/.aitools/config.json, installs the
6	# aitools command to ~/.local/bin/, adds shell integration, and deploys
7	# all configuration scripts.
8	
9	param(
10	    [string]$ReposPath = "",

20	
21	Usage: .\scripts\aitools-install.ps1 [OPTIONS]
22	
23	Options:
24	  -ReposPath <string>       Set repos directory without prompting (default: ~/repos)
25	  -SkipDriveDetection       Skip Google Drive auto-detection
26	  -SkipGhAuth               Skip gh auth login
27	  -DryRun                   Preview mode -- show what would change without writing
28	  -Help                     Show this help
29	
30	Interactive behavior:
31	  When stdin is a terminal, prompts for repos path and drive confirmation.
32	  When piped or run non-interactively, uses defaults and flags.
33	  When config.json already exists, uses saved values without prompting.
34	"@

407	    if ($content -notmatch [regex]::Escape($marker)) {
