1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# setup-python.sh -- Manages Python via uv (unified manager, macOS/Linux)
3	# Safe to re-run -- idempotent.
4	#
5	# uv is the single source of truth for Python on BOTH macOS and Windows. This
6	# script installs the target Python via uv and makes it the default, so bare
7	# `python`/`python3` resolve to the uv-managed interpreter (shims in uv's bin
8	# dir, typically ~/.local/bin). Per-repo overrides use uv's normal mechanism
9	# (.python-version / `uv venv` / `uv run`) -- not a global rebind.
10	#
11	# Requires uv -- setup-uv.sh MUST run before this script.
12	#
13	# See reference/tool-registry.md for install source details.
14	
15	set -euo pipefail
16	
17	# --- Shared library ---
18	source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/aitools-lib.sh"
19	logging_init "setup-python"
20	
21	# --- OS guard ---
22	case "$(uname -s)" in
23	    MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*)
24	        log_error "This script is for macOS/Linux. On Windows, use ${SCRIPT_NAME}.ps1 instead."
25	        exit 1 ;;
26	esac
27	
28	# Target Python version (bump here for future upgrades; mirrors setup-python.ps1)
29	TARGET_PY_VERSION="3.14"
30	
31	# --- Require uv (the manager) ---
32	hash -r 2>/dev/null || true
33	if ! command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
34	    log_error "uv not found -- setup-uv.sh must run before setup-python.sh"
35	    write_summary ERROR "python" "uv not installed (ordering: uv before python)"
36	    exit 1
37	fi
38	
39	# --- Install/update the default Python via uv ---
40	# --default: install unversioned python/python3 executables into uv's bin dir.
41	# --preview-features python-install-default: silence the experimental warning and
42	#   pin the behavior (the --default flag is gated behind this preview feature).
43	log "Installing/updating uv-managed Python $TARGET_PY_VERSION as default..."
44	INSTALL_RC=0
45	INSTALL_OUTPUT=$(uv python install "$TARGET_PY_VERSION" --default --upgrade \
46	    --preview-features python-install-default 2>&1) || INSTALL_RC=$?
47	printf '%s\n' "$INSTALL_OUTPUT" | while IFS= read -r line; do
48	    [ -n "$line" ] && log "$line"
49	done
50	if [ "$INSTALL_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
51	    log_error "uv python install failed (see log above)"
52	    write_summary ERROR "python" "uv python install failed"
53	    exit 1
54	fi
55	
56	# --- Verify python3 resolves to the uv-managed interpreter ---
57	hash -r 2>/dev/null || true
58	if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
59	    PY_PATH=$(command -v python3)
60	    PY_VERSION=$(python3 --version 2>&1 || echo "version unknown")
61	    case "$PY_PATH" in
62	        *"/uv/"*|"$HOME/.local/bin/"*)
63	            log_ok "$PY_VERSION (uv-managed at $PY_PATH)"
64	            write_summary OK "python" "$PY_VERSION (uv)" ;;
65	        *)
66	            # python3 found, but not the uv shim -- PATH ordering issue
67	            log_warn "python3 resolves to $PY_PATH ($PY_VERSION), not the uv shim"
68	            log_warn "Ensure uv's bin dir (~/.local/bin) precedes /usr/bin in PATH"
69	            write_summary WARN "python" "$PY_VERSION (uv shim shadowed -- check PATH)"
70	            write_summary ACTION "" "Put ~/.local/bin before /usr/bin in PATH -- python3 default" ;;
71	    esac
72	else
73	    log_error "python3 not found after uv install -- is uv's bin dir (~/.local/bin) on PATH?"
74	    write_summary ERROR "python" "python3 not on PATH after uv install"
75	    write_summary ACTION "" "Add ~/.local/bin to PATH -- uv python shims"
76	fi
77	
78	# --- pip note ---
79	# uv-managed CPython bundles pip; prefer `uv pip` for project work.
80	if command -v pip3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
81	    log_ok "pip available: $(pip3 --version 2>/dev/null || echo 'version unknown')"
82	else
83	    log "pip not on PATH as a standalone command -- use 'uv pip' or 'python3 -m pip'"
84	fi
85	
86	# --- Exit ---
87	if [ "$ERRORS" -gt 0 ]; then
88	    log "FAILED with $ERRORS error(s)" "error"
89	    exit 1
90	elif [ "$WARNINGS" -gt 0 ]; then
91	    log "COMPLETED with $WARNINGS warning(s)" "warn"
92	    exit 0
93	else
94	    log "COMPLETED successfully" "ok"
95	    exit 0
96	fi

8	# Claude Code launcher with CLAUDE.md check
9	cc() {
10	  if [ ! -f "CLAUDE.md" ] && [ ! -f "CLAUDE.local.md" ]; then
11	    echo "No CLAUDE.md found in $(pwd)."
12	    printf "Create one with 'claude /init'? [y/N] "

14	    if [[ "$answer" =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then
15	      claude /init
16	    fi
17	  fi
18	  claude "$@"
19	}
20	
21	# Quick resume last session
22	alias ccr='claude -c'
23	
24	# Interactive session picker
25	alias ccs='claude --resume'
26	
27	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
28	# clip2md -- Clipboard -> Markdown with AI-powered naming
29	# Supports HTML (preferred, requires pandoc) and plain text (no pandoc needed).
30	# Optional: Claude Code CLI for auto-naming and summaries.
31	# macOS only (uses osascript/pbpaste for clipboard access).
32	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
33	
34	# Logging helper: appends to ~/Library/Logs/aitools/clip2md.log
35	_clip2md_log() {
36	  local logdir="$HOME/Library/Logs/aitools"
37	  mkdir -p "$logdir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
38	  local ts
39	  ts=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
40	  printf '[%s] %s\n' "$ts" "$1" >> "$logdir/clip2md.log" 2>/dev/null
41	}
42	
43	# AI helper: calls claude -p for filename + summary
44	# Outputs "filename|summary" on success, or "|summary" for summary_only mode.
45	# Returns non-zero on failure.
46	_clip2md_ai() {
47	  local md="$1"
48	  local summary_only="${2:-}"
49	
50	  local prompt='Name this clipboard content saved as markdown. Analyze the actual body, not just headers or subject lines.
51	
52	Filename rules:
53	- Lowercase, digits, hyphens only. No extension. Max 50 chars but shorter is better.
54	- Adapt to content type:
55	  Email/thread: compact-date-participant-topic (e.g. 250324-garcia-budget-review)
56	  Article/blog: source-topic (e.g. verge-ai-pricing)
57	  Docs: product-section (e.g. aws-iam-roles)
58	  Other: descriptive topic
59	- Dates: YYMMDD (e.g. 250324). Omit date if content has none.
60	- Be compact. Do not pad to fill 50 chars.
61	
62	Summary: one line, max 80 chars, what the content is actually about.
63	
64	Respond in EXACTLY this format with nothing else:
65	FILENAME|SUMMARY'
66	
67	  local result
68	  # type exempt: function-existence check with explicit fallback
69	  if type invoke_ai &>/dev/null; then
70	    result=$(printf '%s\n\n%s' "$prompt" "$md" | invoke_ai fast none) || return 1
71	  else
72	    # stderr suppressed: claude CLI may emit warnings; exit code checked via || return 1
73	    result=$(printf '%s' "$md" | claude -p "$prompt" --no-session-persistence 2>/dev/null) || return 1
74	  fi
75	
76	  # Normalize: strip newlines, trim whitespace
77	  result=$(printf '%s' "$result" | tr -d '\n' | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')
78	  if [ -z "$result" ]; then return 1; fi
79	
80	  # Parse on first pipe character
81	  local raw_name raw_summary
82	  if [[ "$result" == *"|"* ]]; then
83	    raw_name="${result%%|*}"
84	    raw_summary="${result#*|}"
85	  else
86	    raw_name="$result"
87	    raw_summary=""
88	  fi
89	  raw_name=$(printf '%s' "$raw_name" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')
90	  raw_summary=$(printf '%s' "$raw_summary" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')
91	
92	  # Truncate summary to 80 chars at word boundary
93	  if [ ${#raw_summary} -gt 80 ]; then
94	    raw_summary="${raw_summary:0:80}"
95	    local trimmed="${raw_summary% *}"
96	    if [ -n "$trimmed" ] && [ "$trimmed" != "$raw_summary" ]; then
97	      raw_summary="$trimmed"
98	    fi
99	  fi
100	
101	  if [ "$summary_only" = "summary_only" ]; then
102	    printf '|%s\n' "$raw_summary"
103	    return 0
104	  fi
105	
106	  # Sanitize filename: lowercase, alnum + hyphens only
107	  local name
108	  name=$(printf '%s' "$raw_name" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | \
109	    sed 's/[^a-z0-9-]/-/g; s/-\{2,\}/-/g; s/^-//; s/-$//')
110	
111	  # Truncate to 50 chars at hyphen boundary
112	  if [ ${#name} -gt 50 ]; then
113	    local truncated="${name:0:50}"
114	    local at_hyphen="${truncated%-*}"
115	    if [ -n "$at_hyphen" ] && [ "$at_hyphen" != "$truncated" ]; then
116	      name="$at_hyphen"
117	    else
118	      name="$truncated"
119	    fi
120	    name="${name%-}"
121	  fi
122	
123	  if [ -z "$name" ]; then name="clipboard"; fi
124	
125	  # Reserved names (cross-platform safety)
126	  case "$name" in
127	    con|prn|aux|nul|com[1-9]|lpt[1-9])
128	      name="clip-$name" ;;
129	  esac
130	
131	  printf '%s|%s\n' "$name" "$raw_summary"
132	}
133	
134	# Clipboard -> Markdown (HTML preferred, plain text fallback)
135	clip2md() {
136	  # macOS only (uses osascript/pbpaste for clipboard)
137	  if [ "$(uname -s)" != "Darwin" ]; then
138	    echo "clip2md: clipboard extraction requires macOS (uses osascript/pbpaste)" >&2
139	    echo "clip2md: on Windows, use the PowerShell version instead" >&2
140	    return 1
141	  fi
142	
143	  local md source_type
144	
145	  # Try HTML first (preferred -- richer formatting)
146	  local html
147	  html=$(osascript -e 'the clipboard as «class HTML»' 2>/dev/null | \
148	    perl -ne 'print chr foreach unpack("C*",pack("H*",substr($_,11,-3)))')
149	
150	  if [ -n "$html" ]; then
151	    # HTML path: requires pandoc
152	    if ! command -v pandoc &>/dev/null; then
153	      echo "clip2md: pandoc not found (needed for HTML). Run 'aitools install' or 'brew install pandoc'" >&2
154	      _clip2md_log "error: pandoc not found"
155	      return 1
156	    fi
157	
158	    # Strip Gmail noise (attrs, divs, nbsp)
159	    html=$(printf '%s' "$html" | perl -pe '
160	      s/\s*(style|class|target|saferedirecturl)="[^"]*"//gi;
161	      s/<\/?(div|span)[^>]*>//gi;
162	      s/&nbsp;/ /g')
163	
164	    # Convert via pandoc + clean output
165	    md=$(printf '%s' "$html" | pandoc -f html -t markdown | \
166	      perl -CSD -pe 's/\{=""\}//g; s/\x{00A0}/ /g; s/\x{202F}/ /g')
167	
168	    if [ -z "$md" ] || [ -z "$(printf '%s' "$md" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
169	      echo "clip2md: pandoc produced empty output" >&2
170	      _clip2md_log "error: pandoc produced empty output"
171	      return 1
172	    fi
173	    source_type="HTML"
174	  else
175	    # Plain text fallback (no pandoc needed)
176	    md=$(pbpaste 2>/dev/null)
177	    if [ -z "$md" ] || [ -z "$(printf '%s' "$md" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ]; then
178	      echo "clip2md: no content on clipboard (tried HTML and plain text)" >&2
179	      _clip2md_log "warning: no content on clipboard"
180	      return 1
181	    fi
182	    source_type="text"
183	  fi
184	
185	  # Word count (approximate, rounded to nearest 10)
186	  local word_count approx_words
187	  word_count=$(printf '%s' "$md" | wc -w | tr -d ' ')
188	  approx_words=$(( (word_count + 5) / 10 * 10 ))
189	  if [ "$approx_words" -eq 0 ] && [ "$word_count" -gt 0 ]; then
190	    approx_words="$word_count"
191	  fi
192	
193	  # Join all args as the output filename (supports multi-word names)
194	  local outfile=""
195	  if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
196	    outfile="$*"
197	  fi
198	
199	  # Determine output mode
200	  if [ -z "$outfile" ]; then
201	    # --- AUTO-NAME MODE ---
202	    if ! command -v claude &>/dev/null; then
203	      echo "clip2md: auto-naming requires Claude Code CLI. Provide a filename or install claude." >&2
204	      _clip2md_log "error: autoname requires Claude Code CLI"
205	      return 1
206	    fi
207	
208	    local temp_name=".clip2md-$$-$RANDOM.tmp"
209	    printf '%s' "$md" > "$temp_name"
210	    _clip2md_log "wrote temp $temp_name"
211	
212	    # Call claude for filename + summary
213	    local ai_result
214	    ai_result=$(_clip2md_ai "$md")
215	    local ai_exit=$?
216	
217	    if [ $ai_exit -ne 0 ] || [ -z "$ai_result" ]; then
218	      echo "clip2md: claude failed to generate filename" >&2
219	      _clip2md_log "error: claude failed"
220	      rm -f "$temp_name"
221	      _clip2md_log "cleanup: removed $temp_name"
222	      return 1
223	    fi
224	
225	    local base_name="${ai_result%%|*}"
226	    local summary="${ai_result#*|}"
227	
228	    # Collision avoidance
229	    local final_name="$base_name.md"
230	    local counter=2
231	    while [ -f "$final_name" ]; do
232	      final_name="$base_name-$counter.md"
233	      counter=$((counter + 1))
234	      if [ $counter -gt 100 ]; then break; fi
235	    done
236	
237	    mv "$temp_name" "$final_name"
238	    _clip2md_log "renamed $temp_name -> $final_name"
239	
240	    echo "Saved $final_name ($source_type, ~$approx_words words)"
241	    if [ -n "$summary" ]; then
242	      echo "  $summary"
243	    fi
244	    _clip2md_log "saved $final_name ($source_type, ~$approx_words words)"
245	  else
246	    # --- EXPLICIT NAME MODE ---
247	    # Ensure .md extension (strip if present, re-add)
248	    local name="${outfile%.[mM][dD]}.md"
249	
250	    # Check overwrite
251	    if [ -f "$name" ]; then
252	      printf '%s exists. Overwrite? [y/N] ' "$name"
253	      read -r answer
254	      if [[ ! "$answer" =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then
255	        echo "Aborted."
256	        _clip2md_log "aborted: user declined overwrite of $name"
257	        return 0
258	      fi
259	    fi
260	
261	    printf '%s' "$md" > "$name"
262	
263	    # Try AI summary if claude available
264	    local summary=""
265	    if command -v claude &>/dev/null; then
266	      local ai_result
267	      ai_result=$(_clip2md_ai "$md" "summary_only")
268	      if [ $? -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$ai_result" ]; then
269	        summary="${ai_result#|}"
270	      fi
271	    fi
272	
273	    echo "Saved $name ($source_type, ~$approx_words words)"
274	    if [ -n "$summary" ]; then
275	      echo "  $summary"
276	    fi
277	    _clip2md_log "saved $name ($source_type, ~$approx_words words)"
278	  fi
279	}
280

### L222 assistant 2026-06-17T18:16:11.621Z role=assistant
Confirmed the root cause — and it's not what the install warning claims. Here's the full picture.

## 1. Python troubleshooting

**Your real Terminal is fine.** Interactive login zsh resolves:
```
command -v python3  →  /Users/new-jose/.local/bin/python3  →  Python 3.14.6 (uv shim) ✓
```
The uv shim exists and is correct (`~/.local/bin/python3` → `~/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.14.../python3.14`). Interactively, `.local/bin` sits **before** `/opt/homebrew/bin`, so the uv interpreter wins. Python already works flawlessly when *you* type it.

**The install warning is a false alarm — and its remediation is wrong.** `aitools install` (and Claude Code's shell, and any hook/cron/MDM context) runs under a **different PATH** where `/opt/homebrew/bin` comes *first*:

| Context | `python3` resolves to |
|---------|----------------------|
| Interactive Terminal (login zsh) | `~/.local/bin/python3` → uv 3.14.6 ✓ |
| Non-interactive (install, hooks, Claude Code, cron) | `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3` → brew `python@3.14` 3.14.6 ✗ |

Why the split: the `.local/bin` prepend lives **only in `.zshrc`** (interactive), not `.zprofile` (login) — and anything that re-runs `brew shellenv` after it pushes `/opt/homebrew/bin` back to the front. `setup-python.sh:67-70` then sees brew's python and prints:
> `Ensure uv's bin dir (~/.local/bin) precedes /usr/bin in PATH`

That advice is **doubly wrong**: (a) `.local/bin` is already before `/usr/bin`, and (b) the actual shadow is `/opt/homebrew/bin`, which the message never mentions. You can't fix it by following it.

**Is it actually breaking anything?** Latently, not yet — brew's python is *also* 3.14.6 and the harness's python scripts (`ait-harvest.py`, dashboard, relay sync) are stdlib-only, so they run under either. The real problems are: (1) the design intent ("uv is the single Python") is silently violated in exactly the non-interactive contexts the harness relies on; (2) `uv pip`/`uv tool` packages install into the uv interpreter, so any future non-stdlib hook script would not see them; (3) the misleading, unactionable install noise on every run.

Two incidental findings from the probe:
- **`.zprofile:7` errors on every shell init** — `eval "$(/usr/local/bin/brew shellenv)"` fails (`no such file or directory: /usr/local/bin/brew`); there's no Intel Homebrew on this Apple Silicon Mac. Harmless but noisy; should be guarded or removed.
- Homebrew's `python@3.14` has **no dependents** (`brew uses --installed python@3.14` is empty) — so it's a direct/leftover install, not pulled in transitively. Removing it is *possible* but it's the wrong fix (brew could reinstall it; doesn't help the ordering principle).

### Fix options (pick scope — these are independent)
- **A. Own the PATH ordering in login + non-interactive contexts** (the real fix). Move the `~/.local/bin` prepend into `.zprofile`/`.bash_profile` *after* `brew shellenv`, via the aitools shell integration, so it survives across login and re-eval. Covers Terminals and most launchers. *(Caveat: bare hooks source no profile at all — see B.)*
- **B. Make the harness resolve Python deterministically**, not via PATH — prefer `~/.local/bin/python3` (or `uv run`) in `find_python`/hook shims. Covers hooks/cron where no profile is sourced.
- **C. Fix `setup-python.sh` detection + message** — compare against the *actual* first-on-PATH dir and emit accurate, actionable remediation (and recognize the brew-shadow case explicitly).
- **D. Clean up `.zprofile:7`** Intel-brew line.

My recommendation: **A + C now** (fixes the user-facing symptom and the ordering principle), **B as the robust follow-on** for hook contexts, **D** as a trivial cleanup. None of these are issue #7.

## 2. Managed tools + configs, and install order (macOS)

Dependency tiers — who actually needs whom:

```
TIER 0  FOUNDATION (must exist before the installer can function)
  Homebrew ──┬─ git              clone/pull repos          [assumed present]
             ├─ bash 5.x         all scripts run under bash; dodges macOS 3.2
             └─ (ships most Tier-2 bottles)

TIER 1  RUNTIMES the harness scripts THEMSELVES call
  node ──> npm, npx              `node -e` JSON plumbing in EVERY setup/deploy
   │                             script; profile-check.js; npx launches the
   │                             chrome-devtools MCP server
  uv ────> python3 (uv shim)     hooks (ait-harvest, session-catchup,
                                 harness-db, dashboard-serve), relay→AGENTS
                                 sync, generate-dashboard.py

TIER 2  LEAF TOOLS (managed, but no harness script needs them to run)
  gh · claude code · vercel · pandoc · rust/cargo · typst ·
  modal (needs uv) · go · pup/datadog · perl · ripgrep · cursor/agent

TIER 3  CONFIG DEPLOY (needs node + python from Tier 1)
  shell integration · ~/.claude/{CLAUDE.md, rules, settings.json, skills} ·
  ~/.cursor/{cli-config.json, mcp.json, skills, AGENTS.md} · hooks ·
  ~/.aitools/config.json · relay→AGENTS · ~/.local/bin/{aitools, hh}
```

**Current order vs. your instinct** (you're right — but for a sharper reason than "first is tidier"): node, uv, and python are *hidden hard dependencies of the installer and config-deploy steps themselves*, yet uv/python sit at the back behind pure leaf tools.

| Current step | Tool | Tier | Should be |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | node (→npx) | **1** | foundation — already early ✓ |
| 10–13 | vercel, pandoc, rust, typst | 2 | after Tier 1 |
| 14 | uv | **1** | move up next to node |
| 15 | python (via uv) | **1** | move up after uv |
| 16 | modal | 2 (needs uv) | after python ✓ |
| 17–19 | go, datadog, perl | 2 | after Tier 1 |
| 20 | bash | **0** | move to the front |

**Recommended order:** `brew → git → bash → node → uv → python` as a tight foundation block, *then* all leaf tools, *then* config deploy. This also helps fresh-machine runs (the v0.69.0 bash-3.2 crash class) and guarantees python exists before Step 21/22's python calls.

⚠️ One honest caveat: **reordering install steps does *not* fix the Python shadow** — that's a PATH-resolution problem (fix A/B/C), orthogonal to install sequence. The reorder is a cleanliness + fresh-machine-robustness win, not the python fix.

## 3. npx — yes, it's part of Node

`npx` (and `npm`) ship *inside* the Node.js distribution; there's no separate package or setup step. `which -a npx` → `/opt/homebrew/bin/npx` (the same brew node at v26.3.0). The harness depends on it for the **chrome-devtools MCP server** (`npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest --isolated`), so "npx works" == "node is installed and on PATH." It belongs in Tier 1 as a child of node, not as its own managed tool.

---

So: your Terminal's Python is fine; the install's warning is a non-interactive-PATH artifact with misleading advice; the real gap is that the harness's *own* non-interactive contexts use brew's Python instead of uv's.

Want me to implement the python fix? If so, which scope — **A+C** (PATH ownership + accurate detection, my recommendation), add **B** (deterministic resolution for hooks), and/or **D** (the `.zprofile` cleanup)? And separately, should I draft the install-step reorder, or keep that for later and start on #7?

Base directory for this skill: /Users/new-jose/repos/aitools/.claude/skills/tool-ops

## Intent

**Purpose**: Governed access to tool-ops.json — read operational
metadata, update governance modes, manage per-tool entries.
**Scope**: CRUD operations on tool-ops.json only. NOT the governance
principle (`.claude/rules/tool-ops.md`). NOT the framework documentation
(`reference/framework-tool-ops.md`). NOT per-tool ops references.
**Audience**: Agents checking tool behavior, `/audit` skill validating
ops coverage, setup scripts reading governance modes.

## Reading tool ops

To look up a tool's operational metadata:

1. Read `registries/tool-ops.json`
2. Find the tool key under `tools` (e.g., `tools.claude-code`)
3. Return the requested section: `governanceModes`, `denyRules`,
   `hooks`, `contextInjection`, `kpis`, `verifications`, `docAccess`,
   or `verificationMethod`

If the tool has no entry, report that it has no ops metadata. Most
managed tools do not need an ops entry — only those with deep harness
integration (hooks, deny rules, context injection).

### Common lookups

- **Deny rules**: `tools.<name>.denyRules` — what permission patterns
  are blocked and why
- **Hooks**: `tools.<name>.hooks` — what hooks fire for this tool,
  their event/matcher/script/purpose
- **Doc access**: `tools.<name>.docAccess` — how to read this tool's
  documentation (e.g., chrome-devtools vs WebFetch)
- **Governance modes**: `tools.<name>.governanceModes` — per-category
  audit/active status
- **Verifications**: `tools.<name>.verifications` — how to test hooks
  and deny rules

## Updating tool ops

### Governance mode changes

Mode changes follow observe-to-enforce graduation:

1. **Evidence**: Show zero-drift telemetry (SessionEnd hook data or
   manual audit) for the category being promoted
2. **Read** current entry via this skill
3. **Draft** the mode change: `"audit"` -> `"active"`
4. **Present** for user review (protected file gate)
5. **Write** if approved
6. Update `meta.lastUpdated`

Mode demotion (`active` -> `audit`) does not require evidence — it is
a safety action. Log the reason in the commit message.

### Adding/updating entries within a tool

For adding deny rules, hooks, KPIs, or verification cases:

1. Read the current tool entry
2. Draft the new/modified entry with all required fields
3. Present for user review
4. Write if approved
5. Update `meta.lastUpdated`

Required fields per section:

- **denyRules**: `id`, `permissionPattern`, `hook`, `reason`, `incidentRef`
- **hooks**: `event`, `matcher`, `script`, `purpose`
- **kpis**: `name`, `source`, `unit`
- **verifications**: `type`, `target`, `cases[]` (each with `input`,
  `expectExit`, `expectStdout`)

## Adding a new tool

Not every managed tool needs an ops entry. Create one only when:

- The tool has hooks that fire during sessions
- The tool has deny rules blocking specific permissions
- The tool requires special documentation access methods
- The tool has version-dependent behaviors that affect the harness

To add a new tool:

1. Create the tool key under `tools` with all governance modes set to
   `"audit"`
2. Populate at minimum: `governanceModes`, and whichever sections
   triggered the entry (e.g., `denyRules` if a deny rule was the cause)
3. Empty sections may be omitted — their absence means "no metadata
   for this category"
4. Present for user review
5. Write if approved
6. Update `meta.lastUpdated`
7. Create `reference/tool-ops-<toolname>.md` for the full ops reference
   (separate from the JSON registry)

## Cross-references

- Governance rule: `.claude/rules/tool-ops.md`
- Framework documentation: `reference/framework-tool-ops.md`
- Per-tool ops references: `reference/tool-ops-*.md`
- Framework registry: `reference/framework-registry.json`
- Governed data access pattern: `.claude/rules/governed-data-access.md`

- `http` requires `url` field
- `agent` requires `prompt` field

**Rule**: When reading web content that will be recorded verbatim
(install commands, config steps, API references), use the
chrome-devtools skill instead of WebFetch. WebFetch summarizes via a
smaller model and misses JS-rendered content. WebFetch is fine for
general research, blog posts, and quick fact-checks.

## Claude Code — Version Dependencies (CRITICAL)

is silently ignored. All Windows dispatch must use `pwsh -File` for PS1

**Impact of #2**: Session archive hook parses stdin JSON. If the contract

## Subagent Cross-Repo Access Restriction (#24)

Subagents launched via the Agent tool have restricted file access
outside the CWD repo:

- **Glob/Grep**: Denied outside CWD repo boundaries
- **Read**: Works with explicit absolute paths (even outside CWD repo)
- **Write/Edit**: Denied outside CWD repo

**Impact on delegation**: When delegating work that needs files from
another repo, include the file content in the delegation prompt
(inline via XML delimiters) rather than expecting the subagent to
read it. Alternatively, use Read with explicit paths for known
file locations.

## Agent Continuation Gap — SendMessage (#25)

Since v2.1.77, there is no working mechanism to send messages to a
previously spawned subagent:

- **Old mechanism** (`resume` parameter on Agent tool): Removed in
  v2.1.77. Had longstanding issues and was effectively non-functional
  before removal.
- **New mechanism** (`SendMessage` tool): Part of the Agent Teams
  feature set, gated behind `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS`
  (disabled by default). Even with the flag enabled, reports of
  unavailability.

**Impact on delegation patterns**:

- Subagents must be fully self-contained at launch. No follow-up
  messages possible.
- The Agent tool's own return value includes `agentId` with
  instructions to use SendMessage — the model will attempt to use
  it and fail.
- Sequential delegation (launch new agent with prior agent's output)
  is the only working pattern for iterative subagent work.

**Workaround**: Include all context in the initial Agent launch
prompt. Use TaskOutput to read completed agent results. Launch new
agents for follow-up work, passing prior output as context.

Upstream: #35240, #37051, #38183

## Session Management Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `claude -c` | Resume most recent session in current directory |
| `claude --resume` | Interactive session picker (current directory only) |
| `claude --resume "name"` | Resume a named session |
| `/resume` | Switch sessions from inside a running session |
| `/rename <name>` | Name the current session for easy recall |
| `claude --continue --fork-session` | Fork current session into a new one |

Sessions are local to each machine and tied to the directory they were
started in. They do not sync across devices.

## CLAUDE.md Hierarchy (5 levels)

| Level | Path | Scope |
|-------|------|-------|
| Managed (org/IT) | `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md` | All users on machine |
| User (personal global) | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` | You, all projects, this machine |
| Project (team) | `./CLAUDE.md` in repo root | All team members via git |
| Project (personal) | `./CLAUDE.local.md` | You only, auto-gitignored |
| Subdirectory | `./some-dir/CLAUDE.md` | Loaded on-demand when working in that dir |

All levels merge together. More specific wins on conflict.

## Hook Portability Rules

Hooks (`shared/hooks/*.sh`) run in bash on ALL platforms — macOS,
Linux, and Windows Git Bash. They must be portable across all bash
environments. Hooks cannot source `aitools-lib.sh` or `check-lib.sh`
— they are standalone deployed files.

### Known command divergences

| Command | macOS (BSD) | Linux/Git Bash (GNU) | Correct Pattern |
|---------|-------------|---------------------|-----------------|
| `stat` modification time | `stat -f %m file` | `stat -c %Y file` | `uname -s` dispatch |
| `stat` birth time | `stat -f %B file` | `stat -c %W file` (0 if unsupported) | `uname -s` dispatch |
| `stat` formatted date | `stat -f "%SB" -t "%Y-%m-%d"` | `date -d "@$(stat -c %Y)"` | `uname -s` dispatch |
| `find` formatted output | `find -printf` not available | `find -printf '%T@'` | Use `find -print0` + `stat` loop |
| `grep` Perl regex | Not available | `grep -P` | Use `perl -ne` or `grep -E` |
| `date` parsing | `date -j -f fmt` | `date -d string` | `uname -s` dispatch |

**Never use the fallback chain pattern** `stat -f %m "$file" || stat -c %Y "$file"`.
On Git Bash, GNU `stat -f` means `--file-system` (not format). It
partially succeeds with wrong multiline output, contaminating the
variable.

## Claude Code — Verification

Hook and deny rule testing uses mock-json-pipe:

```bash
echo '{"tool_name":"Agent","tool_input":{"subagent_type":"claude-code-guide"}}' | bash block-claude-code-guide.sh
# Expected: exit 0, stdout contains "permissionDecision.*deny"

echo '{"tool_name":"Agent","tool_input":{"subagent_type":"Explore"}}' | bash block-claude-code-guide.sh
# Expected: exit 0, no stdout (not blocked)
```

## Windows Shell Limitations

CC on Windows is hardcoded to Git Bash. The `CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL`
environment variable is broken (silently ignored).

**Working workarounds**:

- Run PS1 commands: `pwsh -NoProfile -Command 'Your-Command Here'`
- Run PS1 scripts: `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "path/to/script.ps1"`
- Quoting rule: Always single-quote the outer `-Command` string.
  Use double quotes inside for PS interpolation.
- For complex PS1: Write to a temp `.ps1` file, execute with `-File`.

## `claude update` Hook Cancellation (#23)

`claude update` starts a transient session. When it completes,
SessionEnd hooks fire but CC immediately cancels them. Observed
output: `SessionEnd hook [...] failed: Hook cancelled`.

**Impact**: None. The hooks exit before doing real work (no session
dir exists for the transient update session). This is benign noise.

### L296 assistant 2026-06-17T18:34:45.722Z role=assistant
Both live fixes are in and verified: `agent` → Cursor CLI `2026.05.21-f84ab11`, `grok` still → `grok 0.2.51`. ⚠️ One caveat — this live fix isn't *durable* yet: `~/.grok/bin` still precedes `~/.local/bin` on PATH, so if grok's updater recreates `~/.grok/bin/agent`, grok reclaims the name. The durable fix is the PATH-ownership work below.

Here's the full picture and a plan.

## Where shell integration happens **today** (your #2 question)

| Concern | Location | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| macOS/Linux integration | `aitools-install.sh` Step 7 (L464-491) | Appends `# aitools shell integration` + `source aliases.sh` to `~/.bashrc` and `~/.zshrc` |
| Windows integration | `aitools-install.ps1` Step 7 (L364-429) | Marked block in `$PROFILE`: `. aliases.ps1` + `function aitools`/`hh` |
| Sourced content | `shared/shell/aliases.sh` / `.ps1` | `DD_SITE`, `cc()`, `clip2md`, `ccr`/`ccs` — **no PATH management at all** |

So today the harness **owns zero PATH ordering**. It only appends a `source` line to your `*.rc` files. PATH order on your Mac is incidental — `brew shellenv` (`.zprofile`) + manual prepends from the grok/antigravity/claude/uv installers (`.zshrc`). That's why `python3` and `agent` resolution is fragile. Two more gaps I found:
- Step 7 is **inline in the installer** — there's no `setup-user-shell.{sh,ps1}`, and `build-deploy.sh` embeds nothing for it, so the **MDM/deploy path never sets up shell integration**.
- The Windows block uses a begin-marker + "following non-empty lines" as its boundary — **no explicit END marker** (fragile).

## tool-ops finding (your #3 recollection)

I loaded both skills + re-confirmed the rules. The "everything we manage should be used by the harness" work was **not** started in tool-ops. `registries/tool-ops.json` contains exactly **one** tool — `claude-code` — and only covers CC's deny rules / hooks / governance modes. tool-ops is about *Claude Code behavior governance*, not *which binary a managed tool resolves to*. The pieces that actually exist for this are:
- `registries/tool-registry.json` — install methods + paths (the right home for "canonical path per managed tool").
- `aitools-lib.{sh,ps1}` — `ensure_tool_on_path`, `find_python` (dashboard), `KnownPaths` (build prereqs). These are the seeds of deterministic resolution, but they're scattered and PATH-lookup-based, not "use the managed copy."

So the principle is real but unimplemented. I'd record the managed-binary expectation in **tool-registry** and implement a single resolver in **aitools-lib** — not in tool-ops.

## The plan (no tiers — flat, concrete)

**Canonical PATH order aitools should own** (macOS), highest-precedence first:
```
~/.local/bin        # uv python3/pip · agent→cursor · claude · modal · aitools · hh   ← WINS over brew
/opt/homebrew/bin   # node · npm · npx · uv · vercel · pandoc · typst · go · pup · bash · rg · git
/opt/homebrew/sbin
<macOS system paths>
~/.cargo/bin · ~/go/bin
# grok/antigravity bins go AFTER ~/.local/bin so they can't reclaim `agent`
```
The key move: **`~/.local/bin` before `/opt/homebrew/bin`** — that single ordering makes the uv-managed `python3` *and* `cursor-agent` win deterministically, in interactive **and** non-interactive shells.

**Install/criticality order** you described, applied to the 22 steps: `brew (+git+bash) → node → uv → python3 → claude → agent(cursor)+rg → gh, vercel, pandoc, rust, typst, modal, go, datadog, perl → deploy configs`. (Currently uv/python are at 14/15, behind vercel/pandoc/rust/typst — they move up.)

**Work items, batched** (each batch = verify before next, per your smaller-batches preference):

| Batch | Files | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Shell ownership | new `setup-user-shell.{sh,ps1}`, `aitools-install.{sh,ps1}` Step 7, `build-deploy.sh`, `aliases.sh/.ps1` | Extract Step 7 into a dedicated script; write a **`# >>> aitools managed >>>` … `# <<< aitools managed <<<`** block in the login profile (`.zprofile`/`.bash_profile`) that sets the canonical PATH order; embed in deploy/ |
| 2. Deterministic resolution | `aitools-lib.{sh,ps1}`, dashboard scripts, hook shims, relay sync | One resolver that returns the **managed** `python3` (uv shim / `uv run`), used by all harness python callers |
| 3. Detection/message fixes | `setup-python.{sh,ps1}`, `setup-go.{sh,ps1}`, `setup-user-cursor.{sh,ps1}` | Accurate shadow detection + remediation; fold GOPATH/bin into the managed block; **fix Cursor detection** (verify `agent` is cursor, not grok) + manage the `agent→cursor-agent` symlink durably |
| 4. Install reorder | `aitools-install.{sh,ps1}` | Reorder steps to the criticality order above |
| 5. Docs (protected) | new `reference/ait-shellintegration.md`; `CLAUDE.md`/glossary if `agent` naming changes; `RELEASE_NOTES.md` | Document the managed block + PATH order for all platforms |

This is 10+ files across cross-platform pairs and touches protected files — so per this repo's plan-execution rule I'd capture it as a `plans/*.md` and execute batch-by-batch with verbatim diffs + the error-handling audit, and present the protected changes (the new reference's intent, any CLAUDE.md/glossary edits) for your review before writing.

## Decisions I need before building (my recommendation first)

1. **PATH precedence** — put `~/.local/bin` *before* `/opt/homebrew/bin`? **Recommend: yes** (it's what makes uv-python + cursor-agent win).
2. **Block location** — PATH/env block in the **login profile** (`.zprofile`/`.bash_profile`), keep `aliases.sh` sourcing in the interactive `*.rc`? **Recommend: yes.**
3. **brew shellenv** — let the aitools block run `brew shellenv` then prepend `~/.local/bin` (superseding your current `.zprofile` lines 1-5)? **Recommend: yes** (deterministic, owned).
4. **`agent` naming** — keep `agent` = Cursor (harness convention) with the harness managing the symlink + detection? **Recommend: yes** (matches your request); alternative is standardizing on `cursor-agent` and dropping `agent`.
5. **grok** — leave grok unmanaged (run as `grok`), just ensure our PATH block outranks `~/.grok/bin`? **Recommend: yes.**
6. **Capture as `plans/ait-shell-integration.md` and file a tracking issue** (separate from #7)? **Recommend: yes.**

Confirm these (or adjust), and I'll write the plan doc + start Batch 1. Want me to proceed?

### L310 user 2026-06-17T18:39:52.085Z role=user
Base directory for this skill: /Users/new-jose/repos/aitools/.claude/skills/tool-registry

## Intent

**Purpose**: Provide governed access to the tool registry — reading
tool entries, adding new entries, updating install methods, and
tracking versions. **Scope**: Registry data operations only. NOT the
evaluation process (use `/tool-eval`). NOT lifecycle gates or
onboarding checklists (`@.claude/rules/tool-lifecycle.md`).
**Audience**: Any agent that needs to look up a tool's install method,
verify a version, or write a registry entry after evaluation.

## Reading tool entries

1. Read `@registries/tool-registry.json`
2. Find the tool in `tools.<slug>` (CLI tools) or `mcpServers.<slug>` (MCP servers)
3. Present: displayName, source, purpose, install methods per platform,
   lifecycle (platformStatus, concurrency, postInstallConfig, dependencies,
   invocation), versions (per-platform lastVerified), authentication (if
   present), notes, pathIssues, platformGotchas
4. For MCP servers: also present transport, auth, scope, installClaudeCode
5. If any platform version is null, note it as "not yet verified"

## Adding or updating a tool entry

Prerequisite: evaluation completed via `/tool-eval` skill, or user
provides the exact content to write.

1. Verify all required data fields are present:
   - **source** — official project URL
   - **purpose** — what the tool does and why we manage it
   - **install** — per platform: preferred method, command,
     update command, version check
   - **delivery** — per platform: package maintainer, upstream
     source, official endorsement, provenance verified date
   - **health** — per platform: flag (green/yellow/red) with reasons
   - **lifecycle** — platform status, concurrency, post-install
     config, dependencies, invocation command and anti-patterns
   - **versions** — per platform: last verified version and date
   - **maintenance** — harness, last run per platform, workarounds,
     upstream risks
   - **evaluation** — status (current/stale/pending-migration),
     provenance file link, pending changes description
   - **authentication** — if required: method, setup/status/refresh
     commands, token storage, env var override, auth0 migration phase
2. Verify all required onboarding artifacts exist or are planned:
   - **Setup scripts** — `scripts/setup-<tool>.sh` + `.ps1`
   - **Installer integration** — step in `aitools-install.sh/.ps1`
   - **Build pipeline** — copy block in `build-deploy.sh`
   - **Tool skill** — `shared/skills/<tool>/SKILL.md`
   - **Check script entries** — `TOOL_CMDS` dictionary in check scripts
   - **CLAUDE.md entries** — Managed CLI Tools table + deploy list
   - **Evaluation provenance** — `reference/evaluations/<tool>-*.md`
3. Draft the registry entry
4. Present for review — protected per `@.claude/rules/sources-of-truth.md`
5. Write if approved

## Updating version tracking

When a tool is verified on a platform:

1. Read `@registries/tool-registry.json`
2. Navigate to `tools.<slug>.versions.<platform>`
3. Update `lastVerifiedVersion` and `lastVerified`
4. For MCP servers: update `mcpServers.<slug>.versions.lastReviewed`
5. Update `meta.lastUpdated` to today's date
6. Present for review (protected file)
7. Write if approved

## Schema

`registries/tool-registry.json` uses `schemaVersion: "1.0"`. Top-level
keys: `meta`, `tools`, `mcpServers`, `mcpManagement`, `overrides`.
Key sections per CLI tool (`tools.<slug>`):

| Section | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `install` | Per-platform preferred method + alternatives |
| `delivery` | Provenance: who maintains the package, upstream source, endorsement |
| `health` | Per-platform green/yellow/red flags with reasons |
| `evaluation` | Status (current/stale/pending-migration), provenance link |
| `lifecycle` | Platform status, concurrency, config, dependencies, invocation |
| `versions` | Per-platform verified version + date |
| `maintenance` | Harness, workarounds (with severity), upstream risks |
| `authentication` | Auth method, commands, token storage, Auth0 migration phase |
| `nonPreferredMethods` | Cleanup targets for setup scripts |
| `buildPrereqs` | Per-platform build dependencies |
| `knownPaths` | Verified install paths for PATH fallback detection |
| `overrides` | Intentional deviations from upstream defaults |

## When to invoke /tool-registry

- Checking a tool's install method, version, or health status
- Adding a new tool entry (after `/tool-eval` completes)
- Updating an existing entry's fields or version
- User says /tool-registry or /tools

## Cross-References

- Evaluation process: `/tool-eval` skill
- Evaluation principles: `@.claude/rules/tool-evaluation.md`
- Lifecycle gates: `@.claude/rules/tool-lifecycle.md`
- Registry data: `@registries/tool-registry.json`
- Evaluation research: `reference/evaluations/`

1	# Tool Operations
2	
3	**Intent**: **Purpose**: Document the SRE-grounded discipline behind
4	tool-ops — why per-tool operational metadata exists, how
5	observe-to-enforce graduation works, and how tool-ops connects to
6	the broader harness. **Scope**: Discipline source, adoption rationale,
7	and maintenance guidance. NOT the ops data (`/tool-ops` skill). NOT
8	the governance principle (`.claude/rules/tool-ops.md`). **Audience**:
9	Agents understanding why tool-ops exists, harness architects extending
10	the framework.
11	
12	## Source Discipline
13	
14	Three disciplines converge:
15	
16	- **SRE operational readiness** — production services maintain runbooks
17	  with dependency maps, alerting rules, and verification procedures.
18	  Tools with deep harness integration need the same: deny rules, hook
19	  specifications, context injection patterns, and verification specs.
20	- **Hook-rollout observe-to-enforce** — from release engineering's
21	  canary deployment pattern. New operational metadata starts in audit
22	  mode (logged, not enforced), graduates to active after zero-drift
23	  verification. This prevents untested governance from breaking
24	  sessions.
25	- **Lean pull systems** — entries are created on demand when a tool
26	  earns deep integration, not speculatively for every managed tool.
27	  Most tools need only a tool-registry entry. Tool-ops entries exist
28	  only when operational complexity justifies them.
29	
30	## How We Adopted It
31	
32	- **Operational readiness** -> per-tool ops references
33	  (`reference/tool-ops-*.md`) that consolidate scattered operational
34	  knowledge — deny rules, hooks, context injection, KPIs, version
35	  dependencies — into a single governed location per tool.
36	- **Observe-then-enforce** -> governance modes in `tool-ops.json`.
37	  Each metadata category (denyRules, hooks, contextInjection, kpis,
38	  versionDeps, verifications) has its own mode: `audit` (logged,
39	  advisory) or `active` (enforced, blocking). Categories promote
40	  independently based on zero-drift evidence.
41	- **Pull systems** -> tool-ops entries are created when a tool's
42	  operational complexity causes incidents, scattered knowledge, or
43	  repeated agent mistakes. Claude Code was the first entry — its deny
44	  rules, hooks, and version dependencies were scattered across
45	  multiple harness files before consolidation.
46	
47	## How It's Maintained
48	
49	- Governance modes tracked in `registries/tool-ops.json` per tool,
50	  per category
51	- SessionEnd hook (`tool-ops-session-audit.sh`) collects drift
52	  telemetry: did deny rules fire? Did hooks behave as specified?
53	  Did agents access docs via the correct method?
54	- Zero-drift across sessions promotes `audit` -> `active`
55	- Mode changes require `/tool-ops` skill (governed data access)
56	- New tools enter with all categories in `audit` mode
57	
58	## Implementing Artifacts
59	
60	- `.claude/rules/tool-ops.md` (governance rule — always in context)
61	- `.claude/skills/tool-ops/SKILL.md` (governed access to registry)
62	- `registries/tool-ops.json` (registry — per-tool metadata)
63	- `reference/tool-ops-*.md` (per-tool ops references — full detail)
64	- `shared/hooks/tool-ops-session-audit.sh` (SessionEnd drift telemetry)
65	
66	## Cross-References
67	
68	- Framework registry: `@registries/framework-registry.json`
69	- Three-layer governance: `@reference/framework-three-layer-governance.md`
70	- Hook rollout (observe-to-enforce source): `@reference/framework-hook-rollout.md`
71	- Tool lifecycle (install/version tracking): `@reference/framework-tool-lifecycle.md`
72	- Governed data access (skill-gate pattern): `@reference/framework-governed-data-access.md`
73

### L323 assistant 2026-06-17T18:41:46.795Z role=assistant
I've now got both registries and the tool-ops framework in front of me. Here's the deconstruction, grounded in what actually exists today — and it surfaces a few real discrepancies.

## What the two registries do today

**`tool-registry.json`** — the **identity + supply chain** record. Every managed tool has an entry. Its intent says explicitly: *"NOT per-tool ops metadata (tool-ops.json)."* Per tool it holds: `install` (per-platform method/command), `update`, `versionCheck`, `versions` (per-platform last-verified), `lifecycle` (`platformStatus`, `concurrency`, `postInstallConfig`, `dependencies`, **`invocation: {command, antiPatterns}`**), `authentication`, `knownPaths`, `nonPreferredMethods`, `pathIssues`, `platformGotchas`. This is "how we get it, keep it current, and whether it's supported."

**`tool-ops.json`** — the **operational governance** record. Only `claude-code` exists. Sections: `governanceModes` (per-category audit/active), `denyRules`, `hooks`, `contextInjection`, `kpis`, `verifications`, `docAccess`. Framework rationale (`framework-tool-ops.md`) is SRE runbooks + observe-to-enforce + **lean pull**: *"Most tools need only a tool-registry entry. Tool-ops entries exist only when operational complexity justifies them."*

So the split today is: **registry = all tools; tool-ops = only tools with deep integration (so far, just CC's hooks/deny rules).**

## The gap — and three bugs the registry already carries

Your instinct is right, but there's a missing *third* concern that neither registry captures: **resolution** — "when the harness runs `python3`, which interpreter does it get?" Look at the `python` entry (lines 610-658):

1. **`lifecycle.postInstallConfig`** says *"~/.local/bin must precede **/usr/bin** in PATH so the uv shim wins."* That's the **same wrong diagnosis** as `setup-python.sh:68` — the real shadow is `/opt/homebrew/bin`, not `/usr/bin`. The registry is propagating the bug.
2. **`knownPaths: null`** — the one tool whose resolution is most fragile records *no* managed path. Compare `bash` (lines 421-425), which is *less* fragile yet has `knownPaths` populated.
3. **`lifecycle.invocation.command`** = `"python3 / python (uv-managed shims)"` — prose, not machine-usable, and nothing in the harness reads it. So "use the managed copy" is documented as intent but **never enforced or verified**.

Net: a tool can be marked `platformStatus: supported` (python is, macOS, verified 2026-06-15) while the harness silently runs a *different* interpreter in its own hooks. Supported ≠ resolved-correctly. Nothing closes that gap.

## The model I'd propose (the boundary rule)

Keep the two registries' scopes, add resolution to tool-ops, and use one discriminator:

> **A tool gets a tool-ops entry when the harness itself depends on it operationally** — either (a) the harness *invokes* it (resolution concern), or (b) it has governance hooks/deny rules. User-facing-only tools stay registry-only (lean pull).

| Concern | Lives in | Applies to |
|---|---|---|
| Identity, install, version, health, supported-status | **tool-registry** | every managed tool |
| Resolution contract + governance (hooks, deny, verifications) | **tool-ops** | tools the harness *runs* or *governs* |

By that rule, the harness-invoked set earns tool-ops entries: **python, node (+npx/npm), bash, perl, uv, claude-code (extend), agent/cursor**. The user-facing-only set stays registry-only: typst, pandoc, vercel, go, modal, pup, gh, rust. That honors the framework's lean-pull principle while expanding past claude-code exactly as you want.

## python3-via-uv, deconstructed end-to-end

**Lifecycle → registry → tool-ops → harness:**

1. **Evaluate** (`/tool-eval`) → method = uv. **2. Phase-2 gate** → approved.
2. **Onboard** (`tool-lifecycle.md` checklist): registry entry, `setup-python.{sh,ps1}`, installer step, build-deploy block, CLAUDE.md row. *(all exist)*
3. **Mark supported/tested (macOS)** → `versions.macos` set, `platformStatus: supported`. **← today the flow stops here, and resolution is never checked.**
4. **Missing step — resolution:** because the harness *invokes* `python3` (ait-harvest, session-catchup, harness-db, dashboard, relay sync), it earns a **tool-ops entry** + a **resolution verification** that must pass before "supported" is truthful.

**Proposed `tool-ops.json` → `python` entry** (the second entry after claude-code):
```jsonc
"python": {
  "manager": "uv",
  "governanceModes": { "resolution": "audit", "verifications": "audit" },
  "resolution": {
    "canonicalCommands": ["python3", "python", "pip3"],
    "managedPath": { "macos": "~/.local/bin/python3", "windows": "%USERPROFILE%\\.local\\bin\\python3.exe", "linux": "~/.local/bin/python3" },
    "pathPrecedence": "~/.local/bin MUST precede /opt/homebrew/bin (macOS) and any system python dir",
    "invocationContract": "Harness resolves python via the managed shim or `uv run` — never a bare PATH lookup (Homebrew python@3.x shadows the uv shim when /opt/homebrew/bin precedes ~/.local/bin).",
    "harnessConsumers": ["ait-harvest.py","session-catchup.sh","harness-db-*.sh","dashboard-serve.sh","generate-dashboard.py","sync-relay-to-cursor-agents.py"]
  },
  "verifications": [{
    "type": "resolution-check",
    "cases": [{ "command": "python3 -c 'import sys; print(sys.executable)'", "expectContains": "/.local/share/uv/python/" }]
  }]
}
```

**Registry fixes** (same change, two correctness bugs): `python.lifecycle.postInstallConfig` → `/opt/homebrew/bin` (not `/usr/bin`); `python.knownPaths.macos` → `["~/.local/bin/python3"]`. tool-ops `resolution.managedPath` *references* that, so the install fact lives in one place.

**Harness consumption:** a single resolver in `aitools-lib.{sh,ps1}` (e.g. `harness_python` / `Resolve-ManagedTool`) returns the managed shim (or `uv run`), seeded by the resolution contract; the hooks/dashboard/relay callers use it instead of bare `python3`. That's what makes "everything we manage is used by the harness" *true and testable*, not just documented.

## The lifecycle change that wires it together

Add one gate to `tool-lifecycle.md`'s onboarding checklist:

> When marking a tool `supported` on a platform: if the harness invokes the tool, a **tool-ops `resolution` entry** and a **passing resolution verification** are required. "Supported" means *installed, current, and resolving to the managed copy in the harness's own (non-interactive) context.*

That single rule is what would have caught the python shadow before it shipped.

## Decisions to confirm (my rec first)

1. **Boundary** — tool-ops entry = "harness invokes it OR governs it"; user-facing-only tools stay registry-only. **Rec: yes.**
2. **Resolution lives in tool-ops** (new `resolution` section + `resolution` governance mode), referencing registry `knownPaths` for the path. **Rec: yes** (vs. cramming it into registry `invocation`).
3. **Fix the registry python facts** (precedence + `knownPaths`) as part of this. **Rec: yes** — it's a live correctness bug.
4. **Lifecycle gate** added as above. **Rec: yes.**
5. **First implementation = python/uv end-to-end** (registry fix + tool-ops entry + resolver + verification), then replicate to node/bash/perl/uv/claude/agent. **Rec: yes** — prove the pattern on one tool.

All four artifacts here (`tool-registry.json`, `tool-ops.json`, `tool-lifecycle.md`, `framework-tool-ops.md`) are protected, so I'll present concrete diffs for review before writing regardless.

Confirm the model (especially #1 and #2 — they shape everything), and I'll fold this into the plan doc alongside the shell-integration/PATH work and start with python/uv as the reference implementation.

### L343 assistant 2026-06-17T18:52:50.353Z role=assistant
This is foundational enough to get right before any code. Here's where I land on each — including where I'd push back.

## 1. Every managed tool gets a tool-ops entry — agree, with a reframe

You've convinced me; drop my lean-pull boundary. The clean mental model:

- **tool-registry** = supply chain: *what it is, where it comes from, what version, is it supported.*
- **tool-ops** = operations: *where it resolves, how we verify it, how we govern it.*

Every managed tool has both, so **tool-ops.tools should be 1:1 with tool-registry.tools**. Baseline entry for every tool = `resolution` ("installed here, called on this path") + `verification`. The richer sections (denyRules, hooks, contextInjection) stay **optional** — present only when a tool earns them. So lean-pull doesn't die; it just moves from *"does the tool get an entry"* (now: always) to *"which optional sections does it carry."* That 1:1 invariant is also a free audit: `tool-ops-session-audit.sh` can assert every registry tool has an ops entry.

One consequence: `framework-tool-ops.md` currently justifies tool-ops with *"most tools need only a registry entry"* — that rationale has to be rewritten. It's protected, so that's a reviewed edit.

## 2. governanceModes — drop the blanket, keep the canary

Mostly agree. The per-category `governanceModes` block (six audit/active flags on every tool) is ceremony for resolution/verification — those are **inherent**: if we manage it, we own resolving and verifying it, always-on, advisory by default. No mode needed.

**But don't throw out observe→enforce entirely** — it's load-bearing for exactly one thing: rules that can *block a session*. The `claude-code` deny rule traces to an incident (#34730) where a bad rule disabled all hooks; the audit→active graduation is the canary that prevents shipping a blocking rule untested. So:

- Drop `governanceModes` as a per-tool object.
- Keep a single `enforcement: "audit" | "active"` field **only on entries that actually block** (deny rules, and any future "hard-fail resolution"). It lives on the rule, not as a separate modes map.

Net: resolution + verification are always-on and advisory; only blocking rules carry a graduation flag. That matches your instinct without losing the safety mechanism.

## 3. harnessConsumers — drop it, invert it (agree, strongly)

A provider-side "who calls me" list drifts the moment someone adds a caller. Declare the dependency **at the consumer**: each artifact's own metadata says `usesManagedTools: [python, node, ...]`. Then "who consumes python?" is a **derived query** over artifact metadata, never a stored list. This is just locality-of-dependency, and — critically — it's the same mechanism as your #4. Which is the bridge:

## 4. Artifact registry — yes, but generated, not authored (this is the whole ballgame)

I'm in, with one non-negotiable design constraint and a couple of honest cautions.

**The constraint: it must be a DERIVED index, never a hand-maintained source of truth.** The filesystem already enumerates files. A hand-authored registry of every file would instantly become the highest-drift artifact in the repo and turn net-negative. The value isn't the file list — it's the **metadata + relationships**, and that metadata has to live *in each artifact* (header), with the registry **generated by a scan** (treated like `deploy/` — regenerated, never edited). Get this backwards and the whole thing rots.

**This already exists in fragments — you're unifying, not inventing:**
- `shared/hooks/hooks-manifest.json` is a working mini artifact-registry for *one* class (hooks): file + metadata (event/matcher) + generator-consumer wiring (setup scripts, build-deploy, check step 32). It's the proof-of-concept; the artifact registry generalizes its pattern to every class.
- `framework-registry.json` already hand-maintains `artifacts: [...]` per framework — and it's *already drifting*: line 183 still lists `reference/tool-ops.json`, but the v0.69.0 consolidation moved it to `registries/tool-ops.json`. That stale pointer is exactly the bug a generated registry catches — and it's the same inversion as #3: artifacts should declare *which framework they implement*, making framework→artifacts derived.
- `sources-of-truth.md`'s protected list = a hand-maintained subset (artifacts where `governed: protected`). Becomes a derived view.
- Intent statements = per-artifact metadata you already require everywhere.

So three-to-four scattered, hand-maintained, already-drifting indexes collapse into one generated registry keyed by artifact. That's a real consolidation, not new ceremony.

**Discipline:** this is a **CMDB** (ITIL Configuration Management Database — configuration items + relationships) crossed with an **SBOM**. It's a `/frameworks` adoption in its own right (there's a `pending` slot pattern for that), and probably RFC-worthy given the blast radius.

**Proposed shape (three-layer + generator):**
- **Metadata convention** (extends the intent header): `kind` (rule|skill|hook|setup-script|lib|reference|registry|plan|framework-doc|entry-point|alias|config), `framework` (implements, if any), `governed` (protected?), `deps` (managed tools + artifacts), `lastReviewed` — plus existing `intent`.
- **Generator** scans the tree → emits `registries/artifact-registry.json` (derived).
- **`/artifact` skill** + `artifact-governance.md` rule + a **check step** (orphans, missing intent, protected-without-review, broken deps, stale cross-refs).

**Scope — track source artifacts only.** "Every file is an artifact" is true, but track the *permanent, hand-authored* ones. Exclude `deploy/` (generated), `.scratch/` + channel dirs (ephemeral), logs + `*.bak.*` (transient), `node_modules`/`.git` (vendored). `harvesting/` already has its own manifest (it's a different lifecycle — candidates), so leave it to that.

**Honest cautions (cost, not just upside):**
- **Backfill is a big one-time effort** — hundreds of existing files need metadata headers. Stage it: new/changed files must carry it; backfill opportunistically; track a coverage KPI rather than blocking on 100%.
- **Heterogeneous parsing** — md headers vs JSON `meta` vs `.sh`/`.ps1` comment headers. Doable (intent statements already follow a pattern), but the convention has to be uniform enough for one parser.

## The one piece of pushback on sequencing

We've now climbed three levels above "python is wrong on my Mac":
- **A** — python/uv resolution + PATH/shell-integration ownership (the live pain).
- **B** — tool-ops for every tool (resolution + verification, drop governanceModes).
- **C** — artifact registry framework (metadata convention + generator + derived views).

A is mostly independent and is the thing actually biting you today. My recommendation: **don't hold A hostage to B and C.** But there's one real dependency — A's deterministic resolution wants B's `resolution` entry, and B's consumer-deps want C's metadata convention. So the minimal critical path is:

1. **Define the artifact metadata convention** (smallest slice of C — just the header spec). Everything else consumes it.
2. **Ship A** (python/shell fix) + the **python tool-ops resolution entry** as B's first instance, consuming the convention.
3. **Build B out** (every tool) and **C** (generator + registry + derived views) as deliberate follow-ons — C as a proper framework adoption.

That way the live fix lands soon, and it lands *on* the new model instead of being redone later.

## Decisions to confirm

1. tool-ops 1:1 with tool-registry; baseline = resolution + verification; rich sections optional. **Rec: yes.**
2. Drop `governanceModes`; keep `enforcement` only on blocking rules. **Rec: yes.**
3. Deps declared at the consumer; tool-ops consumers derived. **Rec: yes.**
4. Artifact registry = **generated** from in-file metadata, scoped to source artifacts, adopted as a CMDB/SBOM framework. **Rec: yes.**
5. Sequencing: metadata convention → ship A + python tool-ops entry → build out B and C. **Rec: yes** (vs. fully designing B+C before touching A).

Where I most want your call: **#5** (do we ship the python fix on the new model now, or design B+C fully first?) and **#4's generated-not-authored constraint** — if you ever want the registry hand-editable, say so now, because it changes the entire architecture.

If these land, I'll capture C as a framework-adoption brief + the metadata-convention spec, and write the consolidated plan doc covering A→B→C. Want me to draft those?

1	# setup-python.ps1 -- Manages Python via uv (unified manager, Windows)
2	# Safe to re-run -- idempotent.
3	#
4	# uv is the single source of truth for Python on BOTH Windows and macOS. This
5	# script installs the target Python via uv and makes it the default, so bare
6	# `python`/`python3` resolve to the uv-managed interpreter (shims in uv's bin
7	# dir, %USERPROFILE%\.local\bin). Per-repo overrides use uv's normal mechanism
8	# (.python-version / `uv venv` / `uv run`) -- not a global rebind.
9	#
10	# Requires uv -- setup-uv.ps1 MUST run before this script.
11	#
12	# NOTE: Replaces the previous pymanager-based flow. A legacy pymanager, Microsoft
13	# Store (MSIX) Python, or winget Python.Python.3.x may still shadow the uv shim on
14	# PATH -- this script WARNS (does not auto-remove) so you can clean those up.
15	#
16	# See reference/tool-registry.md for install source details.
17	
18	# --- Shared library ---
19	. (Join-Path (Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path) "aitools-lib.ps1")
20	Initialize-Logging "setup-python"
21	
22	# --- OS guard ---
23	if ($PSVersionTable.PSVersion.Major -ge 6 -and -not $IsWindows) {
24	    LogError "This script is for Windows. On macOS/Linux, use the .sh version."
25	    exit 1
26	}
27	
28	# Target Python version (bump here for future upgrades; mirrors setup-python.sh)
29	$targetPyVersion = "3.14"
30	
31	# Refresh PATH to pick up tools installed by prior steps (e.g., setup-uv)
32	Refresh-Path
33	
34	# --- Require uv (the manager) ---
35	# Get-Command exempt: command-existence check with explicit error/exit
36	if (-not (Get-Command uv -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
37	    LogError "uv not found -- setup-uv.ps1 must run before setup-python.ps1"
38	    Write-Summary "ERROR" "python" "uv not installed (ordering: uv before python)"
39	    exit 1
40	}
41	
42	# --- Install/update the default Python via uv ---
43	# --default: install unversioned python/python3 executables into uv's bin dir.
44	# --preview-features python-install-default: silence the experimental warning and
45	#   pin the behavior (the --default flag is gated behind this preview feature).
46	Log "Installing/updating uv-managed Python $targetPyVersion as default..."
47	$installOutput = uv python install $targetPyVersion --default --upgrade --preview-features python-install-default 2>&1 | Out-String
48	$installOutput.Trim().Split("`n") | ForEach-Object {
49	    $l = $_.TrimEnd()
50	    if ($l.Trim()) { Log $l }
51	}
52	if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
53	    LogError "uv python install failed (exit code $LASTEXITCODE)"
54	    Write-Summary "ERROR" "python" "uv python install failed"
55	    exit 1
56	}
57	
58	Refresh-Path
59	
60	# --- Verify python resolves to the uv-managed interpreter ---
61	# Get-Command exempt: command-existence check with if/else fallback
62	$pythonCmd = Get-Command python -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
63	if ($pythonCmd) {
64	    $pyVersion = python --version 2>&1
65	    $src = $pythonCmd.Source
66	    if ($src -match '\\uv\\' -or $src -match '\.local\\bin') {
67	        LogOk "$pyVersion (uv-managed at $src)"
68	        Write-Summary "OK" "python" "$pyVersion (uv)"
69	    } else {
70	        LogWarn "python resolves to $src ($pyVersion), not the uv shim"
71	        LogWarn "A legacy pymanager / Microsoft Store / winget Python may be shadowing uv on PATH"
72	        LogWarn "Ensure uv's bin dir (%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin) precedes those in PATH"
73	        Write-Summary "WARN" "python" "$pyVersion (uv shim shadowed -- check PATH)"
74	        Write-Summary "ACTION" "" "Put %USERPROFILE%\.local\bin first in PATH -- python default"
75	    }
76	} else {
77	    LogError "'python' not found after uv install -- is uv's bin dir (%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin) on PATH?"
78	    Write-Summary "ERROR" "python" "python not on PATH after uv install"
79	    Write-Summary "ACTION" "" "Add %USERPROFILE%\.local\bin to PATH -- uv python shims"
80	}
81	
82	# --- pip note ---
83	# uv-managed CPython bundles pip; prefer `uv pip` for project work.
84	# Get-Command exempt: command-existence check with if/else fallback
85	if (Get-Command pip -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
86	    $pipVersion = pip --version 2>$null
87	    if ($pipVersion) { LogOk "pip available: $pipVersion" }
88	} else {
89	    Log "pip not on PATH as a standalone command -- use 'uv pip' or 'python -m pip'"
90	}
91	
92	# --- Exit ---
93	if ($errors -gt 0) {
94	    Log "FAILED with $errors error(s). See log: $logFile" "error"
95	    exit 1
96	} elseif ($warnings -gt 0) {
97	    Log "COMPLETED with $warnings warning(s)" "warn"
98	    exit 0
99	} else {
100	    Log "COMPLETED successfully" "ok"
101	    exit 0

**Step B — tool-ops for every tool**

**Step C — Artifact registry (CMDB + SBOM framework adoption)**
Adopt via `/frameworks` (discipline: ITIL CMDB + SBOM; concepts: configuration items, dependency graph, single-source-via-generation). Three-layer: `artifact-governance.md` rule + **generated** `registries/artifact-registry.json` + `/artifact` skill + generator + check step. This file is the durable record of decisions reached in\nthat conversation.\n\n---\n\n## Status (2026-06-17)\n\n**Shipped this session:**\n- `~/.zprofile` — removed the dead Intel-brew line (`eval \"$(/usr/local/bin/brew shellenv)\"`) that errored on every shell init (no Intel Homebrew on Apple Silicon).\n- `agent` symlink — removed stale `~/.grok/bin/agent` (→ old grok 0.2.3), repointed `~/.local/bin/agent` → `cursor-agent` (Cursor CLI). **Live only; not durable** until Workstream A owns PATH order (`~/.grok/bin` still precedes `~/.local/bin`).\n- `scripts/setup-python.{sh,ps1}` — shadow detection now names the *actual* shadowing dir (parent of the resolved binary) instead of the hardcoded `/usr/bin`. `setup-python.sh` passed `bash -n`; `.ps1` not parse-checked (no pwsh on this Mac — see backlog).\n- `registries/tool-registry.json` `python` entry — corrected `postInstallConfig` (the `/usr/bin` mis-diagnosis → the real Homebrew-bin shadow) and populated `knownPaths` with the uv shim paths.\n\n**Not yet done:** Workstreams A, B, C below; ROADMAP index row; `framework-registry.json` pending entry for C.\n\n---\n\n## Problem\n\n1. **python3 shadow.** Interactively, `python3` resolves to the uv shim (`~/.local/bin/python3`, 3.14.6) — correct. In the harness's *non-interactive* contexts (SessionStart/SessionEnd hooks, `aitools install`, Claude Code's Bash tool, cron/MDM) it resolves to Homebrew's `python@3.x` at `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3`. Cause: the `~/.local/bin` prepend lives only in `.zshrc` (interactive), and `brew shellenv` (`.zprofile`, login) plus re-evals push `/opt/homebrew/bin` ahead. **The harness owns zero PATH ordering today.**\n2. **Mis-diagnosed remediation.** The install warning and the registry's `postInstallConfig` both blamed `/usr/bin`; the real shadow is `/opt/homebrew/bin`, and `~/.local/bin` is already ahead of `/usr/bin`. (Fixed in scripts + registry this session.)\n3. **No \"harness uses what it manages\" model.** `tool-ops.json` governs only `claude-code` (deny rules + hooks). There is no place that says how the harness should *resolve and invoke* a managed tool, and nothing verifies it.\n4. **`agent` resolved to grok**, not Cursor (stale user symlink). The harness's own `setup-user-cursor.sh` \"Cursor CLI\" check matched grok 0.2.3.\n\n---\n\n## Confirmed decisions\n\n1. **tool-ops is 1:1 with tool-registry.** Every managed tool gets a tool-ops entry — *every managed tool is a governed tool*. Baseline entry = `resolution` + `verification`. Richer sections (`denyRules`, `hooks`, `contextInjection`, `kpis`) are optional, added only when a tool earns them.\n2. **Drop the blanket `governanceModes` field.** Resolution/audit/verification are inherent to being managed (always-on, advisory by default). Keep a single `enforcement: \"audit\" | \"active\"` flag **only on rules that can block a session** (deny rules), so observe-to-enforce graduation survives where blocking actually happens (ref incident #34730).\n3. **Dependencies declared at the consumer.** Each artifact declares the managed tools it uses in its *own* metadata (`usesManagedTools`). tool-ops does **not** store a `harnessConsumers` list — the \"who consumes X\" view is derived by scanning artifact metadata.\n4. **Artifact registry = generated, never hand-authored.** Per-artifact metadata lives *in each file*; `registries/artifact-registry.json` is produced by a scan (treated like `deploy/` — regenerated, never edited). Scope = source artifacts only. Adopted as a **CMDB + SBOM** framework via `/frameworks`.\n5. **Two registries, clean split.** tool-registry = supply chain (identity / install / version / health / supported-status). tool-ops = operations (resolution / verification / governance). Install-path facts live in tool-registry `knownPaths`; tool-ops `resolution` references them.\n6. **PATH precedence (macOS):** `~/.local/bin` → `/opt/homebrew/bin` → `~/.grok/bin` / other installer bins. This makes the uv `python3` and `cursor-agent` win deterministically.\n7. **aitools owns a marked block** (`# >>> aitools managed >>>` … `# <<< aitools managed <<<`) in the **login** profile (`.zprofile` / `.bash_profile`); `brew shellenv` runs *inside* that block, then `~/.local/bin` is prepended. The interactive `*.rc` keeps only the `source aliases.{sh,ps1}` line.\n8. **`agent` = Cursor** (harness-managed symlink + corrected detection); **grok stays unmanaged** (invoked as `grok`).\n9. **Install order (flat, no tiers):** brew (+ git + bash) → node → uv → python → claude → agent → everything else → deploy configs.\n10. **Lifecycle gate:** marking a tool `supported` on a platform requires a tool-ops `resolution` entry and a **passing resolution verification** — \"supported\" means installed, current, *and resolving to the managed copy in the harness's non-interactive context.*\n\n---\n\n## Step 0 — Artifact metadata convention (smallest slice of C; unblocks #3)\n\nDefine a uniform per-artifact metadata header, extending the existing intent block. Fields:\n\n| Field | Meaning |\n|-------|---------|\n| `intent` | purpose / scope / audience (already required on governed files) |\n| `kind` | rule \\| skill \\| hook \\| setup-script \\| lib \\| entry-point \\| reference \\| registry \\| plan \\| framework-doc \\| check-script \\| generator \\| alias \\| config |\n| `framework` | which framework this artifact implements (null if none) |\n| `governed` | protected? (true/false) — derives the sources-of-truth list |\n| `usesManagedTools` | array of managed-tool slugs invoked at runtime |\n| `deps` | other artifacts relied on (optional) |\n| `lastReviewed` | YYYY-MM-DD |\n\nWhere metadata lives by file type: `.md` / `.sh` / `.ps1` → header comment block; `.json` → `meta` object; files that cannot carry a header → sidecar or a registry override map. This convention is the single source the artifact-registry generator (C) reads.\n\n---\n\n## Workstream A — Durable resolution + shell-integration / PATH ownership (ship first)\n\nThe live fix. Mostly independent; consumes the python tool-ops entry from B.\n\n- **A1.** New `scripts/setup-user-shell.{sh,ps1}` — dedicated owner of the managed shell block (extracted from `aitools-install` Step 7, which currently only appends `source aliases.sh` and owns no PATH).\n- **A2.** Managed block in the **login** profile: `brew shellenv` (guarded — `/opt/homebrew` Apple Silicon, `/usr/local` Intel) → prepend `~/.local/bin` → fold in `$GOPATH/bin` and `~/.cargo/bin` → ensure precedence over `~/.grok/bin` / antigravity. Idempotent: replace content between `# >>> aitools managed >>>` / `# <<< aitools managed <<<`.\n- **A3.** Replace `aitools-install.{sh,ps1}` Step 7 to call `setup-user-shell`; keep the `source aliases.{sh,ps1}` line in the interactive `*.rc`.\n- **A4.** Embed `setup-user-shell` in `build-deploy.sh` (closes the gap that the MDM/deploy path sets up no shell integration today).\n- **A5.** Deterministic resolver in `aitools-lib.{sh,ps1}` (e.g. `harness_python` / `Resolve-ManagedTool`) returning the managed shim (or `uv run`); repoint harness python callers (dashboard `find_python`, hook shims, relay sync) off bare PATH lookup.\n- **A6.** `setup-user-cursor.{sh,ps1}` — manage the `agent → cursor-agent` symlink and fix detection to verify the resolved `agent` is actually Cursor (not grok).\n- **A7.** Reorder installer steps to decision #9.\n- **A8.** New `reference/ait-shellintegration.md` (all platforms) — the managed block, marker convention, canonical PATH order, what aitools owns vs preserves. (Protected: new intent statement.)\n\nCross-platform: every `.sh` needs a `.ps1`; PS1 manages the block in the login `$PROFILE` analog with an explicit END marker (today's Windows block has none).\n\n---\n\n## Workstream B — tool-ops for every managed tool\n\n- **B1.** Schema change in `tool-ops.json`: drop per-tool `governanceModes`; add baseline `resolution` (`canonicalCommands`, `manager?`, `managedPath` per platform, `pathPrecedence`, `invocationContract`) + `verifications`; `enforcement` flag only on blocking rules.\n- **B2.** `python` reference entry (resolution + verification), e.g. verification `python3 -c 'import sys; print(sys.executable)'` must contain `/.local/share/uv/python/`.\n- **B3.** Replicate to the harness-invoked set first (node + npx/npm, bash, perl, uv, claude-code [extend], agent/cursor), then resolution-baseline entries for the rest.\n- **B4.** Amend (protected, present diffs): `framework-tool-ops.md` (lean-pull reframe — every tool gets an entry; lean-pull now governs *which optional sections*); `.claude/rules/tool-ops.md`; `.claude/rules/tool-lifecycle.md` (add the decision-#10 gate); `tool-ops` SKILL.md (new schema).\n- **B5.** Wire `shared/hooks/tool-ops-session-audit.sh` to run resolution verifications and assert 1:1 coverage (every registry tool has an ops entry).\n\n---\n\n## Workstream C — Artifact registry (CMDB + SBOM framework adoption)\n\n- **C1.** Adopt via `/frameworks` (pending → adopted). Discipline: ITIL **CMDB** (configuration items + relationships) + **SBOM**. Concepts: configuration items, dependency graph, single-source-via-generation. Reference doc: `reference/framework-artifact-registry.md`.\n- **C2.** Three-layer: rule `.claude/rules/artifact-governance.md` + **generated** `registries/artifact-registry.json` + `/artifact` skill + generator (`scripts/generate-artifact-registry.*`) + a check step.\n- **C3.** Generator scans source artifacts, reads the Step-0 metadata, emits the registry. **Scope — exclude**: `deploy/` (generated), `.scratch/` + channel session dirs (ephemeral), `harvesting/` (its own manifest), logs, `*.bak.*`, `.git`, `node_modules`.\n- **C4.** Derive existing scattered indexes from it: the sources-of-truth protected set; `framework-registry` framework→artifacts; tool-ops consumers.\n- **C5.** Backfill metadata staged (new/changed files must carry it; opportunistic backfill; coverage KPI). Check step flags: missing intent/metadata, orphans, broken deps, stale cross-references (e.g. the `framework-registry.json` → `reference/tool-ops.json` drift below).\n\n---\n\n## Sequencing\n\nStep 0 (metadata convention) → **A** (ship now) + **B2** (python tool-ops entry, which A5 consumes) → **B** (rest) → **C** (framework adoption).\n\n---\n\n## Open threads / backlog\n\n| # | Item | Lands in |\n|---|------|----------|\n| 1 | python non-interactive shadow (the core durable fix) | A |\n| 2 | `agent` durability (PATH ownership) | A |\n| 3 | `setup-user-cursor` detection matched grok 0.2.3, not Cursor | A6 |\n| 4 | `setup-go` GOPATH/bin \"session only\" warning | A2 |\n| 5 | **pwsh gap** — in registry as macOS-supported (7.5.4) and required by `build-deploy.sh` for PS1 validation, but **no install step** in the 22; macOS PS1 validation silently skips, and `.ps1` edits can't be parse-checked locally | new tool-lifecycle item |\n| 6 | **`framework-registry.json` stale** — lists `reference/tool-ops.json`; should be `registries/tool-ops.json` (post-v0.69.0 consolidation).
